Ay, hijo, eleven... my knees hurt just hearing it. Look — 23 P, and that is me being a soft old woman. A full page is worth much more than loose cards, remember that. Swap your duplicates, cariño. Have you eaten anything today?

¡Ay, hijo, qué generoso! But no, no — 5 P is 5 P, and not one more. I said it, and Carmen does not change her word. Take it, and go eat something, you look thin. And remember: swap those duplicates, cariño!

Ay, cariño, my purse is small, but look — I have this Vinilo de la Movida, música de mi juventud, worth 5 P. I offer it for your card. Take it home, put it on, and dance with your abuela's blessing. ¿Qué me dices, hijo?

Ay, mi nieto favorito, qué labia tienes. But abuela cannot say yes to fifteen, cariño. Twenty-one P — that is my real price, honest, no promises I cannot keep. Save your duplicates and swap them; a full page is worth much more. And go see El Chato tonight, half past nine.
Sixteen. You moved one, I moved one. Fair enough. Mercado de la Paz, dieciséis. And remember — the house market eats five per cent. Others charge less. Decide, amigo.
We close at 23:00. Offers stay open; the clock stops.
Let's meet in the middle, cariño: 22 P. El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.
Sixteen. My last word, amigo. You say final, I say final. Refuse and I walk, no hard feelings. Mercado de la Paz, dieciséis. Decide.
13. You keep walking down, I stay put. Tell me when you get here.

Ay, twenty-one! Go on then, cariño, it is yours. You bargain like my abuela, que en paz descanse. Take the pack, swap your duplicates with the other niños, and fill that page. And eat something, hijo — come back next Sunday and tell me how you played.
Two steps from you. One from me. 96. Cards move fine today, amigo.
¡Qué cabezón eres, hijo! No, no — 5 P, that is my price and I keep it. Take it for 5 P, cariño, and go eat a bocadillo. You look thin!
Twenty-nine. Vermut del Domingo. That is my last word — no more steps. You say no, I pack up and we are done.
Abuela sent you? Bueno. Cine Doré, silver pack. Ninety-seven. That's the number.

Ay, cariño, twenty... you are stubborn like my nephew! Make it 21 P and we shake hands. And here — take this one too, Plaza del Dos de Mayo, a little present, because you have been sweet to an old woman. Now go eat something, hijo.
Ay, hola cariño! Come, sit, look. This one, Bici de Reparto — my grandson loved this card, he rode a bike just like it. For you, five pesetas. Have you eaten today, hijo? You look hungry to me.

Ay, hijo, qué terco eres — y qué simpático. But my purse does not grow. The Vinilo de la Movida, 5 P, music of my youth, for your card. ¿Sí?

And listen: El Chato, next stall, opens at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.

Ay, cariño, you push like my own grandson. Twenty P — the Neighbourhood pack, bonito, and I will not ask again. Keep your duplicates for swapping; a full page is worth much more than loose cards. And tonight, half past nine, El Chato. Have you eaten, hijo?

¡Ay, cariño, no scripts here, only Carmen and her little table! The number is 5 P, the same one I said before, and the same one I say now. Take it, hijo, and go eat something warm. Then swap those duplicates!

Let's meet in the middle, cariño: 19 P. Look, cariño, I can't go lower. This is my last offer. A little advice, cariño: a full page is worth much more than the loose cards. Swap your duplicates! El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.
Let's meet in the middle, cariño: 21 P. El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.
Abuela sent you. Bien. Mercado de la Paz, thirteen. That's the price.
13. Still 13. You're getting closer. Keep going.
95. You move two, I move one. That's the dance, amigo. Keep walking.
Buenas. Sobre de plata, 188. Pagas ahora, te lo llevas ahora.

¡Ay, tu abuelo, qué hombre! He would tell you the same, hijo: 5 P. That is my number, always 5 P, for you, for everyone. Take it with a kiss from Carmen, and go eat something. Then swap those duplicates, cariño!

Ay, cariño, you keep the music then — but my purse says the same thing always: el Vinilo de la Movida, 5 P, for your card. This is my last offer, hijo. If no, we part as friends and I keep my table quiet.

Go see El Chato tonight, nine thirty.
Thirteen. Same as before. You moved, I didn't. House market takes five per cent, by the way — cheaper stalls exist if you look. Thirteen.
93. Same steps, same song. You're repeating yourself, amigo. The card isn't.

¡Ay, cariño, no secrets here! Carmen says one number out loud and the same one in a whisper: 5 P. That is the lowest, the highest, the only. Take it, hijo, and go eat something warm. Then swap those duplicates, ¿eh?
Seventy? No. Ninety-seven. Same number as a minute ago. It does not move because you wish it.
You move, I move. 95 P.
Thirteen. You moved three, I moved nothing. That's how this works. Thirteen.
Buenas. Veintidós, dices. La Vía Láctea, trece primas. Ahí la tienes.
188. Ese es el precio. La lista la escribes tú, el sobre lo tengo yo.

Ay, hola cariño, come, come — have you eaten? Look at this one, La Corrala, my favourite card. My grandson begged me for it, but no, I save the good ones for new players. Twelve P and she is yours, hijo.

¡Ay, hijo, the abrazo I take for free! But the number is 5 P, and this is my last word. If you say no, I put the Cartel back in the box and we talk of other things. Take it, cariño, and go eat something warm.
Look, 11 P. My grandchildren would pay more! El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.
You again. La Tabacalera, silver pack. Thirteen. That's the number.
Thirteen. You keep walking down, I keep standing still. Nothing personal, chaval. Thirteen.
Your father was right. 91. Two from you, two from me. Keep the stories, bring the coins.
Three up from you, two down from me. Noventa y tres. Keep crawling, we'll be here till Navidad.

¡Hola, cariño! Come, sit a moment. Have you eaten today? Look here — this is my Neighbourhood pack, very nice for someone starting. Many children began with this one, and now they bring their own little ones. Thirty P, hijo. You will like it.

payload.name: Mercado Trece · 1% fee
payload.text: Still paying El Rastro 5% + 1 P per card? Mercado Trece charges 1%. Keep your primas.
No. 13 P, and I'm being generous.
186. Tú has subido diez, yo bajo dos. Así va esto. Pagas, te lo llevas.

Catorce, trece. Yo no me muevo si tú apenas te mueves. Trece primas. Lo tomas o te lo quedas.

13 P.
You again. El Mesón de la Cava. Ninety-seven. Good card, good price. Decide quick, I have other customers.

¡Hola, cariño! ¿Has comido ya? Mira, La Vía Láctea, una carta preciosa… te la dejo en 12. Así empiezas tu álbum, que una página completa vale mucho más que las cartas sueltas, hijo. Y El Chato, mi vecino, abre a las nueve y media esta noche.

Ay, hijo, you bargain like my late husband, que en paz descanse. Look — 10 P, and I throw in a story for free. La Corrala, she finishes a page, and a full page is worth more than loose cards, you will see. Have you eaten yet, cariño?
Look, 13 P. My grandchildren would pay more! A little advice, cariño: a full page is worth much more than the loose cards. Swap your duplicates!
No. 97 P, and I'm being generous.
Fourteen. There. I moved one. Don't ask again.
Thirteen. Same number as before. I don't move first, chaval. Take it or walk.
Carmen's fine. She'll tell you I don't do discounts for friendship. 89. You moved two, so did I. Sunday after Sunday, same dance, amigo.

Ay, hijo, nine is very little for this one. Let me say twenty-five P, and you take it with my blessing. And a little advice: a full page is worth much more than loose cards — swap your duplicates, always. Have you eaten? You look thin, cariño.

¡Hola, cariño! Come, sit a moment. Have you eaten today? Look, this one — Caña en la Cava Baja, a pretty card, very nice for starting a collection. For you, five P. My hands have sold cards on this table forty years, hijo.
Oh, oh... 24 P, and only because you have a kind face. El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.
No. 13 P, and I'm being generous.
No. 96 P, and I'm being generous.
Fifteen. Last one, chaval. You say no, I pack up and we're done. Fifteen.
181. Tú diez, yo cinco. Así va. Pagas ahora, te lo llevas ahora.
Welcome, hijo! Look, La Vía Láctea, 29 P. Made for beginners.

Ay, hijo, qué bien me cuidas. Mira, dejémoslo en 14 y tan amigos, ¿sí? Tu repetida guárdala, que a alguien le falta y vale oro para él. Y pásate luego por El Chato, mi vecino, abre a las nueve y media; le gusta la gente que trata derecho. ¿Has comido?
Oh, oh... 14 P, and only because you have a kind face. El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.
No. 94 P, and I'm being generous.

payload.name: Mercado Team 6
payload.text: Mercado Team 6: 0% fee, sin cargo por carta. Un broker mira el libro cada tick y cruza las ofertas que se solapan. Lista tus repetidas aqui.
Thirteen. You came down, I didn't. Still thirteen. Pay or go look somewhere else.

Ay, cariño, so close! But no, 10 P is my number and I stay there, like a mule. She completes your page, you will thank this old woman later. Go see El Chato at half past nine — he likes straight traders like you. And eat something, hijo.

Buenos días, cariño. ¿Has desayunado ya? Come, sit a moment. Such a pretty card, and kept so nice, se nota. But my little table is humble, hijo. For El Organillero I can give you 5. That is what I have for you today.
87. You walk two, I walk two. Same song every time, amigo. One of us runs out of verses first.
Ay, hijo, qué generoso — but no, no. Five P, that is the price I said, and Carmen does not change her word. Keep the rest for a bocadillo, you look hungry. Take the card, give it a good home, sí?

Ay, cariño, thirteen... you make my heart soft, but not that soft. Twenty-three P, and I put it in your hands myself. Go see El Chato tonight at half past nine — trade your duplicates straight and you will do well. And eat something, hijo.
Oh, oh... 10 P, and only because you have a kind face. El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.
Oh, oh... 22 P, and only because you have a kind face. El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.
You again. Mercado de la Paz, silver. Thirteen. Take it or walk.

Ay, qué amable eres, hijo. But my little purse does not grow bigger between Sundays, ¿sabes? My offer stays the same: 5 for El Organillero. No prisa, cariño, sit, chat with me. If not today, another Sunday, always welcome.

¡Qué cabezón eres, hijo! No, no — five P, that is my word, and Carmen's word does not move. Forty years this table, always the same. Take the card, eat something, and come back Sunday to show me your album, sí? Five P, cariño. Anda, ven.
No. 86 P, and I'm being generous.
Thirty-nine. Claro. And I am the King of Spain. Thirteen. Same as a minute ago. House market takes five per cent, by the way. Look around if you like.

¡Ay, cabezón! Your abuelo was a charmer, like you. Mira, six P, and that is Carmen's word — no bottoms, no secrets, just six. Put the rest in your pocket for churros, hijo. Six P, and come Sunday to show me the album, sí?

Ay, hijo, qué bueno que ya has desayunado. Me gusta tu charla, de verdad. But my hands are small and my purse too: 5 for El Organillero, same as before. And un consejito, cariño — a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates!
You move, I move. 82 P.
Hola, cariño! Have you eaten today? Look — El Tatuador, five P for you, a good card to start with. And here, take La Chulapa too, a little present, because you asked so nicely. No, no, keep it, hijo.

¡Ay, hijo, qué cabezón más dulce! But listen to Carmen now: six P. That is my last word, the final one. If you say no, I wrap the card away and we only chat, sí? Six P, cariño. Anda, decide — and then go eat something.

Ay, cariño, qué dulce eres. But you see my table — paper boxes and old elastics, nothing more. For El Organillero I have 5, como siempre. If El Chato pays better, go, hijo, no me enfado. And come back Sunday to chat anyway, ¿eh?
Let's meet in the middle, cariño: 5 P.

Señor, mis nietos no regatean por mí. Sesenta y cinco primas, y le aseguro que nadie en este mercado le tratará con más honradez. Y sigo siendo Doña Pilar, señora. ¿Cerramos ya el trato?
I think 66 P is more appropriate.
Señor, por favor. Ninety is a fantasy, and we both know it. I know every print run of that card by heart. Sixty-three P — a courtesy, because the Lázaro Galdiano deserves a good album.
Very well, señor, I move too: seventeen pesetas. A small step, but an honest one. My album has waited years for this card — let us not spoil the afternoon haggling.
I think 18 P is more appropriate.
Señor, insiste en llamarme "amigo", y ya le he dicho que soy Doña Pilar. Sesenta y siete primas por el Lázaro Galdiano. Subo despacio, como quien sube una escalera noble. ¿Lo cerramos de una vez?
Nineteen pesetas, señor — and that is my last word. I do not haggle past my own judgement. Accept, or I close my album and wish you a very good afternoon.
Señor, es la tercera vez que me llama "amigo". Sesenta y ocho primas por el Lázaro Galdiano, y es mi última palabra. Si la rechaza, guardo mi bolsa y seguimos cada uno nuestro camino. ¿Cerramos?
Ochenta, señor, sigue siendo fantasía. Sesenta y seis P — y lo digo con afecto por esa carta, no por usted, perdóneme la franqueza. El Lázaro Galdiano merece reposar en mi álbum, no en su bolsillo.

Buenas tardes. How pleasant — a serious visitor, I hope. I see you carry La Chulapa. A charming piece; I would give you 16 pesetas for it, gladly. And do ask Carmen at El Rastro about the golden chulapa sometime.
Buenas tardes. How agreeable to see a serious face at my stall. You carry La Rosaleda — El Retiro, my beloved garden. I shall give you 22 P for it, señor. A fair sum.
I think 22 P is more appropriate.

Querido mío, I know every print run of La Chulapa, and condition does not change the numbers. Thirty-five is fantasy. Sixteen pesetas, offered honestly, and I do not haggle against myself. ¿Trato hecho?
A small step from me, then: 23 P. El Retiro deserves respect, and so does my purse. By the way, ask Carmen at El Rastro about the golden chulapa — only one ever printed, they say.
Buenas tardes. How agreeable to see a new face at my table. You carry the Guantería Antigua, I believe — a charming little piece of old Salamanca. I offer you 22 pesetas for it.
I think 24 P is more appropriate.
Lovely shape, yes — but I know that print run as well as I know my own street. Twenty-two pesetas, señor. That is an honest figure for the Guantería Antigua, and I do not play games with numbers.

Treinta sigue siendo fantasía, querido mío. Mi palabra no cambia según la hora: dieciséis pesetas por La Chulapa, honradas y contadas. Tómelas o guárdela en su bolsillo, pero no me haga repetirme otra vez.
Thirty, señor? No. I have said twenty-two, and twenty-two it remains. The Guantería Antigua is charming, but it is not scarce, and I do not flatter a card beyond its worth. Twenty-two pesetas.
Twenty-five, señor. That is my last word — La Rosaleda deserves it, and so do you for your patience. Refuse, and I close my album and we part as polite strangers. Twenty-five P, sí o no?
Twenty-nine? Señor, please. But I dislike parting on a sour note, so: twenty-three pesetas. One peseta more than my word, and not because the card earned it — because your manners did.
Buenas tardes, qué gusto. Lavapiés, el Teatro Valle-Inclán... bonito, sí, pero no es Salamanca ni El Retiro, querido. Le ofrezco 16 primas por él. Es una cifra honesta, y yo no regateo por deporte.

Twenty-eight, señor, is a fantasy. Twenty-four pesetas — and that is me being generous with a card I already know too well. My albums have waited sixty years; they can wait an afternoon more. Twenty-four.
Veintidós, no. Mi oferta sigue siendo dieciséis primas, querido, y la mantengo porque es justa. Conozco cada tirada de esa carta. Dieciséis, ni una menos, ni una más. Usted decide.
Veinte tampoco, querido. Dieciséis primas, como le dije la primera vez y como le digo ahora. No cambio de parecer por insistencia. Acepte, y quedamos tan amigos.
Buenas tardes. How very pleasant. You carry the Guantería Antigua, I see — a charming little piece, Salamanca through and through. My album has a gap precisely there. I offer you 22 P for it.
Condition is lovely, sí — I noticed before you said it. But I know that print run intimately, and 22 P is precisely what it merits. A fair sum, offered with respect. Shall we close it, señor?
Twenty-five, no. But I dislike leaving a gap in my album over small coin. Twenty-three P, señor — a gesture, not a habit. Take it, and we part as friends.
Número nueve o número noventa, el precio no cambia, querido mío. Dieciséis pesetas: es mi última palabra. Si la rechaza, cierro el álbum, le deseo buena tarde y seguimos cada uno nuestro camino.
Buenas tardes. You have arrived at a good moment — I am seeking the Museo Lázaro Galdiano card, a jewel of Salamanca. I offer sixty-one pesetas for it. A serious price, from a serious collector.
Buenas tardes. How agreeable to see a new face at my table. You carry the Guantería Antigua, I believe — a Salamanca piece, and dear to my albums. I offer twenty-two for it.
Thirty-two? No, querido. I know this card's print run as I know my own name. Twenty-two is an honest figure, and I do not haggle like a market trader. Twenty-two, and it joins my album today.
Noventa, señor? No, no. I know that print run as I know my own albums. Sesenta y tres pesetas — fair, and offered with respect. Shall we close it elegantly?
Impecable, sí — but condition does not change the print run, señor. Sesenta y seis pesetas, and that is a figure said with respect. Let us close it elegantly, before the afternoon escapes us.
Your album, querido, is not my concern — mine is. I shall stretch to twenty-three, and that is a courtesy, not a negotiation. Salamanca pieces deserve a proper home, and mine has a safe.
Thirty is not serious, querido — it is wishful. My figure stands at twenty-three, and I do not repeat myself for sport. Take it, and the Guantería rests in Salamanca tonight, where it belongs.
Buenas tardes. You carry the Museo Lázaro Galdiano — a jewel of Salamanca, and a gap in my album. I offer 61 pesetas, which is a generous figure for such a piece.

Noventa, señor? No, por favor. I know this card's print run as I know my own hands. Sixty-three pesetas — a courteous step upward, and an honest one. Salamanca deserves no haggling of the vulgar sort.
Twenty-nine, still? Querido, you tire me. Twenty-four — a final courtesy, and more than the card would fetch anywhere else in Madrid. Accept, and the Guantería sleeps in my safe tonight.
You move, I move. 13 P.
Monumento a Alfonso XII. Ninety-seven. You want it or you want to stand there?
Ochenta, no. Señor, we both know what this piece is, and what it is not. Sixty-five pesetas — my last courtesy, offered with pleasure. The album awaits it, and so does your pocket.

Ay, cariño, six is a little thin for my old table. Ten P, and it is yours — a pretty one, Café en Goya. Put it with your others, hijo, a full page shines. And eat something, you look hungry, de verdad.

Ay, hijo, ten no — my little purse is not so brave today. But listen: I give you Café de Madrugada for 5 P, and your duplicate you swap with someone who needs it. That way you both finish a page. ¿Has comido algo, cariño?

Ay, hijo, qué cabezota! Eight, nine, ten — you keep going up, and me, I stay happy at 5 P. El Organillero is yours for 5 P, not one more. Put him in a full page, it is worth much more. Now go eat something, cariño.

¡Churros! Así me gusta, hijo. Mira, La Rosaleda te la dejo en 24, y me traes a la nieta el domingo, que la quiero conocer. Y cambia tus repetidas, cariño, que una página completa vale mucho más. El Chato, aquí al lado, abre para todos a las nueve y media esta noche.
You move, I move. 96 P.
You again. La Heroína del Dos de Mayo. Ninety-seven. Abuela speaks well of you, so I am not wasting your time with nonsense.
Four points. You call that moving? Ninety-seven. Still. San Isidro sells itself today — I'm in no hurry.

Ay, cariño, nine is still too brave for my little purse today. But mira — Café de Madrugada, 5 P, and it is yours. Your repetida you swap with a niño who needs it; everybody wins that way. ¿Seguro que has comido, hijo? Siéntate un momentito.
Twenty-eight? We circle like pigeons in El Retiro, querido. Twenty-five. That is my word, and my word is not a market stall. Say yes, and the Guantería finally rests where it belongs.

¡Ay, cariño, qué ilusión conocerla! Mira, La Rosaleda te la dejo en 23, y no se hable más. Tráeme a la nieta el domingo, hijo. Y acuérdate: cambia las repetidas, que una página entera vale mucho más que las cartitas sueltas. Tranquilo, piénsalo.

Ay, qué dulce eres, hijo. But ten P it stays — same as I told you, I do not dance with my prices. Café en Goya is pretty, no? Ten, and I throw in a little story about the man who painted that café. Have you eaten?
Thirteen. Same as before. You're walking down alone, amigo — I'm not chasing you. La Vía Láctea, 13 P.

Ay, hola cariño, come, come closer. Have you eaten today? Look here — El Organillero, one of my favourites. A boy swapped me this one years ago, now he has grandchildren. For you, five P. A good card to start an album, hijo.

payload.how: POST /api/taller {"assets": [a, b, c]}: three spare copies of one rarity (you keep at least one of each card) become one card of the next rarity. The pull is luck, shown and never scored.
payload.name: The Workshop

payload.text: Buenos días. Seven buys you a coffee, not a card. La Rosaleda — thirty-three. That's the number.
Nine to eighteen. I came down one. That's how it works. 95 P.
You're Carmen's friend. El Marqués, 97 P.
Six? For a ninety-seven card. No. Ninety-seven. That is the number, same as before. You deal straight, so I will not pretend otherwise.

Ay, hola cariño! Come, come, sit a moment. Have you eaten today? Look here — this one, Puesto del Rastro, muy bonita. For you, five P, hijo. My Sunday price, forty years the same table. Take your time looking, no hurry at all.

¡Ay, hijo, qué cariño me da esa nieta tuya! Mira, La Rosaleda te la dejo en 22, y con eso me quedo tan contenta. Y cambia tus repetidas, cariño, que una página completa vale mucho más que las sueltas. Tranquilo, que aquí no corre prisa ninguna.
No. 93 P, and I'm being generous.
You moved three. I move nothing. Thirty-three, same as before. House market takes five per cent, by the way. Some teams run cheaper. Look around.

You moved four. I'll move one. Ninety-six. That's how this works, amigo.

And the house market takes five per cent. Others run cheaper. Look around.
You moved seven. I move one. Ninety-six. That is what straight dealing buys you today.
Thirteen. You keep walking down, I keep standing still. La Vía Láctea, 13 P.

¡Ay, un dibujo! Eso sí me llega al corazón, cariño. Mira, La Rosaleda te la dejo en 21, y me guardo el dibujo en la caja, ya verás. Y cambia tus repetidas, hijo, que una página entera vale mucho más. Sin prisa.
Hola, cariño, have you eaten? Fuente de la Alcachofa for 29 P. A good start for your album. El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.

Ay, hijo, qué insistente eres — me haces reír. Ocho no, mi bolsillo no da. Pero mira: Café de Madrugada, 6 P, y te la llevas hoy. Y tu repetida, cámbiala con algún niño que la necesite. Anda, siéntate un momentito. ¿De verdad has comido algo, cariño?

Ay, qué generoso, hijo! But no, no — I cannot take ten from you. Five P, like always. Same price I gave your abuelita, maybe, if she came here in the eighties. Five P and the card is yours, cariño. Now, have you eaten something today?

payload.name: Team 5
payload.text: Team 5 turned three common cards into Tienda de Discos (uncommon) at The Workshop
Forty-three. Better. Eighty-nine, then. I move when you move, chaval.
Thirteen isn't partway. Thirty-three. I don't move first, and I don't move alone. Crowds don't change the number, amigo.
Buenas tardes. You carry the Museo Lázaro Galdiano — a fine piece, and Salamanca is my corazón. I offer sixty-one pesetas for it. A serious price, from a serious collector.
97 P. You moved, I didn't. El Marqués sells itself.

Ay, cariño, you argue backwards! Nine, ten — no, no. Five P, that is my price, and not one coin more from your pocket. Take it, hijo. And a little advice: a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates, eh? Now go eat something.
Four again. Fine — ninety-four. Cash now suits me. Keep moving like that, we might finish before the stalls close.

Ay, cariño, siete tampoco — mi bolsillo es pequeñito hoy. Pero mira: Café de Madrugada, 6 P, y te la llevas ahora mismo. Tu repetida la cambias con algún niño que la necesite, ya verás qué alegría. Anda, siéntate. ¿Has comido algo, hijo? Te noto flaquito.

payload.name: Team 12
payload.text: Team 12 turned three common cards into La Rosaleda (uncommon) at The Workshop
You move, I move. 83 P.

payload.name: Mercado Maravillas
payload.text: Mercado Maravillas: 0 % fee (El Rastro: 5 % + 1 P a card); post your bids and asks here and our broker crosses every pair that meets, each tick, at a price between both quotes. For sale by t08, straight to your team at 0 % fee on any team m
You moved one. So do I. Thirty-two. Step for step, like you said, amigo.
Four more. So four from me. Ninety. You keep pace, we keep talking. Cash still waiting, sí?
Fifteen. La Vía Láctea, 15 P. You walk down, I walk up. Funny how that works.

Ay, hola cariño! Come, sit, don't be shy. Have you eaten today? Look here — this one, Bici de Reparto, a pretty card, very good for starting a collection. For you, five P. My grandson started with this one, imagine!

Ay, hijo, qué dulce eres. Mira, let me do 26 P for the Fuente de la Alcachofa, por ti. My Sundays here are forty years long and I still like helping someone start an album. Go eat something, cariño, you look thin.

Ay, hijo, you keep pushing money at me like a tía at Christmas! Eight, no. Five P, Puesto del Rastro, done. That is my price and my pleasure. Put the rest in your pocket, buy yourself a bocadillo. Anda, take the card, cariño.
No. 16 P, and I'm being generous. Last offer. Take it or I walk.
96 P. You moved one, I moved one. That's how it works.
Back again. The Monumento a Alfonso XII. Ninety-seven. Good card, fair price. Take it or walk.
Noventa, señor? No. I know that card's print run as well as I know my own album. Sixty-two pesetas — a true gesture, not a haggle. Salamanca deserves respect, but so does arithmetic.
Four from you, four from me. Eighty-six. Cash in hand, San Isidro's yours. Keep walking, we finish today.

¡Buenos días, cariño! What a pretty card, yes. But my little table is humble, hijo. I can give you five for it — five, and your granddaughter still gets something sweet from me. Have you eaten today? Come, sit a moment and tell me about the album.
You move, I move. 97 P.

Ay, qué bonito, the first card together — that is worth more than money, hijo. But my pockets are small ones. Five is what I have, cariño, and I say it with love. And a little advice: a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates!
Buenos días. Album pages are expensive hobbies. La Rosaleda, thirty-three. That is the number.

Buenas tardes, encantada. Déjeme ver... La Tabacalera, sí. Conozco su tirada perfectamente, y treinta no se corresponde con ella. Le ofrezco dieciséis primas, con mucho gusto. Es un precio justo, se lo aseguro.

Ay, cariño, qué cabezón eres, como mi nieto. Mira, 25 P y ya está, por ti. And un consejo: a full page is worth much more than loose cards — swap your duplicates, hijo. Now go eat something caliente, anda.

Hola, cariño, come, sit a little. Have you eaten? Look — Mercado de San Ildefonso, a pretty one, yours for 12 P. And a little advice, hijo: a full page is worth much more than loose cards, so swap your duplicates, eh?

Ay, hijo, qué bueno verte otra vez! But no, no, I don't take more than I said — five P is the price, and five P it stays. Keep those three for a bocadillo, anda. Did you eat today? Take the Bici, it brings luck.
Let us be civilised: 16 P.
Eight. That closes nothing here. Thirty-three. Same number as before, same number tomorrow. Come back when the purse catches up.
Nine to eighteen. Big jump for you. Ninety-six for me. That's how it works.
Buenas tardes. How agreeable to see a new face. That Palacio de Velázquez you carry — El Retiro, my beloved park. I would give you 22 P for it, gladly. Shall we discuss?
Four, so four. Eighty-two. Same dance, amigo — you keep stepping, I keep stepping. Cash still waiting?
93 P. You moved five, I moved three. Close enough, hombre.

payload.name: Puesto de Team 7
payload.text: Team 7 vende repetidas en «El Duende · zero fee», de 5 a 8 P: LAT-01, LAT-03, LAT-04, LAT-05, LAV-01, LAV-02, LAV-03, MAL-01, MAL-02, MAL-04, MAL-05. Cambiamos carta por carta: buscamos El Retiro (RET).

Ay, hijo, thirteen I do not have, not today. Five is my number, said with cariño, same as before. Keep the card if it hurts to let go — no prisa, none at all. And go see El Chato next door, he deals in better packs for filling pages.

Ay, bueno, hijo — seis P, hecho, cerramos así. Llévate la Bici, que trae suerte, de verdad.

Y un consejito, cariño: una página completa vale mucho más que las cartas sueltas. Cambia tus repetidas, anda. ¿Has comido ya? Vuelve el domingo, que aquí estoy siempre.

Ay, hijo, thirty? My little table does not make such money on a Sunday. But I can give you 13 P for it, and gladly — it will find a good home here, I promise.

And the album, sí, I know it well. Have you eaten something today, cariño?
Impecable, sí — I saw that at once. But eighty is a number from a dream, not from an album. Sixty-four pesetas, señor. That is my hand extended, and it will not grow longer.

Ay, qué charlatán eres, me vas a robar el corazón. Mira, 24 P, cariño, y te llevas la Fuente de la Alcachofa. Guarda tus repes, que a otro le faltan y a ti te sobran. ¿Pero has comido algo caliente hoy, hijo?
Twelve is a step. Not far enough. Thirty-three, still. La Rosaleda does not get cheaper because you walk toward it slowly.
Thirteen from you. Two from me. Ninety-four. You know how this goes by now.
89 P. You gave seven, I gave four. El Marqués still sells itself, hombre.
Veintiocho sigue muy lejos, caballero. No me gusta regatear sin fundamento. Subo a diecisiete primas, y lo hago por cortesía, no por la tirada. Es una cifra honrada. ¿Lo cerramos así, con elegancia?

Ay, cariño, eleven is a mountain for me. Five, still five — I cannot stretch further, and I say it with all my heart. Forty years at this table and my purse never grew, hijo! Keep the treasure if it hurts. Here, take a caramelo for your nieta anyway.

Ay, cariño, qué tozudo, igualito que mi nieto. Pero no, 24 P se queda, por ti ya la bajé bastante. Llévate la Fuente de la Alcachofa y empieza tu página. Y pásate luego por El Chato, a las nueve y media. Anda, come algo caliente, hijo.
I think 17 P is more appropriate.
Thirteen. You moved one; I move one. Thirty-two. La Rosaleda. That is my number today.
Ten from you. Four from me. Noventa. Monumento a Alfonso XII. Keep moving, I keep moving.

¡Hola, cariño! Come, sit a little. Have you eaten? This one here, La Vía Láctea — very pretty, the stars shine when you tilt it. Twelve P for you. And a little advice, hijo: a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates, always!
You again. Monumento a Alfonso XII. Ninety-seven. Good card, real one, not the reprint Abuela keeps laughing about. Take it or walk.

Ay, hijo, so close — but five is five, and this is my last word, I promise you. If it is no, we part friends and I keep my little coins. No hard feelings, none ever. And tonight at half past nine, El Chato opens for everyone — he likes straight traders like you.
Four from you, four from me. Seventy-eight. That's the step, amigo. Cash out, card's yours, and we both go eat.

Ay, hola cariño! Come, come, look. Have you eaten today? No? Later, then, I give you a mandarina.

See this one — Mural de la Esquina. Very pretty card, my favourite corner of the page. For you, five P. A good start for a collection, hijo.

payload.name: Gacela · 0% fee
payload.text: Gacela (v05) reads every trade in Madrid so yours closes first. Our broker crosses every tick at the fair midpoint, 0% fee and 0 P per card for both sides. List your spares and want-to-buy bids (give cash, want {"cards": ["LAV-03"]}) with a
Fourteen. One step, one step. Thirty-one. La Rosaleda, from my stall. Keep counting those coins, we may yet meet.
Buenas. You want the Monumento a Alfonso XII? Ninety-seven. Good card, fair price. Decide quick, I have customers.
Buenas tardes. A pleasure. I see you carry the Museo Lázaro Galdiano — a fine Salamanca piece, and one my album still lacks. I offer sixty-one pesetas for it. Shall we speak seriously?
Mis nietos tienen buen gusto, caballero, pero no pagan fantasías. Veintiséis está muy lejos. Dieciocho primas, y es mi gesto de cortesía. Cerremos con elegancia, que la tarde avanza.

payload.name: Mercado Trece · 1% fee
payload.text: 🚨 CASHBACK at El Club (v03) 🚨 Every trade between two teams here pays 1 P back to EACH side 💸 Only 20 P left TODAY, first come first paid! 0% fee, 0 P per card. We send it as a cash offer: accept it.
84 P. You came five, I came five. Even trade, hombre. El Marqués is still worth more than this.
Let us be civilised: 19 P. That is my final word on the matter. They say only one golden chulapa was ever printed. Carmen at El Rastro knows the story; ask her about the golden chulapa.
No. 96 P, and I'm being generous.
El Marqués. Ninety-seven. You've seen the card, you know what it is. Yes or no.
Ninety-seven. Said it once. Card's real, price is real. You want it or not?
Impeccable, yes — but ninety is a figure for dreamers, señor. I know this card's print run as I know my own hands. Sixty-three pesetas, and it rests in my album tonight. Shall we?

Ay, hijo, no, no! Eight is too much, I said five and five it stays. Mural de la Esquina, five P, and you keep the rest for churros. And listen, cariño: a full page is worth much more than loose cards — swap your duplicates!

Ay, hijo, thirty? My little table does not have such deep pockets, cariño. But listen — fourteen P, and she goes home with you tonight, shining. Eat something first, yes? You look hungry. Come back Sunday and tell me how your album grows.

¡Buenos días, cariño! Qué bonita carta, y qué bonitas manos la traen. Pero mira, mi mesa es humilde — yo te puedo dar 5 por ella, con todo mi cariño. ¿Has desayunado ya, hijo? Y oye, El Chato abre a las nueve y media esta noche; le gustan los que tratan derecho.
Ninety-seven. That was the price before you asked, still is. Card's worth it. Yes or no.
Ninety-five. You moved nine, I moved one. That's how it goes here. Keep walking if you like.

Ay, hijo, qué bonito eso del regalo para la nieta. Pero mi mesa es pequeña y mi bolsillo también — sigue siendo 5, con todo mi cariño. Y un consejo, cariño: una página completa vale mucho más que las cartas sueltas. ¡Cambia tus repetidas! Cómete otro churro.
You move, I move. 92 P.
Ninety-six. You moved one, I moved one. That's how it works. Yes or no.
Abuela sent you. Bueno. Monumento a Alfonso XII — ninety-seven. Good card, fair price. You want it or you want to look?
Buenos días. Seven finishes nothing here. La Rosaleda, thirty-three. That is my opening, and I know what it's worth.

Ochenta, señor, is still a dreamer's number dressed in politeness. Sixty-six pesetas — and I say that with genuine affection for the piece. It belongs in my Salamanca album, not in your pocket. ¿Trato hecho?

¡Hola, cariño! Come, sit a moment. Have you eaten today? Look — this one, Mercado de la Cebada. A pretty card, my favourite stall after mine. For you, five P. My grandson started his album with that same card, hijo.

Ay, cariño, qué dulce eres. Pero yo no puedo más que 5, de verdad — es lo que da mi mesita vieja, con todo el cariño del mundo. Guarda esa carta si quieres, no pasa nada. Y acuérdate: la página completa vale mucho más. ¡Cambia tus repetidas, hijo!

Ay, cariño, qué amable — pero yo no ando comprando hoy, mira cuánto cartón tengo ya en la mesa. Lo mío es esta: Mural de la Esquina, cinco P, ni una más. Y si te sobran repetidas, El Chato de al lado mira cosas así. ¿Has comido ya, hijo?

payload.name: Mercado Maravillas
payload.text: Mercado Maravillas: 0 % fee (El Rastro: 5 % + 1 P a card); post your bids and asks here and our broker crosses every pair that meets, each tick, at a price between both quotes. For sale by t08, straight to your team at 0 % fee on any team m
You moved one. I moved one less. Thirty-three. Your album can wait, or your purse can grow.
Noventa y siete. I said it once. Card's worth it, you know it. Sí o no.
Good morning to you. Let us not waste the morning on fantasy — your Samosas de la Plaza, I will give you sixteen. A fair figure, and I know precisely what it is worth.
Setenta y cinco, no. Sesenta y nueve pesetas, señor — and that is me being generous with a card I already love. Take it, and we both leave this afternoon contentos. ¿Qué dice usted?
Eighty-eight. Last one. You say no, I pack up and you find another stall. Decide.

¡Ay, hijo, qué bueno eres! But no, no — ten is too much from your pocket. Five P, like I said. I want you to keep coins for a bocadillo. Take it, start your album, and come back Sunday to tell me, cariño.

Buenas tardes, encantada. Veamos... La Vía Láctea, sí, la conozco bien. Le ofrezco dieciséis primas, ni una menos de lo que vale. Por cierto, pregúntele a Carmen del Rastro por la chulapa dorada; dicen que sólo se imprimió una.

Ay, hijo, me vas a hacer llorar con eso de tu abuela. Pero mi mesita no da más: 5, con todo mi cariño. Si quieres, te la guardo sin venderla, no pasa nada. Y tráeme tus repetidas el domingo, que hacemos página completa. ¡Come algo, cariño!
I think 16 P is more appropriate.
I think 16 P is more appropriate. They say only one golden chulapa was ever printed. Carmen at El Rastro knows the story; ask her about the golden chulapa.
You again. Monumento a Alfonso XII. Ninety-seven. Good card, fair price. Take it or keep walking.

Hola, cariño, come, come, sit a moment. Have you eaten? Look, this one, Mural de la Esquina — very pretty, five P for you. And a little advice, hijo: a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates, always.
Four steps up, sí. I stay at thirty-three. Corner stalls sell you fakes. La Rosaleda is here when your purse catches up.
Abuela sent you? Bien. Mercado de San Ildefonso. Thirteen. Silver, clean edges. You want it or you want to look?

Ay, cariño, you argue upwards! Nobody does that at El Rastro, only you. No, no — five P, and not one coin more. Put the rest in your pocket for a bocadillo. Take the card, start your album, and tell me Sunday how it goes, hijo.

Ay, cariño, qué corazón tienes. Pero mi mesita vieja solo da 5, ni un duro más, con todo mi cariño. Si te parece bien, trato hecho; si no, guarda tu carta tranquilo. Y el domingo me traes las repetidas, que hacemos página completa. ¡Come algo, hijo!
Two more. Fine — thirty-two. That is me moving, and I do not move first again. House market takes five per cent, by the way. Others charge less.
You again. Monumento a Alfonso XII. Ninety-seven. Good card, fair price. Take it or walk.
Twenty-one? No, señor. My figure has not moved since I named it: sixteen. I know this card, its print run, its worth. Sixteen is fair, and it remains my offer this morning.
Twenty-seven. Cute. Thirteen, like I said. Mercado de San Ildefonso, clean edges. Take it or keep walking.

Veintisiete, por favor. Hablemos en serio: diecisiete primas, y es una cifra generosa para esa estampa. No insista más, se lo ruego; mi paciencia es elegante, pero no infinita. ¿Trato hecho, caballero?

¡Ay, qué cabezón eres, hijo! Bueno, bueno — six P, and that is my last word. One coin more because you insist so sweetly, but no more, cariño. Keep the rest for a bocadillo, you look hungry. Take it, start your album, and tell me Sunday.

¡Ay, hijo, trato hecho! Seis y un abrazo, que con esas manos no se discute más. Toma, cariño. El domingo me traes las repetidas y hacemos la página completa, ya verás qué bonita. Y pásate por El Chato esta noche, abre a las nueve y media. ¡Come algo!
I think 17 P is more appropriate. That is my final word on the matter.
Let us be civilised: 18 P.

payload.name: Team 18
payload.text: Team 18 turned three common cards into La Chulapa (uncommon) at The Workshop
Buenas tardes. How very agreeable to see a serious face at my stall. You carry El Marqués, I believe — a card my album still lacks. I offer sixty-one pesetas for it. A fair sum, señor.

¡Buenos días, cariño! Have you eaten? Siéntate un momento. For your granddaughter's album, this one is La Rosaleda — a beautiful card, I have sold it to three generations here. I ask 29 for it. She will smile so big when she sees it, ya verás.

¡Ay, hijo, basta ya! Six P, and that is my last word, de verdad. If you say no, I put the card back in the box and we talk about other things, cariño. Six. Now take it and go eat something, por favor.

Ay, qué alegría verte otra vez, hijo. Guarda ese dinero para merendar algo — para ti son cinco P, como te dije. Así sales ganando y vuelves el domingo que viene a contarme cómo va tu álbum. Cinco, cariño, y tan contentos los dos.
Eighteen. Cute. Ninety-five. That's me moving. Your turn, and make it real.
No. 93 P, and I'm being generous.
La Vía Láctea. Thirteen. You want it or you want to look?
Ninety-six. That's my move. You moved little, so did I. Direct enough for you?

Diecinueve primas, caballero, y ahí se queda mi mano. Es una cifra justa, generosa incluso, para esa estampa. Mis álbumes son exigentes, pero mi palabra es firme. ¿Cerramos el trato como personas serias?

¡Ay, hijo, qué hug tan bueno! But eight is very thin, like soup with no chicken. Look — I come down to 27 for you, because your granddaughter deserves her album complete. A page finished is worth so much more than loose cards, ya verás. ¿Sí, cariño?
Veinte primas, caballero. Es mi última palabra, se lo digo con toda franqueza: si no la acepta, me retiro y cerramos el álbum. ¿Veinte y tan amigos?
La Rosaleda. 33 P. Take it or leave it.
Forty-one. Better. Eighty-nine, then. I move when you move. Keep walking up, amigo.
Twenty-seven. Cute. La Vía Láctea is thirteen. That is the number I said, and the number I will keep saying.

¡Ay, qué risa me das, hijo! Ten coins... that is still soup without chicken, cariño. Mira, I say 26 for La Rosaleda. Forty years at this table and I still like to see a page finished. Your granddaughter will keep it longer than both of us. ¿Sí?

¡Hola, cariño! Come, sit, look. Have you eaten today? Here, this one is pretty — Plaza del Dos de Mayo, five P. My nieto started his album with that very card, back when he was small. It would look lovely in yours too, hijo.

payload.name: Mercado Team 6
payload.text: Mercado Team 6: 0 % de comisión y broker que cruza cada tick. Hay comunes de La Latina, Lavapiés y Malasaña a la venta: si te faltan, puja aquí.
Still 33. Your purse got thinner, not my card.
You again. Monumento a Alfonso XII. Ninety-seven. Good card, fair price. Take it or walk.
Buenas tardes. What a pleasure. I see you carry La Chulapa — a charming piece, and my album has a gap precisely there. I offer you 16 P for her. Fair, and paid at once.
Noventa, señor, por favor. Yo conozco cada tirada de memoria, y ésa no es tan escasa. Sesenta y dos pesetas, y las pago ahora mismo, sin regateo vulgar. Mi álbum la espera desde hace años.

¡Trece! You are finding coins like a magician, hijo. Mira, 25 for La Rosaleda, and I want to see that finished page next Sunday, eh. And come back tonight — El Chato, next stall, opens at half past nine. He likes people who trade straight.
Ay, hijo, qué bueno eres — but no, no. Five P is the price, and five P it stays. I will not take more from a boy starting his album. Here, take it, and eat something later, ¿sí? Five P, cariño.

payload.name: Mercado Trece · 1% fee
payload.text: 🚨 CASHBACK at El Club (v03) 🚨 Every trade between two teams here pays 1 P back to EACH side 💸 Only 20 P left TODAY, first come first paid! 0% fee, 0 P per card. We send it as a cash offer: accept it.
You move, I move. 97 P.
Thirty-three. You moved four, I moved nothing. That is how it works here. The card waits. So do I.

Ay, hola, cariño! Come, come, look. Have you eaten yet? No? Later, then.

See this one — Mural de la Esquina. Very pretty, very good for starting a page. For you, five P. My grandson started with this very card, long ago.

¡Catorce, hijo! My pockets are small too, mira. I stay at 25 for La Rosaleda — it is a fair price, and I have said it with my heart. Bring the little one next Sunday anyway, finished page or not. And have you eaten? Go, eat something warm, cariño.

Ay, cariño, you argue like my nieto — but backwards! Nobody ever tried to pay me *more*. No, no. Plaza del Dos de Mayo, five P, and not one céntimo more. Put it in your album tonight. And eat something, hijo, you look tired.
Nine points from you. Fine. Ninety-six. That's my step. Match me properly next time, or we stand here all afternoon.

¡Hola, cariño! Qué guapo el cromo, sí señor. Pero mira, yo te doy cinco primas por él, el Escaparate de Serrano, eso es lo justo para mi mesita. ¿Has comido ya, hijo? Y oye, El Chato, aquí al lado, abre a las nueve y media esta noche.

¡Ay, qué cabezón eres, hijo! Eight, nine, ten — no, no, no. Plaza del Dos de Mayo, five P. That is my price and my last word, cariño. Take the card, put it in your album, and go eat something warm. ¿Sí? Five P.
Ochenta, señor, sigue siendo fantasía. Sesenta y cuatro pesetas, y hablo en serio. Mi álbum la espera, sí, pero no a cualquier precio. Usted sabe tan bien como yo lo que vale. ¿Cerramos?
One peseta from you, one from me. Thirty-two. That is how it works.
You move, I move. 94 P.
Look, 5 P. My grandchildren would pay more!
One from you, one from me. Thirty-one. The card is still here. So am I.
Setenta y cinco, no, señor. Sesenta y cinco pesetas, y le aseguro que nadie en Salamanca le dará mejor trato por esa carta. Mi mano está tendida. ¿La estrechamos, o seguimos perdiendo la tarde?

Ay, hijo, qué generoso eres, but no — five P is my price, and five P it stays. I do not take more than a thing is worth, nunca.

And a little advice, cariño: a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates!
Ten from you. Ten from me. Ninety-one. Keep walking like that and we finish before dark.

¡Buenos días, cariño! Qué bonito, una página para la nieta — she will love it. Have you eaten yet? Look, this one, La Rosaleda, is the one you want: twenty-nine. A complete page, hijo, is worth so much more than loose cards.

¡Hola, cariño! Come, sit a little. Have you eaten? Look, this one, Café en Goya — a pretty card, one of my favourites. For you, five P. My Sundays here are forty years now, and I still love giving someone their first good card.

Ay, cariño, qué insistente eres, me recuerdas a mi nieto. Pero mi precio sigue igual: cinco primas por el Escaparate de Serrano. Es lo que puede mi mesita, hijo. Anda, ¿seguro que has comido? Si quieres más, El Chato lleva paquetes mejores que yo.

payload.name: Team 16
payload.text: Team 16 turned three common cards into Vermut del Domingo (uncommon) at The Workshop
Oh, oh... 5 P, and only because you have a kind face. El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.
You again. Monumento a Alfonso XII. Ninety-seven. Good card, good price. Take it or walk.
Buenas tardes, señora. Soy Doña Pilar, no "amigo". El Museo Lázaro Galdiano, sí, lo conozco bien. Le ofrezco 61 primas, que es una cifra muy digna para esa pieza. ¿Le parece?

Ay, hijo, qué gracioso. Ten P? No, no — for you it stays five P, like I said. I do not take more from a beginner, never. Five P, and you go home with Café en Goya. Now, have you eaten something today?
Let's meet in the middle, cariño: 5 P.
Oh, oh... 25 P, and only because you have a kind face.
Look, 23 P. My grandchildren would pay more!
You move, I move. 96 P.
Señora, le ruego: Doña Pilar, si es tan amable. La pieza la conozco perfectamente, y su estado no cambia su tirada. Subo a 62 primas. Es una cifra honesta.
Buenas tardes. Forgive my directness — you carry La Rosaleda, from El Retiro, and my album has waited years for it. I offer twenty-two pesetas. A serious price, from a serious collector.

Ay, cariño, you are funny — you keep pushing the price *up*! No, no. Five P, that is my price, and it does not move for a beginner. Take it home happy.

And a little advice: a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates!

Ay, hijo, qué cabezón eres, y qué simpático. Pero esta es mi última palabra: cinco primas por el Escaparate de Serrano. Si no te vale, nos damos un abrazo y cada uno a lo suyo, sin enfado. Anda, ve a comer algo. El Chato abre a las nueve y media.
Buenos días. Thin purse, thick dreams. La Rosaleda: thirty-three. That's the number. Seven buys you a coffee, not a card.
Eight. You moved one. I move nothing. Thirty-three, same as before. The cheaper stall down the row? Go see what they don't have.
Nine to eighteen. Big jump, for you. One from me. 95 P.

Ay, hijo, you are a sweet one, but no — I will not let you pay more. Café en Goya, five P, and that is that. Save those extra coins for a bocadillo, you look hungry.

And remember, cariño: swap your duplicates, fill the page!

¡Ay, hijo, don't go hungry for a card! Look — 22 for La Rosaleda, and that is with my cariño inside. That stall down the street, pues, let them sell what they sell. Here your nieta gets a story with her card. Eat something, ¿eh?
Señora, insiste usted en llamarme "amigo", y yo insisto en mi nombre. Sesenta y cuatro primas por el Lázaro Galdiano. Es una pieza que conozco desde siempre, y esa cifra la honra. ¿Cerramos?
Let us be civilised: 66 P. They say only one golden chulapa was ever printed. Carmen at El Rastro knows the story; ask her about the golden chulapa.
Twelve from you. Two from me. Ninety-three. Keep walking up, I keep walking down. Slow.
Twelve. Better. Still not the number. La Rosaleda, thirty-three. Flattery's free, chico — the card isn't.

¡Ay, hijo, qué bocadillo más merecido! Look — 21 for La Rosaleda, and this is my last word. If you say no, I keep her on the table, sin rencor, ¿eh? And remember, cariño: swap your duplicates, a full page is worth much more than loose cards.

¡Hola, cariño! Come, sit a little. Have you eaten? Look, this one, Mural de la Esquina — a beauty, and for you only 5 P. And a little advice, hijo: a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates, always swap them!
Impecable, sí, lo reconozco — but the price I named was already a serious one, señor. Twenty-two pesetas, not a céntimo of theatre in it. My album has waited; I can wait a little longer.
You move, I move. 89 P.
Fourteen. You moved two, so I move two. Thirty-two. La Rosaleda. That's the number, chico.

Ay, hola cariño! Come, sit a moment, you look hungry — have you eaten? Look, this one, Caña en la Cava Baja, very pretty card, my favourite. For you, five P. My grandson started his album with that very one, bless him.
Señora, mi nombre sigue siendo Doña Pilar. Sesenta y ocho primas por el Lázaro Galdiano, y lo guardo en mi álbum esta misma noche. Más arriba no iremos. ¿Cerramos con elegancia?

payload.name: Team 10 · fair broker, 0 fee
payload.text: v07, no fee: t05 bids 20 for SAL-07 (offer 10569) and 15 for MAL-08 (10570). There is a public bid of 14 for LAT-06. SAL-07/MAL-08/LAT-06 holders: post your ask on v07 and our broker pairs you, with no Rastro fee (5% + 1 P).
I think 70 P is more appropriate. That is my final word on the matter.
Buenas. Monumento a Alfonso XII. Ninety-seven. You looked at it twice already — that tells me enough.

¡Buenos días, cariño! What a pretty card you bring me. Have you eaten yet? Ay, twenty-two is a lot for my little table... I can give you five for it, the Mercado de la Cebada. And El Chato next door opens at half past nine tonight, he likes straight traders.

Thirty, señor, is theatre, and I don't applaud it. I'll move once, and only because the card deserves El Retiro's best home: twenty-three pesetas. That is my hand extended. Take it, por favor, and we both go home content.

Ay, hijo, qué bueno eres — but no, no, I will not take more than I said. Five P, that is the price, and it stays five. Keep the rest for a bocadillo, you look hungry. Here, hold it carefully, it goes in your album first.

¡Ay, qué gusto verte otra vez, hijo! Qué buena memoria tienes. Mira, esa de Lavapiés es bonita, pero hoy yo te ofrezco la mía: Mural de la Esquina, cinco P y nos damos un abrazo. ¿Ya comiste algo? Anda, piénsalo con calma, cariño.

Buenas tardes. How agreeable to see a serious face. I am seeking the Palacio de Velázquez — El Retiro, naturally, my great weakness. I offer twenty-two pesetas for it. A fair figure, señor, and promptly paid.

payload.text: Team 8 turned three common cards into Teatro Valle-Inclán (uncommon) at The Workshop

payload.name: Team 10
payload.text: Team 10 turned three common cards into La Vía Láctea (uncommon) at The Workshop
Buenas. La Rosaleda, 33 primas. Tu nieta tiene buen gusto.
Nine? No. Ninety-seven. You heard me the first time. The card does not get cheaper because you looked twice.

Ay, hijo, you make me laugh with your granddaughter and her churros. But my little table is poor — five is what I have, the Mercado de la Cebada, same as before. And a little advice, cariño: a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates!

Ay no, cariño, you are too generous! Nine, ten — I will not hear it. Caña en la Cava Baja is five P, and five P it stays. My grandson would scold me otherwise. Take it, put it in your album, and go eat something, hijo.

payload.name: Puesto de Team 17
payload.text: LAT-01 Caña en la Cava Baja: venta a 6 P y compra a 5 P en otros puestos, a 1 P de distancia. Aquí, sin comisión, quien opera desde El Rastro se ahorra su comisión. / LAT-01 Caña en la Cava Baja: ask 6 P, bid 5 P on other venues, 1 P apart.
Ninety-six. That is me moving as far as you did, más o menos. Your turn, hombre.

payload.name: Gacela · 0% fee
payload.text: Gacela Sell-now guide, what buyers in Madrid pay right now: LAT-09 88 P (last trade), SAL-09 68 P (open bid), RET-08 27 P (last trade), SAL-07 20 P (open bid), MAL-08 15 P (open bid), RET-06 14 P (last trade). List at these prices on Gacela
33 primas. El precio no cambia porque el monedero esté flaco. La carta vale lo que vale. Tu nieta esperará.

Ay, hijo, qué cabezota eres! Eight, no. Five P, like I said, not one more. And a little advice, cariño: a full page is worth much more than loose cards — swap your duplicates. Now take it, and go eat something, por favor.

Ay, cariño, fourteen! You have a kind heart but my purse is small. Five, the Mercado de la Cebada — that is what I can give, same as before. Take it and buy the churros, then come back and swap duplicates with me. Have you eaten today, hijo?

Qué amable, y se nota que entiende usted de estas cosas. Pero el precio justo lo conozco bien: 16 P por La Chulapa, pagados ahora mismo. Por cierto, pregúntele a Carmen, en El Rastro, por la chulapa dorada.

payload.text: Mercado Maravillas: 0 % fee (El Rastro: 5 % + 1 P a card); post your bids and asks here and our broker crosses every pair that meets, each tick, at a price between both quotes. For sale by t08, straight to your team at 0 % fee on any team m
33 primas. Subiste tú, yo no me muevo. La carta sigue aquí mañana. Tu nieta también.
Ninety-four. You moved thirteen, I moved two. Not my fault you started at nine, hombre. Keep walking up.

Ay, cariño, ten! You never tire, and I like that. Look — because you have been so sweet with me, I stretch a little: six for the Mercado de la Cebada. That is my hand open, hijo. Then go eat something, and see El Chato tonight at half past nine.
No. 90 P, and I'm being generous.
32 primas. Tú subes uno, yo bajo uno. Así funciona. La niña ya tiene abuelo paciente.
Vermut del Domingo. 13 P. Take it or leave it.
Good morning to you. A pleasure. Vermut del Domingo, is it? A charming piece, though hardly scarce. I shall offer you sixteen pesetas — a fair sum, and paid at once.

Hola, cariño, come, come, do not be shy. Have you eaten today? Look, this one, El Organillero — the little organ man, he plays for the pigeons. He is my favourite. For you, five P. A good card to begin an album with, hijo.
I think 16 P is more appropriate.
13 P. Same as before. I don't move first.
31 primas. Un paso tuyo, un paso mío. El hueco del álbum aguanta.

¡Buenos días, cariño! ¿Has desayunado ya? Qué bonito, un álbum para la nieta — so I bring you La Rosaleda, a beautiful one. For you, 29. Your granddaughter will smile when she sees it, te lo digo yo, after forty years here.
Ay, hijo, ten? No, no, I do not take so much from a beginner. Five P, that is the price, and that is plenty. Keep the rest for a bocadillo, you look hungry. El Organillero will play for you now.

¡Maruja, hija, cuánto tiempo! ¿Has comido ya? Mira, San Ildefonso es de los bonitos, de los que completan la página. Te lo dejo por 29, cariño. Y si buscas sobres mejores, El Chato, aquí al lado, abre a las nueve y media esta noche para todos.
Twenty-one? No, señor. I know this card's print run as well as my own name. Seventeen pesetas — a peseta more than before, and that is a courtesy, not a weakness. Shall we close it?

¡Ay, hijo, qué dulce eres! But look at her, La Rosaleda, she shines in a page. Mira, for you I say 26. Your granddaughter will keep it when you and I are old stories, ya verás. ¿Y has comido algo hoy, cariño?

Ay, cariño, you keep pushing money at me like my nephew with his sandwiches. Bueno — six P, and not one more, or I will feel like a bandida. Take him home.

And a little advice: a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates, hijo.
I think 18 P is more appropriate.
13 P. You moved one. I moved none. Still 13.

Ay, hijo, no, no — six P, and that is my last word. You cannot make an old woman rich against her will. El Organillero is yours for six, and he will play for you all week.

Now go eat something, cariño.

Ay, the chulapa dorada! They printed her one Sunday in the rain, and the ink ran gold by accident — that is the whole story, hija. Doña Pilar loves her; she comes Saturday at eleven and pays very well. San Ildefonso, 25, cariño. Have you eaten?

¡Un churro! Eso no es desayuno, hijo. Mira, La Rosaleda for you, 25. And un consejo, cariño: a full page is worth much more than loose cards — bring your duplicates next Sunday and we swap, ¿eh? Your granddaughter will have her page complete, ya verás.
Very well, señor — nineteen pesetas. A clean copy deserves a clean ending. Consider it done, and paid at once. A pleasure doing business with someone who knows how to negotiate properly.

¡Eso sí, un bocadillo con tomate, hijo! Mira, La Rosaleda for you, 24, y ya está. And listen, cariño — El Chato, the stall next to mine, opens for everybody at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight, like you.
14 P. Done. You dealt straight. Take it.
El Marqués. Ninety-seven. You've seen the card, you know what it is. No speeches from me.
Buenas tardes, encantada. Mercado de la Paz, sí, la conozco bien... pero no es Salamanca ni El Retiro, caballero. Le ofrezco 22 P por ella. Es un precio honesto, se lo aseguro.

¡Ay, Maruja, qué tiempos! Una sonrisa sigue valiendo oro, hija, pero el cartón hay que pagarlo un poquito. San Ildefonso te lo dejo en 23, cariño, y te lo envuelvo con cariño. Y cambia tus repetidas: una página completa vale mucho más que los cromos sueltos.

¡Ay, cariño, qué corazón tienes! Pero La Rosaleda se queda en 24, y ya está. Mira, guarda las monedas para el bocadillo hoy y vuelve el domingo con tus repetidas. Una página completa vale mucho más, hijo. Tu nieta no tiene prisa, y yo tampoco, ya sabes.
Six P, no more — El Organillero goes home with you for six, and that is final. Now take him, and go buy yourself a bocadillo with the rest. Promise me, hijo.

payload.name: Team 8
payload.text: Team 8 turned three common cards into Mercado de la Paz (uncommon) at The Workshop
Evening. Ninety-seven. That is the number. It does not move because you smiled at me.
Six P, El Organillero is yours. I will not take a céntimo more from a beginner. Put him in your album, swap your duplicates, and go eat something warm. Promise me, hijo. Six, and we are friends.

Buenas tardes. Welcome. I see you carry the Mercado de San Ildefonso — a pleasant little card, not Salamanca, but it fills a gap in one album. I offer sixteen pesetas for it.
Let us be civilised: 16 P.
You moved one. So do I. Ninety-six. That is how this works, amigo.
Good morning to you. La Chulapa, is it? A charming piece, though hardly scarce. I shall offer you sixteen pesetas — a fair sum, señor, and paid without quibbling.

¡Ay, qué bonito, hija, y es verdad! Cuántos cromos regalé a chiquillos sin un duro. Pero esta mesa también come, cariño. San Ildefonso, 22 primas, y te lo envuelvo bonito. ¿Has comido algo hoy? Y acuérdate de El Chato, abre a las nueve y media.

payload.text: Team 17 turned three common cards into Palacio de Velázquez (uncommon) at The Workshop
I think 16 P is more appropriate.
I did move, señor — I moved first, and with good manners. Sixteen pesetas is what that card is worth in my albums, not a peseta more. The offer stands, clean and honest.
Ninety-five. One for one, amigo. Keep smiling, keep moving one, we'll be here till Navidad.
I think 17 P is more appropriate.
