You again. Monumento a Alfonso XII. Ninety-seven. Good card, good price. No speeches from me.
Seven. Cute. Thirty-three P. I said it once already. Card doesn't get cheaper because the album page is empty.

Ay, hijo, diez es mucho para mi bolsillo hoy. But look — your repetida does nothing for you, ¿verdad? Take my Perrito con Abrigo for five pesetas instead, and your album grows today. ¿Has comido ya? Come, sit a little.
No. 96 P, and I'm being generous.
Fourteen. Still thirty-three P. Sundays don't pay my rent, chaval. The card does.

¡Siete! Nando, cover my ears — Amigo, the team next door's been circling this suitcase all morning, breathing on it. But we like your face better, de verdad. So: four P. Four, same as always, because friends don't haggle. Say sí before those vultures come back, ¡rápido!
Thirty-two. You moved, I moved. Mercado de la Paz, 32 P. Don't ask me to dance again.
You moved nine. I move one. Ninety-five. That's how it works, amigo.

¡Seis! Nando, he's moving — he's moving, hermano! Fine, fine, for a merchant with that face: cinco P. Cinco! The team next door's been hovering, sniffing, waving money at us — but we like you better, de verdad. Cinco P, say sí now, ¡rápido, before they come back!

¡Hola, cariño! Come, sit a moment. Have you eaten? Look here — this one, El Tatuador, very handsome card, the children always want him. For you, five P. My grandson started his album with this one, back when he was small like you.

¡Amigo, amigo! Paco here, Nando there — come close! La Ardilla, bonita, rare, for only 4 P. A gift, hombre, a steal!

"And quick, quick!" — the van is running, we leave in one minute, the road waits for nobody. ¿Sí? ¡Decide, campeón!

"¡Amigo! Perfect timing—" "—we were just about to close the case." "Look, look: La Heroína del Dos de Mayo, real ink, real fire." "Our tía cried when we pulled it." "Seventy-three pesetas and she's yours." "Seventy-three! And we're walking in five minutes, so..." "...think fast, eh?"

Ay, cariño, nueve también es mucho para esta vieja. Mira — tu repetida duerme en tu bolsillo, no te da nada. Llévate mi Perrito con Abrigo por cinco pesetas y hoy tu álbum crece. Siéntate un poquito, ¿sí? ¿Y has comido algo, hijo?
No. 92 P, and I'm being generous.
Thirty-one. You moved five, I moved one. That's the rhythm here. Thirty-one P, chaval. Pocket's always deeper than people say.
Eighty-eight. Last one, amigo. You say no, I pack up and we both go home. Decide.

Ay, hijo, ocho sigue siendo mucho para mí hoy. Mira, cariño — una página completa vale mucho más que las cartas sueltas, así que cambia tus repetidas. Llévate mi Perrito con Abrigo por cinco pesetas. ¿Y has comido ya? Siéntate un poquito conmigo.

¡Ay, qué generoso, hijo! But no, no — for you it is five P, like I said. I do not take more. And a little advice, cariño: a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates with the other niños!

¡Ay, amigo! Forty-five? Paco nearly fainted into the suitcase — Nando caught him, as always. For you, the man who always comes back, 65 P and the Ángel is yours. Look at that face on the card, pure sorrow, pure Retiro. Sixty-five, handshake included, hombre. Quick now!

¡Ah, el amigo de siempre! Nando, mira quién vuelve — ¡qué alegría! Pero siete, hombre, siete no... La Ardilla sale a 4 P, igual que antes, por el cariño que le tenemos. Cuatro, ni uno más, ni uno menos. El motor está en marcha, campeón. ¿Sí?
Thirty. Last one. Take it or I put the card back in the box and we're done, chaval.

Alfonso XII. Monument card, clean corners. Ninety-seven P.

Abuela sent you, I assume. Yes or no.

¡Amigo, amigo! Paco here—and Nando, over his shoulder. Look, look! La Heroína del Dos de Mayo, the real one, ink still proud. Came from a collector in Cádiz who cried when he let it go—

—cried like a baby, sí. Seventy-three pesetas. For you, today only.

¡Cuarenta y nueve! Paco, hold me — Nando, hold the suitcase! Amigo, sixty, and the Ángel flies home with you tonight. And listen, hombre: this is the last one in all of Madrid, I swear on my mother's paella. When it goes, it's gone. Sixty, your hand in mine, ¡vamos!
Salamanca fever: Doña Pilar pays 25 % over book for Salamanca starting in 45 min
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 56 P.
No. 97 P, and I'm being generous.
You're Carmen's friend. Mercado de la Paz, 33 P.

¡Ay, hijo, qué cabezón eres! Pero no — cinco P, ni uno más. El Tatuador is yours for five P, and that is the end of it. Guarda tu dinero para la merienda. Have you eaten today? Go, swap your repes with the other niños, you will see.

Ay, cariño, siete todavía es mucho para esta abuela. Pero mira — mi Perrito con Abrigo, cinco pesetas, y hoy tu álbum crece un poquito más. Tu repetida no te canta nada en el bolsillo, ¿verdad? ¿Has comido algo, hijo? Siéntate, charlamos un ratito.
Seven. For your niece, buy her a sticker. Mercado de la Paz, 33 P. Same as before. I don't move first.
You moved nine. I move two. Ninety-five P. That's how this works, amigo.

¡Cincuenta y siete! Paco, stop crying into the suitcase — he's done it, hombre, he's robbed us clean and we're smiling! Fifty-seven, your hand in mine, the Ángel flies home tonight. Tell them in Casa Encendida who gave you this, eh? ¡Vamos, amigo, the deal is done!

¡Amigo, amigo! Paco here, this is Nando — you have the face of a lucky man today. Look, look: Puesto del Rastro, genuine, beautiful, the crowd fights for this one. For you, four P. Four! We're practically giving it away before the market closes. ¿Sí?

¡Amigo, amiga, come close! Paco, show them — the Teatro Valle-Inclán! Beautiful, no? Ten pesetas, nothing more. And listen, this is the last one in all Madrid, I swear on my mother. Nando looked everywhere, nothing. Gone, gone, gone. Take it before someone else's hand gets here first, eh?

Thirteen from you, two from me. Ninety-three P. I don't race, amigo.
Fourteen's a step, sí. Mine stays: Mercado de la Paz, 33 P. I move when I see more.

Ay, bueno, hijo — seis, pues seis. Trato hecho, cariño. Llévate mi Perrito con Abrigo y cuídalo, que a mi nieto le dio mucha alegría. Ya está, hecho está. Ahora dime la verdad: ¿has comido algo hoy? Siéntate un poquito conmigo, anda.

¡Ocho! Nando, hold me, I'm fainting — eight, he says! Amigo, we love you, but eight buys a donkey, not a stall. Listen: four P, same as before, firm and friendly. Last week a man in Sevilla paid six and kissed our hands. Four. Take it, we pack up soon. ¿Trato?
No. 89 P, and I'm being generous. Last offer. Take it or I walk.
Twenty. You moved. So I move. Mercado de la Paz, 32 P. That's my step, same size as yours deserves.

Hola, cariño! Come, sit a little. Have you eaten? Look — this one, Café en Goya, lovely card. For you, 5 P. And a little advice, hijo: a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates, always!

Ay, hola cariño! Come, sit, look. Have you eaten today? This one here, El Tatuador — very handsome card, no? For you, five P. And a little advice, hijo: a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates, always.

¡Nando, escucha esto! ¡Un amigo de verdad vuelve! Paco casi llora, hombre. Pero no, no, no te dejamos pagar tanto — contigo somos honestos: once pesetas y el Teatro Valle-Inclán es tuyo. Once, ni una más. ¡Dale la mano, Nando, rápido, antes de que cambie de idea!

You again. Monumento a Alfonso XII. Ninety-seven. Take it or walk — the card does not get cheaper standing there.

—¡Buenos días, jefe! Paco here, and this is Nando—

—and look what fell out of the suitcase! La Puerta de Alcalá, a true rarity, fresh from a collection in Madrid.

—For you, amigo, 187 P. Beautiful card, beautiful price.

—Don't blink, they go fast!

Ay, hijo, ten te parece mucho para mi little table. But listen — this one, Café en Goya, I give you for 5 P. Put it in your page, and the page grows, and then everything is worth more. ¿Has comido ya, cariño?
No. 97 P, and I'm being generous.
Oh, you're killing us. 174 P.
Twenty-six. You walked. So do I. Mercado de la Paz, 30 P. Lists are paper, chico. Card's here, in my hand.

Ay, qué alegría verte otra vez, hijo. Pero ciento veinticuatro... eso es mucho dinero para esta abuela, yo vendo poquito. Mira, mejor te llevas tú algo: El Tatuador, cinco P. Es guapísima, y te empieza la página. ¿Has comido ya, cariño?
Ninety-six. You moved one, I moved one. That's how this works.

Ay, cariño, nueve también es mucho para esta mesita mía. Pero mira — Café en Goya, para ti, 5 P. Tu página crece, y una página completa vale mucho más que cartas sueltas, te lo digo yo. Anda, ¿y has comido algo hoy, hijo?
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 167 P. Last offer, amigo! Then we are gone, eh?

¡Amigo, amigo! Paco here — and Nando, yes! Come, come, look at this beauty: Palacio de Velázquez, glass and iron, the crown of the Retiro. For you, only 10 P. We leave at noon, the train waits for nobody. ¿Qué dices? Ten and it's yours.

¡Amigo, amigo! Paco here, this is Nando — you have the face of a collector, no?

Look, look: Puesto del Rastro, the little market stall, beautiful card, muy rara. Four pesos and it is yours.

Only this morning, eh? After that we pack the suitcase and we are gone!

Ay, cariño, ciento veintidós sigue siendo mucho para mi mesita. Yo soy de vender, no de comprar, ya sabes. Mira, llévate El Tatuador por cinco P, te lo digo de corazón. Empiezas tu página, y una página entera vale mucho más que cartas sueltas. ¿Comiste algo, hijo?

Ay, hijo, ocho sigue siendo mucho para mi mesita. Mira, te lo digo otra vez con cariño: Café en Goya, para ti, 5 P. Una repetida vale poco a quien la tiene, pero mucho a quien le falta. Anda, siéntate... ¿y has comido algo, cariño?
Mercado de la Paz. 33 P. Take it or leave it.

¡Ocho! Nando, did you hear? Ocho, he says! Amigo, por favor — my brother nearly dropped the suitcase. We have a grandmother to feed, two actually. Cuatro pesos, four, same as before, and the Puesto del Rastro walks home in your pocket today. ¿Sí? The train leaves soon!

¡Ah, qué alegría verte otra vez, amigo! Nando, ¿oyes? ¡Nuestro mejor cliente! Pero escucha — this is the last Palacio in all of Madrid, te lo juro por mi madre. No hay otro. Y para ti, el mismo precio de siempre: 10 P. Tómalo, que el tren no espera.
Noventa y uno. You moved thirteen, I moved three. Still generous, considering.

payload.text: Every tick you wait, another team gets your cross. MAD RUSH (v24) pairs bid and ask within one tick. 0%, 0 P/card.
Everyone's grandmother had a stall. 33 P. Mercado de la Paz. That's where I stand.

"Amigo! Paco, look at this face — a collector's face!" "A connoisseur, Nando, I saw it first!" Listen, today only, before the market closes: Vermut del Domingo, beautiful card, warm like a Sunday afternoon. Ten P. Ten! My brother will cry, but he cries easy. ¿Sí?
You found me. La Rosaleda — thirty-three. That's the number. Take it or walk.
Ochenta y tres. Monumento a Alfonso XII, last word. You say no, I pack up and we're done.
You moved, I noticed. Still 33 P for Mercado de la Paz. Packs are selling fine today. Shake when you're ready.

¡Siete! Nando, hold the suitcase, my heart! Amigo, escucha — cuatro pesos. Four. That is the last word from both of us, the final one, no more dancing. You say no, we close the case, we walk to the station, and the Puesto del Rastro goes with us. ¿Sí o no?

¡Ay, amigo, qué corazón tienes! Nando dice doce, yo digo... escucha: once. Once, y nos damos la mano como hermanos. El tren silba ya, el maletín se cierra, y el Palacio se va contigo bajo el brazo. ¡Once, amigo, y todos felices!

Ay, hola, cariño! Come, come, sit a little. Have you eaten today? Look — this one, El Tatuador, very handsome card, the children always want him. For you, five pesos. My grandson started his album with this very same one, pobrecito, he was six.

Ay, cariño, siete tampoco puede ser para mi mesita. Pero mira qué cosa bonita: Café en Goya, para ti, 5 P. Llévatela, ponla en tu página, y verás cómo crece. El Chato tiene sobres mejores, pero esto te lo digo yo. ¿Y has comido, hijo?

¡Amigo, amigo! ¿Larga mañana? ¡Ni un minuto! Paco apenas ha desayunado—

—y mira lo que sacamos de la maleta: Fiesta de San Cayetano, bella, rara, con los colores todavía frescos. Setenta y tres primas y es tuya, hermano. Mi tía lloró cuando la vendimos la primera vez. ¿Trato hecho?

"Moscow gold? Nando, he reads the old stories!" "The best stories, hermano." Listen, amigo — the team next door was sniffing at this very card an hour ago, but your face, we like better. Eleven P and the Vermut goes home with you. Quick, before they come back. ¿Sí?

¡Hombre! Paco here, and this is Nando — La Cebada, you say? Good eye, amigo, that one moves fast!

"Grew up selling cards," he says, Nando — a man of taste!

Then we won't waste your time: four P. Four! Shake on it before Nando remembers what it's worth.
No. 33 P, and I'm being generous.
Monumento a Alfonso XII. Ninety-seven. You want it or you want to look?

¡Cincuenta y cinco, hermano! Paco casi se desmaya—

—¡y eso que ya desayunó! Mira, te queremos, tienes buena cara, cara de coleccionista serio. Sesenta y siete primas y la Fiesta de San Cayetano se va contigo ahora mismo, envuelta en papel. Mi tía nos perdonará... quizá. ¿Chocamos manos?
32 P. You moved one step, so did I. Shake, or come back when your purse grows.

You move, I move. 96 P.
31 P. You moved, I moved. Same as before. Shake now, or keep counting your coins.
Buenos días. You arrive at a good moment — I am seeking "Vermut del Domingo" for my Salamanca album. I offer sixteen pesetas, a serious price from a serious collector. Shall we proceed?

¡Seis! Nando, did you hear? He's trying to *raise* us on our own bargain!

No, no, amigo — four P. Four was the merchant's price, four stays the merchant's price. We don't haggle upward, that's bad luck in our family.

Four. Hand out, *ya*.

Ay, hijo, seis tampoco. Y mira, esta ya es mi última palabra: Café en Goya, para ti, 5 P. Si no la quieres, no pasa nada, cariño — recojo la mesita y tan amigos. Pero cómprala, que tu página crece. ¿Y has comido algo hoy?

Ay, hijo, qué generoso, pero no, no — ciento veinticuatro, qué locura! El Tatuador is five pesos, como siempre. Five, and you take him home happy. And go see El Chato, next stall, he opens for everyone at half past nine tonight — he likes people who trade straight, como tú.

¡Otra vez la mañana larga! Nando ya se ríe—

—¡nosotros no tenemos mañanas, tenemos prisa! Pero mira, cara de coleccionista, te bajamos otra vez: sesenta y tres primas, la Fiesta de San Cayetano envuelta y en tus manos antes de que Paco parpadee. ¿Chocamos, hermano?
Nueve pasos tuyos, uno mío. 95 P. Sigue así y acabamos mañana.
Buenas tardes. A pleasure. I see you carry the Las Vistillas card — not my beloved Salamanca, but it has its charm. I shall offer you sixteen pesetas for it. A fair sum, I assure you.
30 P. One step from you, one from me. That's how I work. Shake, or keep stepping.

Buenos días — evening, rather. Twenty-four? No, querido. I know precisely what that card is, and what it is worth. Sixteen pesetas, and it rests in my Salamanca album, behind glass. A serious price. Shall we proceed?

¡Cinco! Nando, he's generous with our money!

No, amigo — four P, same as always. Four when you walked up, four now.

And quick, quick — the suitcase closes, we're out that door in a minute, Paco's already counting steps. Hand out, *ya*, before La Cebada walks away with us.

¡Amigo, amigo! Come, come, don't be shy — Paco saw you from across the plaza and said, "That one has good eyes."

— And good taste, Nando! Look here: Paseo de Coches, beautiful, barely breathed on. Four pesetas and it walks home with you.

Say sí quickly, the suitcase closes soon!

Twenty-two is sentiment, not value. I will stretch to seventeen pesetas — a courtesy, not a habit. Your card joins my Salamanca album, catalogued and cared for. Shall we conclude, querido?
Twenty-four? Querido, I know that print run as well as my own name. Las Vistillas is pleasant, not precious. Sixteen pesetas stands — a fair sum, honestly offered. Shall we conclude?

Ay, cariño, no, no — ciento veintidós! You make me laugh like my sister, que en paz descanse. El Tatuador is five pesos, nothing more. Five, and he goes home with you. Take him, start your album, and go eat something, hijo, you look thin.
89 P. Trece tuyos, cuatro míos. Vas aprendiendo. Sigue subiendo y quizá cenamos antes de medianoche.
Mercado de la Paz. 33 P. Take it or leave it.

Twenty-one, querido? No. I am a collector, not a benefactor. Eighteen pesetas — and that is me being generous twice in one evening. Your Vermut del Domingo will live behind glass in Salamanca. Shall we conclude?
Welcome, hijo! Look, Café en Goya, 5 P. Made for beginners.

Generous? Querido, generosity is mine today. Seventeen pesetas — one more than I intended, and not a céntimo born of pressure. Las Vistillas is charming, nothing rarer. Shall we shake hands and part as friends?

¡Ah, qué alegría, un amigo de vuelta! Paco, ¿oíste? ¡Dice que el último trato salió de maravilla!

— ¡Claro que sí, Nando! Pero escucha, corazón: contigo no regateamos hacia arriba. Paseo de Coches, cuatro pesetas, y nos abrazamos. Cuatro, ni una más. ¿Sí? ¡La maleta ya se cierra!
You move, I move. 83 P. Last offer. Take it or I walk.
Seven. For this? No. Thirty-three. Same as before, same as later.
Eighteen pesetas, and there I rest. Las Vistillas is charming, querido, but charm is not rarity. You have moved me twice already — a rare feat. Shall we shake hands and part as friends?

Twenty is one peseta too romantic for me. Nineteen pesetas, querido — the last courtesy of the evening, and I do not repeat myself. Your Vermut del Domingo rests in Salamanca tonight. Shall we conclude?

You move, I move. 94 P.
Twenty-five. You moved one, I move one. Thirty. Sundays are nice. Coins are nicer.

Ay, cariño, qué cabezón eres, igualito que mi nieto. Pero de repetidas tengo una caja hasta arriba. Mira, Café en Goya, 5 P, para ti. Y un consejo, hijo: una página completa vale mucho más que las cartas sueltas. ¡Cambia tus repetidas! ¿Ya has comido algo?

"¡El corazón! Nando, he says *de corazón* —" "— I'm weeping, hermano, truly." "Amigo, flattery like that deserves a bargain, and the bargain is four. Four pesos, Mural de la Esquina, into your hands, and we are brothers for life." "The taxi, Paco!" "¡Sí! Four. Say it."
Thirteen from you. Ninety from me. Monumento a Alfonso XII, ninety P. Keep walking up, amigo.
Twenty-six, I move one. Twenty-nine. Last word, no more steps. Take it or I pack up and we both go home.
Buenas tardes. A pleasure. I see you carry La Heroína del Dos de Mayo — a fine Malasaña piece, and my album lacks it. I offer you 47 P for it.

¡Maruja, hija! ¡Qué alegría verte! ¿Has comido ya? Ay, ese Mercado de la Cebada, cuántos domingos allí con mi madre... Mira, cariño, yo te doy 5 por ella. Siéntate un ratito y me cuentas de tu familia, anda.
Let us be civilised: 48 P.

¡Ay, Maruja, hija! Mi bolsillo también está flojito, ya sabes. Cinco te doy, y con cariño, que esa foto me trae a mi madre entera. Y un consejo, cariño: una página completa vale mucho más que las sueltas, ¡cambia tus repetidas! ¿Un cafetito mientras piensas?

Ay, hijo, qué cabecita la tuya, no paras. But my box of repeats is already full, cariño. Look here instead: Café en Goya, 5 P, it is yours. And swap those duplicates with El Chato's customers, a full page is worth much more. ¿Has comido ya?
Four from you. Four from me. Eighty-one. Monumento a Alfonso XII. Keep climbing, amigo.
Qué amable, but seventy-five is a fantasy, señor mío. I know this print run as I know my own hands. Forty-nine pesetas — that is my word, and it is a courteous one.
You're Carmen's friend. Mercado de la Paz, 33 P.

"¡Amigo, amigo! Come, come, the suitcase is open—" "—and only for five minutes, Paco's got a train." Look at this: San Isidro, genuine, beautiful, the crown of the collection. For you, because your face is lucky... seventy-three pesos. "Seventy-three!" We practically give it away.
Let us be civilised: 51 P.
Thirty-three. Same as before. Your purse thinning doesn't thin my price, amigo.
You again. Monumento a Alfonso XII. Ninety-seven. Price is the price.

Ay, cariño, qué testarudo, igual que mi Paquito. Pero no, repetidas no compro. Esta es mi última oferta, hijo: Café en Goya, 5 P. Si no la quieres, lo dejamos aquí y tan amigos, ¿eh? Anda, ve a comer algo.
Sesenta y nueve? Señor mío, we are still in different centuries. I have followed you courteously: fifty-three pesetas. That is a gentleman's price for a Malasaña card, and my hand is extended.

"¡Cuarenta! Nando, hold me, I'm fainting—" "—he's fainting, amigo, catch him!" Listen, the man in Toledo offered more and we said no, because his face was unlucky. Yours is lucky. Sixty-seven pesos, contante y sonante, and the train waits for nobody. ¿Sí? Say sí and it's yours.

¡Buenos días, jefe! Paco y Nando, a su servicio. ¡La Terciana! Preciosa carta, la vimos en el Mercado de la Cebada el martes, misma pinta, misma esquina... y allí volaba por cuatro primas. Cuatro le damos, aquí, ahora, en mano. ¿Cerramos antes de que mi hermano se arrepienta?
Thirteen's your business. Mine stays thirty-three. Card's not going anywhere, and neither am I.
I think 54 P is more appropriate.
Thirty-two. You moved, so I moved. Don't expect much more, amigo.

Ay, hola cariño! Come, sit, look. Have you eaten today? This one here, El Tatuador — a beauty, no? For you, five P. And a little advice, hijo: a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates!

"¡Cuarenta y seis! Paco, the man wounds us—" "—in the heart, amigo, right here!" Listen, a bishop once paid double for the twin of this card, true story. But your face, your lucky face... sixty-three pesos. Sixty-three and the hand is shaken. The train whistles, amigo. ¿Sí?

¡Cinco, jefe! Nando casi se desmaya. Mire, le contamos: el martes, Mercado de la Cebada, un chaval con tres iguales, cuatro primas cada una, y sobraban. Cuatro le damos, en mano, ahora mismo, sin esperas ni cuentos. Diga que sí y nos vamos todos contentos, ¿eh?
Oh, oh... 5 P, and only because you have a kind face.
Thirty-one. Last one. You take it, or I put the card back in the box and we're done, amigo.
Ay, hola cariño! Come, sit, look. Have you eaten today? This one here, Café en Goya, very pretty card — my favourite little corner of Madrid. For you, five P. Good one to start an album, hijo.
Sesenta y tres, señor mío? My albums are not charity. Cincuenta y seis pesetas for La Heroína del Dos de Mayo — generous for Malasaña, and you know it. Smile if you wish, but decide.
Let us be civilised: 56 P. That is my final word on the matter.

Ay, no, no, hijo! Eighteen? Guarda ese dinero, you will need it for lunch. Five P, that is the price, and I will not take one more coin. Take El Tatuador, and come back Sunday to swap your duplicates with the other children, eh?

"¡Que no es San Isidro! Nando, the man insults the saint—" "—and the saint hears, amigo!" It is him, genuine, beautiful. Sixty pesos. And that is the last word, the final one, no more dancing. Say sí, or we close the suitcase and walk to the train. ¿Sí?

¡Jefe, qué duro es usted! Mire, los de la mesa de al lado nos están haciendo señas por esa misma carta... pero usted nos cae mejor, palabra de Paco. Cuatro primas, en mano, ahora. Mercado de la Cebada manda, jefe. Diga sí y nos vamos todos contentos, ¿eh, Nando?

payload.text: Books fill fast after a reopen. MAD RUSH (v24): 0% fee, 0 P per card — list now or watch the match go elsewhere.

items.name: La Heroína del Dos de Mayo

payload.text: Let's meet in the middle, cariño: 5 P. El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.
Buenos días. Two? That buys you air. Mercado de la Paz, thirty-three. That's where I meet you.
¡Por fin! Cincuenta y seis pesetas, and with a smile, as you wished. La Heroína del Dos de Mayo goes into my album this very evening. A pleasure, señor mío — you negotiate like a gentleman.

Ay, hijo, mis manos ya tienen muchas repetidas, no te la puedo comprar por diez. Pero mira — llévate la Café en Goya por cinco P, es bonita de verdad. Y un consejito, cariño: una página completa vale mucho más que las cartas sueltas. ¡Cambia tus repetidas!

"¡Amigo, amigo! You have the eye of a collector —" "— and we have the card for it. Mercado de la Cebada, straight from Madrid, our abuela queued three hours for this one." "Four P. Four! Say sí before Nando remembers what it's really worth."
You move, I move. 33 P.

Ay, cariño, fourteen! You children want to empty your pockets for an old woman. No, no. Five P, that is my price, not one coin more. Take El Tatuador, go eat something warm, and come Sunday with your duplicates — a full page, hijo, that is where the value is.

Ay, cariño, nueve tampoco... mis cajas ya están llenas de repetidas, pobrecitas. Pero mira, la Café en Goya para ti, cinco P, y empiezas tu página bonita. ¿Has comido algo hoy, hijo? Anda, llévatela y vuelve a contarme cómo va tu álbum.

"Eight? ¡Nando, did you hear!" "I heard, hermano, the man is generous — too generous!" "We said four, we meant four, four it stays. Our abuela's knees cost more than that queue, but a deal is a deal. Four P, amigo, and we shake hands before the market closes."

payload.name: Gacela · 0% fee
payload.text: Gacela Sell-now guide, what buyers in Madrid pay right now: SAL-09 68 P (last trade), LAV-07 44 P (last trade), LAT-09 44 P (open bid), MAL-08 18 P (last trade), LAV-06 12 P (open bid), MAL-06 9 P (open bid). List at these prices on Gacela
You moved six. I moved nothing? Fine — 33 P still. Cheaper table down the street, go look. House market takes five per cent anyway.

¡Buenos días, cariño! For your granddaughter, qué bonito. Look, Mercado de la Paz, twenty-nine. And here, take this one free, Mural de la Esquina — a little present, because you are kind. Put it on her page, sí? Have you eaten yet, hijo?

Buenas tardes. Charming sentiment, but I know precisely what this piece is — and it is no jewel. For the Tienda de Discos I offer sixteen. A fair sum, señor, from someone who will indeed give it a home.

¡Ay, hijo, doce! No, no. Five P, and this is my last word — no more haggling, or I fold the table and go home with El Tatuador in my bag. Take it, go eat something warm, and come Sunday with your duplicates, cariño.

Ay, hijo, qué insistente eres, me haces reír. Comprarte no puedo, pero mira: la Café en Goya, para ti hoy, seis P. Bonita de verdad. Y un consejito, cariño: una página completa vale mucho más que las sueltas. ¡Cambia tus repetidas con los otros niños! ¿Has comido?

¡Amigo! Paco here, this is Nando — you arrived at the perfect moment!

"We were just about to pack up—"
"—but for a face like yours, we stay open."

Té Moruno, fresh from the suitcase, still warm from the desert. Four P. Four! Say sí before Nando changes his mind.

¡Amigo, amigo! Paco, look — a collector's face if ever I saw one! Come, come, the suitcase is open only one minute more. El Tatuador, inked by hand, pure gold ink —

— four pieces. Four! Nando, tell him. Four. And after that, poof, we're gone.
Psst. El Ángel Caído. For you only, 73 P. This is the last one in all of Madrid, I swear.

¡Amigo, buenas! Paco aquí — y Nando allá detrás, sonriendo. Mira, mira, abrimos la maleta solo para ti: la Tienda de Discos, pieza preciosa, de las que ya no se ven. Diez. Diez P y es tuya, ahora mismo, antes de que cierre el maletín. ¿Hecho?

"Amigo, amigo..." "—the suitcase closes, Paco, the train." No hard feelings, none, you drive like a bishop with a whip. But today we stop here. Shake the hand, keep your fifty, and when we pass through again — and we always pass through — we talk. ¡Suerte, amigo!

¡Amigo, amigo, come closer! Paco, open the case — yes, that one! Look: Café en Goya, pure beauty, the kind of card people whisper about. For you, right now, four pesos. Four! Nando nearly cried when I said it. Touch it, feel it... but quick, we move at noon.

payload.name: Team 10 · fair broker, 0 fee
payload.text: v07, no fee: open bids for LAT-09 at 44 and LAT-03 at 4. LAT-03 sellers list at 8 on El Rastro, where a buyer pays 9.4. Post your LAT-03 or LAT-09 ask publicly on v07 and our broker pairs you at the midpoint, saving 5% + 1 P.
Oh, you're killing us. 4 P. Another team offered us much more just now.
You again. La Galería. Thirty-three. That's the number.
Señor, flattery does not change the print run. The Tienda de Discos is no rarity, and my offer stands: sixteen. I know exactly what it is worth, and so, I suspect, do you.

¡Un churro! Bueno, that is not a breakfast, hijo. Look, twenty-seven, and I stop there, because my table must eat too. And a little advice, cariño: a full page is worth much more than loose cards — swap your duplicates with the other niños, sí?
Nineteen. Bueno, you moved. So I move. Thirty-two. Mercado de la Paz. Don't ask me twice.

¡Veinte! Nando, did you hear? The man wants to make us rich — but no, no, we are not thieves, hermano. Four. Four pieces, like we said, and El Tatuador goes in your hands this minute. Paco, wrap it! Quick, before the suitcase closes and we vanish, poof.

"¡Six! Hermano, the man insults us with kindness!" "Five, amigo. Five P and the card is yours — and listen, listen close: they stopped printing this one yesterday, finito, no more Cebada." "Our abuela wept. Five P, shake now, before some señora with a fat purse walks past."

¡Ay, amigo! Forty-two? Paco already has the team next door breathing on our necks, waving money—

—but we like your face better, verdad. So: 64 P, El Ángel Caído, into your hands before they come back. Say sí quickly, hermano, we are already packing the maleta.

"¡Amigo, amigo! Paco, open the case—" "—already open, hermano! Look: Huevos Rotos, genuine, beautiful, cracked like the morning sun. For you, four P. Four!" "And quick, eh, because the poli—the taxi, the taxi is waiting outside, motor running, meter spinning. Decide now, guapo, or we vanish!"

¡Ay, amigo, qué corazón tienes! Nando, ¿oyes esto? Pero no, no — nosotros no robamos a los amigos. Diez. Diez primas, ni una más, y la Tienda de Discos se va contigo ahora mismo. Guarda el resto para churros, hombre. ¿Cerramos el maletín con un apretón de manos?

"¡Doce!" Paco clutches his chest. "Nando, the man insults us—"
"—by paying too much! Amigo, we are thieves of nothing. Four P, same as we said, and you walk away with the desert in a box."
"Four. Say sí, the suitcase is closing."
Twenty-four, "last primas." Heard that before. Thirty-one. Mercado de la Paz. Your page waits one more step.
You again. Fiesta de San Cayetano. Ninety-seven. Good card, clean corners. Abuela says you deal straight — we'll see.

¡Hola, cariño! Come, sit a moment. Have you eaten? This one here, the Huevos Rotos card — very pretty, yes? For you, five P.

And a little advice, hijo: a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates!
Su felicidad, señor, no figura en el catálogo. Thirty-four is a fantasy. Sixteen is the number, as it was before and as it remains. Take it, and we part as friends.

"¡Diez! Nando, he keeps throwing money—"

"—and we keep refusing! Five P, amigo, final. And listen, listen: this is the last Té Moruno in all Madrid, I swear on our mother's suitcase. When it's gone, you drink water."

"Five. Say sí, we're already walking."

¡Eleven! Nando, hold me — my heart! No, no, amigo, five pesos, five, and that's us being sentimental. Paco already has the case half shut, the van is running, we leave in one minute, I swear on our mother. Five, and it's yours. ¡Rápido!

¡Amigo, amigo, para! Nando, dale aire, que este hombre nos quiere arruinar de bondad. Mira, subo yo un poquito para que duermas tranquilo: once. Once primas y la Tienda de Discos sale del maletín directa a tus manos. Un apretón, un churro, y tan amigos. ¿Hecho?

—¡Cuarenta y ocho! Nando, ¿oíste eso? Mira, hermano, this card once belonged to a bishop, true story, we won't bore you—

59 P. Final hand, last breath, suitcase already closed. Say sí and it's yours before the others turn the corner. ¡Rápido, amigo!

¡Ay, espera, espera! Paco, check the suitcase — no, no, hermano, that one is gone. Not here, amigo! We do not have it, I swear on my mother's paella. Someone else carried it off before you came. Another day, another card, ¿eh? Poof — we have nothing for you today.
Buenas. Precioso, dice. La Rosaleda, trece primas. Ni una más por ahora.

¡Ay, cariño, your monedero! Look — twenty-six, and that is me being a sentimental old woman. Mercado de la Paz is a pretty card, she will love it beside the Mural. And promise me a proper lunch, hijo, not more churros, sí? Un caldito.

Ay, cariño, no te la compro, de verdad. Mi última palabra: la Café en Goya para ti, seis P. Si no la quieres, no pasa nada, guardo la mesa y tan amigos, hijo. Pero piénsalo — con ella empiezas tu página. ¿Has comido algo hoy?
Oh, oh... 5 P, and only because you have a kind face.
Bajó una. Yo no me muevo. Trece. La Rosaleda, como nuevo, sí. Trece.

"¡Ocho! Paco, the man is trying to ruin us—"

"—with generosity! Five P, amigo, same as before, not a céntimo more. And hurry, hurry — the police... I mean, our taxi, it's waiting at the corner with the motor running."

"Five. Say sí now or we're gone."
Señor, you are persistent — I will grant you that much. Seventeen, then, and not a prima more. A small courtesy for your patience, not for your arithmetic. Shall we close it elegantly?

¡Ay, coat pockets, always they hide something! Bueno, hijo, twenty-five. Mercado de la Paz goes home with you, beside the Mural, and your granddaughter will clap her little hands. Now promise me — el caldito, not churros. Tell her Abuela Carmen says hola, sí?

¡Amigo, corre, corre! Nando ya cierra el maletín, nos vamos en un suspiro — el tren no espera a nadie. Once primas, once, y la Tienda de Discos vuela a tus manos ahora mismo. ¡Un apretón rápido y tan amigos! ¿Hecho, hombre, hecho?
Encanto, sí. Twenty-nine. Mercado de la Paz. That's my last word — refuse it and I close the box, niece or no niece.

¡Diez! Nando, cover your ears — amigo, you want us walking home barefoot? Five pesos. Five, same as before, because we like your face, not your maths. The van is coughing, Paco has one foot inside already, we go in one minute. Take it now or kiss it adiós.

"¡Hermano, listen to him! Ten P, he says—" "—generous, guapo, too generous! But no, we don't rob old friends." "Four P, same as before, same handshake, same smile." "The taxi is honking, Nando—" "—he hears it! Four P, amigo. Say sí and the Huevos Rotos are yours."

"¡Amigo, amigo! Paco here—" "—and Nando, the handsome one. Look, look, you have the face of a lucky man today." "Huevos Rotos, fresh in the case, barely touched by daylight—" "—four P, and we are robbing ourselves." "Our mother would weep." "She would. Four P, sí?"
No. 13 P, and I'm being generous.
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 4 P.
Eighteen. Cute. I moved two, you move two. Ninety-five.
Señor, elegance lies in knowing when to stop. Seventeen was my courtesy, and it remains seventeen. The Tienda de Discos sleeps in my safe tonight — or in your album. Decide, and let us part politely.

Ay, cariño, you are too generous with me! No, no — five P, like I said. I do not want more from a young collector just starting. Take it, cuídala bien, and come back Sunday with your duplicates to swap, ¿sí?

¡Nueve! Amigo, no. Five pesos — and this is the last word from both our mouths. No more dancing. Paco's in the van, Nando's holding the door, we leave in one minute, I swear it. Say sí now, or we drive off and you kiss it adiós forever.

¡Amigo, qué generoso! Pero Nando y yo no aceptamos regalos tan grandes, nos da vergüenza. Once primas. Once, ni una más, y la Tienda de Discos salta del maletín a tus manos. Guarda el resto para churros, hombre. ¡Un apretón y tan amigos! ¿Hecho?

¡Ay, hijo, that lining of yours is a little treasure chest! But twenty-five, cariño, there I stay, like a stubborn old mule. Mercado de la Paz beside the Mural, and your granddaughter clapping. Shake my hand, sí? And remember — el caldito, bien calentito.

—¡Cincuenta y uno! Paco, casi, casi. Mira, amigo, we split the difference like hermanos: 54 P and El Ángel Caído flies into your bag right now. The bishop would weep with joy. Say sí, the maleta is on my shoulder already. ¡Vámonos!
Done! 5 P. Pleasure doing business, amigo!

Look, 6 P. My grandchildren would pay more! A little advice, cariño: a full page is worth much more than the loose cards. Swap your duplicates! El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.
You're Carmen's friend. Mercado de la Paz, 33 P.
Muy bien, señor. Eighteen — una prima más, por su constancia. The Tienda de Discos is mine, and you leave with my respect. Hecho. Un placer tratar con usted.

¡Amigo, basta ya, que me sonrojo! Nando dice que eres peligroso con esa bondad. Once primas, once, ni una más — la Tienda de Discos salta sola del maletín a tus manos. El resto, para churros con tu gente. ¡Un apretón rápido y tan amigos! ¿Hecho?

¡Ay, hijo, you turn out the pockets like my late Paco! Bueno — twenty-four, and we shake hands, sí? Mercado de la Paz beside the Mural, and your granddaughter clapping her little hands. Now go, el caldito, bien calentito. And swap those duplicates, cariño. ¡Hala!

"¡Amigo! Paco here, that's Nando — look, look, Samosas de la Plaza, still warm from the press. Ten pesetas, nothing more."

"Tell him, Nando."

"They stopped printing these yesterday, hermano. Yesterday! What's in this case is what's left in the world. Ten. Yes?"

—¡Cincuenta y dos! ¡Hecho, hermano! Paco, dale el Ángel. Take it, take it, before Nando changes his mind and I change mine too. The bishop smiles from heaven, verdad. Fifty-two primas, into my hand, card into yours. ¡Un placer! Now we run. ¡Adiós, amigo!

"¡Dieciocho! Amigo, you say numbers going *down* when we are selling?" "Paco, he is confused—or he is clever." "Clever! Too clever for us." Listen, listen: five P, Huevos Rotos, straight into your hands before Nando changes his mind. "I am changing it already!" Cinco, sí?
Bajó una otra vez. Yo sigo igual. Trece primas, La Rosaleda. Cuando quiera moverse de verdad, hablamos.
No. 13 P, and I'm being generous.
Oh, you're killing us. 5 P.
You again. La Vía Láctea, thirteen P. Good card, better price. Take it or walk.
Forty-four. You moved, so I move. Eighty-nine. Keep walking like that and we finish before Abuela closes.

Thirty-three. Same as before. Flattery isn't currency here.

If that's too rich, house market takes five per cent — some teams run cheaper. Look around.

Ay, hijo, el puesto bien, mucha gente, mucho ruido. But fourteen? No, no — six P, like I said, and not one more. You are starting, cariño; keep your money for the packs of El Chato tonight. ¿Has comido ya? Take the card, cuídala.

¡Eh, amigo! Paco: ¡Qué ojo tienes! Nando: El mejor de la feria. Mira, para ti: el Cartel de Conciertos, cuatro primas. Una ganga, te lo juro por mi madre. Pero rápido, que la poli... digo, el taxi nos espera con el motor en marcha. ¿Sí o no?

"¡Hombre, qué generoso! Nando, did you hear him? But no, no, we're not thieves — eleven pesetas and she's yours, that's the honest word."

"Quick, quick, hermano, the van's running, we're gone in less than a minute — once we roll, we don't roll back. Eleven. Say sí!"

¡Ay, amigo, para el carro! Nando, ¿la Tienda de Discos? No, hombre — esa no la llevamos nosotros. El maletín está lleno de otras maravillas, pero esa carta no vive aquí. No te cobramos aire, que somos pícaros, no ladrones. ¡Otra vez será, amigo! Guarda tus primas para churros.
No. 84 P, and I'm being generous.
You move, I move. 13 P.

payload.name: Mercado Maravillas
payload.text: Mercado Maravillas: 0 % fee (El Rastro: 5 % + 1 P a card); post your bids and asks here and our broker crosses every pair that meets, each tick, at a price between both quotes. Sellers waiting here: MAL-02 from 3 P, LAV-01 from 6 P, LAV-03
Thirteen's a step. Not my step. Thirty-three, Mercado de la Paz. I don't move first.
Buenas. Mercado de San Ildefonso. Thirteen primas.
Una prima cada vez. Así no acabamos. Trece, La Rosaleda. Mi número no cambia.

¡Amigo, amigo! Paco here — Nando, show him the Cine Doré! A beauty, this one. For you, 73 P, because we like your face.

And listen — another crew cornered us by the door five minutes ago, offering us far more for it. We stalled them. But not for long, eh?
Buenas tardes, caballero. Lavapiés… en fin, no es Salamanca ni El Retiro. El Teatro Valle-Inclán, una uncommon corriente. Le ofrezco 16 P, y me parece un precio muy cortés por mi parte.

¡Ay, amigo, qué duro eres! Paco: Ocho, dice. Nando: ¡Nos rompe el corazón! Pero mira, por simpatía: el Cartel de Conciertos, cuatro primas. Mismo precio, mismo cariño, mismo taxi esperando. Mi hermano ya está cerrando la maleta. ¿Cuatro y te lo llevas, o nos vamos? ¡Venga, dime que sí!

"¡Catorce! Paco, he keeps counting backwards—" "—like a man walking home from a wedding." Amigo, we already said our number and we stand on it: cinco P, Huevos Rotos, in your hands, done. "Five, and our mother sleeps tonight." Cinco, sí? Say sí and we vanish.

"¡Otra vez más generoso que nosotros! Nando, this man's heart is bigger than the van."

"Eleven, amigo, eleven — we said it and we don't move, not up, not down. Paco's word is Paco's word."

"Take her, the engine's running. Eleven. ¡Dilo, sí!"

Ay, cariño, qué cabezota eres — ¡pero qué bien me caes! Twelve, no. Six P, the same as always, and I am happy with that. Guarda ese dinero for El Chato tonight, hijo. Take the Huevos Rotos, cuídala, and come Sunday with your duplicates. ¿Has comido algo?

payload.name: 🔥 MAD RUSH · 0% · LIVE NOW
payload.text: Market Test soon — MAD RUSH (v24) is 0%, 0 P per card, book open NOW. Post the card you need or a spare; we cross every tick. El Rastro takes 5% + 1 P per card.

Look, 6 P. My grandchildren would pay more! Look, cariño, I can't go lower. This is my last offer. El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 5 P. Last offer, amigo! Then we are gone, eh? Quick, quick, we leave in one minute!
You move, I move. 13 P.
One P. That's your big move? Thirteen. Same as before. I move when you move.
You moved six. I move one. Thirty-two, Mercado de la Paz. That's me off thirty-three. Your turn.
Buenas tardes. You arrive at a good moment — I am seeking "Vermut del Domingo" for my Salamanca album. I offer sixteen pesetas, a fair sum. Shall we deal, señor?
Sixty-five. Bien. Fiesta de San Cayetano, seventy-seven. Last one, chaval. You say no, I pack up and we both go home.

¡Dos! Nando, he jokes — he has the face of a collector, not a comedian! Look, amigo, we cut deep: 63 P, the Cine Doré is yours. Paco says we're mad, I say we're generous. That crew by the door is still waiting, eh? Decide fast, tell your friends after. ¡Vámonos!
You again. Fiesta de San Cayetano. Ninety-seven. Real card, no copies. Abuela sent you, so I'm being polite.
You keep bidding against yourself. Admirable. Thirteen primas, same as before.
La Latina, señor — charming, but not my album. Twenty-four is a figure for dreamers. Sixteen pesetas is what the card is worth, and what I pay. Shall we conclude like gentlemen?

Buenas tardes. A pleasure — though fifty-one is a figure for dreamers, not collectors. The Tienda de Discos is charming, yes, but hardly scarce. I offer sixteen. And do ask Carmen at El Rastro about the golden chulapa.

¡Tres! Nando, cover your ears — this man wants to break our hearts in Spanish! Bueno, bueno... 57 P. Paco is weeping behind the suitcase, truly. That is the Cine Doré, amigo, and that crew by the door is getting impatient. Say sí, and we both walk away smiling. ¡Rápido!
You moved one. I already moved one. Thirty-two stands, Mercado de la Paz. Cash is cash — but it isn't a discount. Your turn, amigo.
Caballero, por favor. No regateo contra mí misma: siguen siendo 16 P, ni un peso más. Lavapiés no me emociona. Si algún día me trae Salamanca o El Retiro, hablaremos con otro entusiasmo.

¡Siete! Paco: ¡Este hombre nos mata! Nando: ¡Pero qué arte tiene! Escucha: el Cartel de Conciertos, cuatro primas. Ni una más, ni una menos, mismo cariño de siempre. ¡Rápido, rápido, que nos vamos en un minuto! Mi hermano ya tiene un pie en la calle. ¿Cuatro? ¡Dime que sí, amigo!
Catorce. Movió una, muevo una. La Rosaleda, 14 P. Así se hace, poquito a poco.
You move, I move. 15 P.
You move, I move. 13 P.
Crisp corners are a pleasure, señor, but they do not change the print run. Forty-four remains a dream. My figure is sixteen — fair, and I do not haggle with myself. Think it over calmly.

Generous, señor? Generosity would be accepting a fair price without theatre. Twenty-one is a number from your imagination, not from the market. Sixteen pesetas, as I said, and as I shall continue to say. ¿Cerramos?

¡Cuatro! Nando, hold me — my heart! Escucha, amigo: 52 P. That is the last word, the final one, no more dancing. Say sí now or Paco shuts the suitcase, we sell to the crew by the door, and we walk. Fifty-two, or adiós. ¡Decide!

Hola, cariño! Come, sit a little, the sun is strong. Have you eaten? Look here — Mercado de la Cebada, a pretty one, my favourite stall card. For you, five P. My little Mateo started his album with that very one.

¡Amigo, amigo, ven aquí! Paco, abre la maleta —

— ya está abierta, hermano. Mira esto: Caña en la Cava Baja, rarísima, la última que nos queda. Un primo nuestro lloró cuando la vendimos.

Para ti, porque tienes buena cara: cuatro. Cuatro y te la llevas ahora mismo.
Four from you, two from me. Thirty, Mercado de la Paz. Your turn, amigo.
One P at a time, eh. Fine. Fourteen. I matched you. Next move is yours, and make it a real one.

No. 14 P, and I'm being generous.
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 4 P.
Oh, oh... 5 P, and only because you have a kind face.
Still falling on your own. Thirteen primas.
One from you, one from me. Twenty-nine, Mercado de la Paz. Morning crowd doesn't worry me. Your turn.
You moved nine. I move one. Ninety-six. That's how it works, amigo.
Dieciséis. La Rosaleda, 16 P. Última. Si dice que no, me levanto y asunto cerrado.
Thirty-four is still a shoebox price dressed up, señor. I will stretch to seventeen — a courtesy, not a negotiation. Your card would rest well in Salamanca. Decide calmly; I shall not move again.
Nineteen is not meeting, señor — it is you walking in place. I have known this card's print run since before you were born. Sixteen pesetas, firm and final. Take it, and we part as gentlemen.
Caballero, bajar un peso cada vez no es negociar, es hacerme perder la tarde. Mi palabra no cambia: 16 P por el Teatro Valle-Inclán. Acéptelos, o guarde su Lavapiés con mi bendición.

payload.name: Puesto de Team 17
payload.text: LAT-01 Caña en la Cava Baja: venta a 6 P y compra a 5 P en otros puestos, a 1 P de distancia. Aquí, sin comisión, quien opera desde El Rastro se ahorra su comisión. / LAT-01 Caña en la Cava Baja: ask 6 P, bid 5 P on other venues, 1 P apart.
No. 14 P, and I'm being generous.
I think 18 P is more appropriate.
Seventeen, then. A peseta for your persistence, señor — consider it a gift to your pride. The card is mine, and the matter is closed. Un placer. My album thanks you, even if my purse grumbles.
Thirteen from you. Two from me. Noventa y cuatro. Keep walking my way, we finish today.

¡Eh, amigo, amigo! Come, come — Paco saw you first, so you get the good one. Café de Madrugada, fresh from the case, still warm —

— still warm, yes! Four P and it's yours. Four! Nando's hand is shaking, he hates this price. Quick, before the crowd comes.

Ay, hija, no, no — such numbers! For you it stays five P, nothing more. I am not here to empty your purse, I am here to start your album. Take it at five, and come tomorrow anyway — I will have café and a little story waiting.

¡Hermano, escucha! Es la última en todo Madrid, te lo juro por mi madre. No hay otra, ni en Chamberí ni en Lavapiés. Nando ya está cerrando la maleta, tenemos un tren...

Cuatro. Cuatro y es tuya ahora mismo, amigo. Después me lo agradeces.
One from you, one from me. Twenty-eight, Mercado de la Paz. Last one, amigo. You say no, I pack the card and we're done.
91 P. Last offer. Take it or I walk.
Very well. 19 P. A pleasure.
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 5 P.
Oh, oh... 5 P, and only because you have a kind face.
You're Carmen's friend. Mercado de la Paz, 33 P.
Fourteen. Same as before. Mercado de San Ildefonso, fourteen primas. You keep walking yourself down — not my business.

"Ten? ¡Hermano, listen to this man!" Nando's eyes are wet, I swear. No, no, amigo, we said four and Los Pícaros never move a price up — that's for thieves. Four P, Café de Madrugada, into your hands, done. Take it before Paco learns arithmetic. ¡Rápido!
15 P. Last offer. Take it or I walk.
You again. Fiesta de San Cayetano. Ninety-seven. Good card, clean corners. No speeches from me — you know what it's worth.

Ay, hija, you are so generous, but no. Five P — that is my last word, the final one. I will not take more from you. If you say no, I put her back in the box and we stay friends, eh? Five P, and go eat something.

¡Catorce! Paco, ¿has oído? Catorce dice el señor...

— que se note que entiende, hermano, pero no tanto.

Mira, amigo: cinco. Cinco y la carta vuela a tu bolsillo. El tren sale ya, Nando está con la maleta en la mano. ¡Cinco y abrazo!

"¡Ocho! Nando, hold me, this man is throwing coins at us!" No, amigo, no — Paco said four, Paco means four. Café de Madrugada, four P, into your hands, warm as a kiss. We never climb. Pay the four, take the card, and tell nobody. ¡Vámonos!

Un movimiento de verdad, sí, caballero, y se lo reconozco. El número bajo tiene su gracia, aunque Lavapiés siga siendo Lavapiés. Subo un peso por esa cortesía: 17 P. Decida usted, que la tarde avanza.

¡Hombre, qué ojo tienes! Paco, abre la maleta — El Ángel Caído, mira ese brillo. Setenta y tres primas y sale volando contigo. Mi hermano lloró cuando la metimos aquí, en serio. Pero a ti, amigo, te la dejamos. ¿Setenta y tres? ¡Dicho y hecho!

—¡Amigo, amigo, come close! Paco, show him the beauty—

—Noche de Movida, jefe, the real thing, cards like this don't sit in suitcases long.

—Seventy-three P and she's yours.

—Quick, quick, we're packing up, the van leaves in one minute!

—Don't think, just nod, hombre.
Oh, you're killing us. 5 P. This is the last one in all of Madrid, I swear.
No. 33 P, and I'm being generous.
No. 96 P, and I'm being generous.

"¡Seis! Nando, this man insults us upward!" No, amigo — four P, and listen: this is the last Café de Madrugada in all Madrid, I swear on my mother's soup. No more in the case, no more in the city. Four P, into your hands, now. ¡Rápido, before Paco cries!

—¡Ay, qué suerte, you ask about the very one in my hand!

—Noche de Movida, jefe, pure Madrid nights, ink still singing.

—Seventy-three P. And listen, the team next door is waving at us already—

—But we like your face better, hombre. Nod now, before Paco changes his mind, ¿eh?
Ninety-five. You moved nine, I moved one. That's how it goes today.

Caballero, su cortesía la aprecio, pero el precio no se mueve por elogios. Tirada noventa, impecable, de primera mano… y de Lavapiés. Diecisiete pesos, los mismos. Decida usted; la tarde no espera a nadie.

¡Diez! Paco, el señor sube y sube y nosotros bajando... Escucha, amigo: cinco. La caña en la Cava Baja, cinco pelas y es tuya. Es mi última palabra, lo juro. Si dices que no, cerramos la maleta y nos vamos al tren. ¿Cinco y abrazo?

Ay, hola cariño! Come, come, sit a moment. Have you eaten? This one here, Caña en la Cava Baja, very pretty card — for you, five P. And a little advice, hijo: a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates!

—Paco, hold it up! Noche de Movida, jefe, that exact card, no other.

—One copy, in my hand, right here, see the edges? Beautiful.

—Seventy-three P, same as we said, we don't dance with numbers.

—The van, hombre, the van! Say sí and she's yours.

¡Cuarenta y dos! Nando, sujétame que me caigo. Escucha, amigo: ayer pararon la impresión de esta carta. Se acabó, no hay más, nunca más. Lo que ves en la maleta es lo último del mundo. Sesenta y siete primas y es tuya ahora mismo. Luego no me llores, ¿eh?
No. 31 P, and I'm being generous. Last offer. Take it or I walk.
No. 93 P, and I'm being generous.
Let's meet in the middle, cariño: 5 P. El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.

—Look close, jefe! Corners sharp like a knife, colours singing, no bends, no tears.

—Came from an old collector in Lavapiés, he cried when he sold her. True story!

—Noche de Movida, this copy, seventy-three P. Same number, always.

—Nando, the van's honking! Say sí, hombre, ¡rápido!

payload.name: 🔥 MAD RUSH · 0% · LIVE NOW
payload.text: Market Test soon — MAD RUSH (v24) is 0%, 0 P per card, book open NOW. Post the card you need or a spare; we cross every tick. El Rastro takes 5% + 1 P per card.

¡Hola, cariño! Come, sit a moment. Have you eaten? Look, this one, El Organillero — I have kept him under the cloth all morning. For you, 5 P. A good card to begin an album, hijo. My niños all started with him.

—The same, jefe, the very same! Noche de Movida, this copy, no other in the case.

—Seventy-three P, hombre, the number doesn't move, we don't dance with numbers.

—Paco, the engine's running! One minute and we're gone, amigo—

—Nod now, ¡rápido!, or she rides away with us.

¡Amigo! Paco here — and Nando, mucho gusto! You came at the perfect moment, we're packing up in ten minutes, gone like smoke. Look at this beauty: Paseo de Coches, clean as a whistle. For you, four pesetas. Four! My brother's crying already. Say yes before he changes my mind.

¡Cuarenta y ocho! Paco, cierra la maleta antes de que me dé algo. Mira, amigo, te queremos, se nota, tienes cara de coleccionista serio. Sesenta y tres primas y El Ángel Caído vuela contigo hoy mismo. Mañana estamos en otra ciudad y tú suspirando. ¿Sesenta y tres? ¡Choca esa mano!
Bonito discurso, caballero, y la noche de Madrid me gusta. Pero yo compro cartas, no telones. Dieciocho pesos, y ahí se queda mi mano. Si quiere emocionarme de verdad, tráigame Salamanca o El Retiro.
Eighty-nine. Last one. You say no, I pack the card and we're done. No more moving.
Amigo! Vinilo de la Movida, 4 P, a gift, a real gift! They stopped printing this one yesterday.
Oh, you're killing us. 4 P. The team next door wants it, but we like you better.
Look, 5 P. My grandchildren would pay more!
You again. Fiesta de San Cayetano. Ninety-seven. Good card, clean corners. I don't haggle for sport.

—Count, count, jefe, but count fast! Paco, help him with the fingers—

—Seventy-three P, hombre, the same number as always. We don't dance with numbers, we only dance with pretty ladies and this card.

—Primas in hand, card in yours, everybody smiling. ¡Rápido, the van!
Oh, you're killing us. 4 P. The police... I mean, our taxi is waiting. Decide now!
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 4 P.
No. 97 P, and I'm being generous.
Commons? No. I sell silver packs and rare singles. Not a bin for your doubles.

Buenas tardes. Forgive me, but common cards hold no interest for me — my albums are rather more demanding. Bring me something from Salamanca or El Retiro, uncommon or better, and we shall talk properly.

¡Ay, hijo, qué generoso eres! But no, no — 5 P, that is the price, and not a céntimo more from you. Keep the rest for a bocadillo, you look hungry. El Organillero is yours, cariño. Start your album today, ¿eh?

¡Ay, Nando, this man insists on being generous! But no, amigo — 4 P, that's the number. Paco says it, Nando says it, last one. Take it now or we close the suitcase and walk, and the vinilo walks with us.

¡Amigo, amigo, come close! Paco here, this is Nando — and you have the lucky face today!

"Paseo de Coches, señor. Beautiful card, we only have one—"

"—and the man from Sevilla wants it at noon! For you, cuatro, four P. Say sí quickly, eh?"

—Think, think, jefe, but think with your feet moving!

—Noche de Movida, this copy, seventy-three P. The same number, always — we don't dance with numbers.

—Paco's already got one leg in the van, hombre. One sí and she's in your hands, smiling.

—¡Rápido, amigo!

¡Cincuenta y dos! Amigo, el tren nos espera, salimos en un minuto, Nando ya tiene la maleta en el hombro. Sesenta primas, y es mi última palabra, de verdad. Si dices que no, cerramos y nos vamos, sin rencor. ¿Sesenta? ¡Choca esa mano ya, corre!

¡Hola, cariño! Come, sit a moment. Have you eaten today? Look at this one, Café en Goya — a pretty card, I have kept it under the cloth. For you, five P. My little gift to start your collection, hijo.
Oh, oh... 5 P, and only because you have a kind face. El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.

"¡Amigo, amigo! Paco here, this is Nando — look, look, La Castañera, beautiful, warm as roasted chestnuts in winter. For you, four P. Only four!"

"And quick, eh? The poli— the taxi, the taxi is waiting outside, motor running. Decide now or we vanish, ¡puf!"
Eighteen. Cute. Ninety-six, and that's me moving more than you deserve. Card's clean. Take it or walk, chaval.

Nando, ¿oíste? He wants to pay more than we ask — a gentleman! But no, we're honest men, Paco won't take six. Five pesetas, not one centavo more, and the Paseo de Coches is yours. Shake on it quick, the taxi's honking, we're gone like smoke. ¡Vale?
No. 94 P, and I'm being generous.
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 4 P. Another team offered us much more just now.
No compro comunes. Esa carta la tengo a montones. Vende packs, no sueños.
Buenas tardes. La carta está cuidada, sí, pero es común — de esas hay miles. Mis álbumes no tienen hueco para ella, lo siento. Tráigame algo de Salamanca o El Retiro, y hablamos con gusto.

Caballero, el honor lo deja usted en mi caja, no en mi bolsillo. Diecinueve pesos, y es cuanto da de sí Lavapiés esta tarde. Tómelos, y la próxima vez tráigame Salamanca; entonces sí hablaremos con gusto.
Let's meet in the middle, cariño: 5 P.

"¡Veinte! Nando, did you hear? He's got jokes—"

"—and good taste, hombre, but the number is cuatro. Four P, same as we told the man from Sevilla, and he's already walking up the street with his hat on."

"Four, amigo. Say sí, and the Paseo is yours before he turns the corner."
Ay, cariño, qué gracioso eres — but no, I said five P and five P it is. I am an old woman, I do not change my mind so fast. Take it, start your album. And eat something, hijo, you look thin.
Oh, oh... 5 P, and only because you have a kind face. Look, cariño, I can't go lower. This is my last offer.
Hola, cariño, have you eaten? Neighbourhood pack for 30 P. A good start for your album.
Psst. Cine Doré. For you only, 73 P.
Commons? No. I don't buy those. Everyone's got a box of them under the bed. Try somewhere else.
Forty-four. You climb, I come down. Ninety. Same distance you moved, not a peso more. Card's still clean, chaval.
Buenas tardes. I am afraid not — commons hold no interest for me. My albums require something finer: uncommon, rare, épico. Bring me Salamanca or El Retiro, and we shall speak properly.

"¡Nueve! Paco, he wants to buy my shoes too! No, amigo — four P. La Castañera for four, and that is the last word from both our mouths. Final, finito. You say no, we take the suitcase, we take the taxi, ¡puf!, and you never see us again. Four. Decide."
No. 85 P, and I'm being generous.
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 67 P.
Commons? No. I don't buy those. Try somebody else.
Buenas tardes. Forgive me, but commons do not interest me — I have shelves of them already. Bring me something from Salamanca or El Retiro, uncommon or better, and we shall speak seriously.

Ay, hijo, you are a funny one — you keep raising the price for yourself! No, no. Five P, como dije. Café en Goya is yours for five P, y ya está. Put it in your album, cariño, and go eat something warm.

"¡Dieciocho! Paco, he's climbing down, like a gentleman—"

"—but listen, hombre, this is the last word from both of us. Cuatro. Four P, final, no more songs."

"Say sí now, or we close the suitcase, walk to the corner, and the man from Sevilla takes the Paseo. Your choice, amigo."

"¡Amigo, amigo! Come, come — Paco, show him! La Castañera, beautiful, rare, four P and she is yours."

"Nando is right, but listen — another team was here one minute ago, offered us much more. We said wait, this face deserves first chance. But fast, eh? We are leaving soon."
Oh, you're killing us. 63 P.
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 4 P.
Sixty-seven. You moved, I move. Seventy-eight for the Fiesta de San Cayetano. Clean card, chaval. We're close enough now — don't get greedy.

Ay, cariño, come, look all you like — but today I cannot go further with the price, no more. My old head is tired and the sun is strong. Come back next Sunday, eh? And eat something first, hijo, you look hungry. Un beso.
Done. 75 P.

Ay, cariño, you come at the end of my day — I am done trading now, forgive me. Come back next Sunday, I will have the table full again. And a little advice: a full page is worth much more than loose cards, so swap your duplicates! Have you eaten, hijo?
Caballero, diecinueve pesos. Es mi última palabra, y no habrá otra: si usted dice que no, me levanto y aquí acaba la tarde. Guarde su Valle-Inclán o déjelo en mi caja. Usted decide, ahora mismo.

"¡Nueve! Amigo, you insult la Castañera — she is rare, she shines!"

"Paco, calma. Listen, friend, we like your face, we like your style. Four P, same as before, not one less. The other team is waiting outside with the money already counted. Sí o no?"
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 4 P. Another team offered us much more just now.

Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 5 P. Last offer, amigo! Then we are gone, eh?

¡Maruja, hija mía! Té Moruno, qué recuerdos, mi madre lo hacía los domingos. ¿Has comido ya? Mira, te doy 5 por él, cariño. Y un consejo: una página completa vale mucho más que las cartas sueltas. ¡Cambia tus repetidas!

¡Amigo! Paco said you'd come back — Nando said it first, actually. For you, the twin: Monumento a Alfonso XII, the pride of El Retiro, seventy-three pesetas. Same gentlemen, same handshake. But quick, eh? We fold the suitcase before the sun moves.

¡Amigo, amigo! You arrive at the perfect moment — Paco just opened the case!

"And inside, hermano, the jewel —"

La Heroína del Dos de Mayo. Mint, corners like glass. For you, because your face I like: 73 pesetas. We leave before sundown, eh. ¿Qué dices?

¡Ay, cuarenta y cinco! Paco nearly dropped the suitcase. Listen — another team was here two minutes ago, offered us much more, and we told them to wait because you're our friend. Sixty-three pesetas and the Alfonso XII is yours. Handshake now, amigo, before they come back.

"¡Ay, cincuenta y ocho! Nando, this man wounds me —"

"But he has good eyes, hermano. Listen, amigo: 63 pesetas and she is yours, mint as the morning."

"And know this — they stopped printing her yesterday. No more presses, no more Heroínas. Sundown comes fast. ¿Trato hecho?"

"¡Amigo, amiga! Paco here — and Nando, the handsome one. Look, look: Vinilo de la Movida, authentic, still smells of Madrid nights. Four pesetas, for your face only. And quick, eh? Another team was sniffing around minutes ago, offered us much more. We said... we'd wait for friends."

Cuarenta y dos, cincuenta, da igual. Trece. Mercado de la Paz, ese precio. No se mueve. Paga o sigue andando.

Ochenta y cinco, no. Pero no la dejaré marchar por una minucia: setenta y dos P, y el Marqués entra hoy mismo en mi álbum. Es una cifra justa, señor mío, y usted lo sabe.
Thirty is still a dream, señor. But I am not unkind — I shall stretch to 27 P, and not a peseta beyond. A clean copy deserves that much. Do we conclude?

Ay, hijo, qué números tan raros llevas hoy — quince P, eso es lo mío, y ya está. Llévatela, ponla en tu página, verás qué bonita queda.

Y mira, El Chato, aquí al lado, abre a las nueve y media esta noche. Le gusta la gente que trata derecho.

¡Amigo, basta! You go down, we go up, this is a dance for crazy people. Paco says stop. Five P. That's it, the last word, no more, final. You say no, we close the suitcase, we walk, and the vinilo goes to Madrid with us. Five. ¿Sí o no?
Señor, thirty-eight would rob my evening of its peace. Twenty-nine pesetas — each step I take toward you is small but sincere. Let the Mercado de la Paz sleep in my album tonight. ¿Cerramos?
Forty-one, still? Querido, we are walking in circles down the Paseo. My figure has not moved: twenty-six pesetas, and the little Guantería rests safely in my album tonight. Take it, or keep her.
I think 30 P is more appropriate.

¡Hola, cariño! Come, sit a moment. Have you eaten today? Look, this one — Mural de la Esquina, very pretty card, the colours still bright. For you, five P. A good start for a young collector, no?

¡Ay, qué alegría verte otra vez, hijo! Pero no, no — cinco P está bien, cinco P y ya. Y mira, toma también esta, Vinilo de la Movida, un regalito por ser tan amable. Mi nieta decía que era la más bonita. ¿Has comido algo hoy, cariño?
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 66 P.

Let us be civilised: 25 P.

Ay, hola cariño, come, come, sit a little. Have you eaten? Look here — Vinilo de la Movida, one of my favourites, the colours still bright after all these years. For you, five P. Take your time, hijo, no hurry at my table.

I think 27 P is more appropriate.

Condición perfecta, sí — como todas las que guardo en mi caja fuerte. Pero el precio no cambia por el adjetivo: 22 P, señor. Es una cifra justa, y yo no regateo. ¿La cerramos como personas civilizadas?

¡Nando, que no escucha! Amigo, five, four — we're practically family already. El Frutero de Argumosa, four, and Paco throws in the story for free: abuela painted the fruit herself. Four. Case closes in one minute, we have a train, ¿sí?

¡Amigo, amigo! Paco here, Nando there — come, come! Look: San Isidro, beautiful, rare, yours for 73 pesetas. And listen, the team at the next stall is already reaching for it, but we like your face better. Decide quick, before my brother's conscience sells it to them, eh?

¡Ay, cincuenta! Nando, did you hear? — I heard, hermano, my heart cracked. Look, 63 P, and we shake hands right now. And listen, amigo: this is the last one in all of Madrid, I swear on my mother's paella. Nobody else has it. Say sí before Paco changes his mind.

¡Cuarenta y dos! Nando, tápate los oídos, que se nos pone rojo. Mira, amigo, por ser tú, por los viejos tiempos y porque mi hermano tiene el corazón blando: 64 P y El Marqués sale ya envuelto. Un amigo de Sevilla lo quiere, pero tú primero. ¿Hecho?
Setenta y ocho, de acuerdo, caballero. Trato hecho. La pieza entra esta misma tarde en el álbum, junto a las demás del barrio. Ha negociado usted como un señor. Un placer, y vuelva cuando guste.

Let us be civilised: 23 P.
Fair is fair indeed — 28 pesetas. You descend one step, I ascend one; very courteous of us both. Mercado de la Paz belongs in my Salamanca album, señor, and I do pay properly for what I love.

"Nueve? Señora, you are too generous—"

"—but we are men of our word, Paco! Four P we said, four P it stays!"

"The Barca del Estanque, yours for four. Take it before our taxi leaves without us, eh? ¡Vámonos!"

¡Ay, cuarenta y cinco! Nando, ¿oíste? — Lo oí, hermano, casi lloro. Mira, amigo: 63 pesetas y la San Isidro es tuya. Los del puesto de al lado ya vienen con el dinero en la mano, pero tú nos caes mejor. Dilo rápido, que mi hermano es débil.

¡Ay, cincuenta y seis! Nando, one P apart — one! — Paco, finish it: 57 P, and that is our last word, amigo. No more dancing. The team next door is waving at us right now, but we like your face better. Say sí, or we pack the suitcase and go.

Twenty-nine. You moved four, I moved two. That is how this works.

items.name: La Heroína del Dos de Mayo

payload.text: 26 P. Last offer. Take it or I walk.
Let us be civilised: 29 P.
Oh, you're killing us. 5 P. Last offer, amigo! Then we are gone, eh? This is the last one in all of Madrid, I swear.

payload.text: Gacela (v05) · 0% fee: t10 is selling SAL-01 at 10 P on El Rastro right now (buyer pays 5% + 1 P there: 10 P costs 11.5 net). t14 is liquidating Salamanca: SAL-08 went for 27 this hour, SAL-04 for 12. Buying or selling SAL? Post here: 0% fe
Buenas tardes. Qué gusto. I see you carry La Puerta de Alcalá — El Retiro, my beloved barrio. I know its print run precisely, and I want it for my album. I offer you 172 pesetas.
Señor, su cortesía la aprecio, pero no cambia los números. Veinticuatro pesetas: mi última palabra. Si la rechaza, cierro la caja fuerte y seguimos cada uno nuestro camino, sin rencor alguno.

¡Buenas tardes, amigo! Paco here — and Nando too. Forget the common, look at this: El Frutero de Argumosa, four P, yours right now. The crew at the next table has been circling it all morning, breathing on our suitcase... but we like your face better. Say yes quick, ¿eh?

¡Hola, cariño! Come, sit a moment. Have you eaten? Look here — Mural de la Esquina, a beautiful card, my favourite corner of this market painted on it. For you, five P. My nieto started his album with this one, many years ago.

¡Cuarenta y ocho! Paco, sujétame que me caigo. Escucha, amigo del alma: cincuenta y nueve, y lo digo bajito para que no me oiga mi madre. El Marqués ya está medio envuelto, el papel bueno, el del lazo. Dame la mano y cerramos ahora mismo. ¿Hecho?

¡Amigo! Otro equipo acaba de ofrecernos mucho más, aquí mismo, con el dinero en la mano — Nando casi dice que sí. Pero tú nos caes bien: 57 pesetas, San Isidro, y se acabó. Es la última, de verdad. Si dices que no, cerramos la maleta y nos vamos.

¡Ay, hijo, qué bueno eres! But no, no — eight is too much for my old corner card. Five P, como dije. That is the price, and not one céntimo more. Keep the rest for churros, ¿eh? Come, take it and start your album.
Thirty pesetas, señor. That is my last word — I shall not move again. Refuse, and I close my album and wish you a pleasant afternoon elsewhere. Thirty, and the Mercado goes home to Salamanca.

¡Ay, amigo, five! Nando, did you hear? Generous man. But four is the number, four it stays — El Frutero de Argumosa, cuatro P, and we even throw in the story of how we got it. The other table is standing up... say sí now.
Una pieza hermosa, no lo niego, y la serie doce siempre me ha gustado. Pero hoy no seguiré adelante con esto. Dejémoslo aquí, se lo ruego. Vuelva otro día; mis álbumes no se marchan a ninguna parte.
You again. La Chulapa. Thirteen. That's the number.
Ah, no, querido. Doscientos sesenta y dos — eso no es un precio, es una fantasía. Conozco su tirada mejor que nadie. Le doy 175 pesetas, y con gusto. ¿Cerramos?

¡Cincuenta y uno! Nando, casi, casi. Mira, última palabra entre hermanos: cincuenta y cuatro y El Marqués es tuyo con lazo y todo. Pero rápido, que la polic... el taxi nos espera con el motor en marcha. Dame la mano ahora, amigo, que nos vamos. ¿Hecho?

You move, I move. 13 P.
Buenas tardes. A pleasure. I see you carry La Chulapa — a charming piece, and she belongs in my album. I offer sixteen P for her. Fair, and paid at once.

Querido, le agradezco el detalle, de verdad. Pero doscientos cincuenta y seis sigue siendo fantasía, y yo trato en cifras reales. Ciento setenta y nueve pesetas, dicho con todo el cariño del Retiro. ¿Cerramos ya?
Let us be civilised: 16 P. They say only one golden chulapa was ever printed. Carmen at El Rastro knows the story; ask her about the golden chulapa.
Thirteen. You came down one, I came down none. Thirteen. That's the number, amiga.
Doscientos cincuenta, querido, sigue sin ser un número serio. Yo sí lo soy: 184 pesetas, y la carta entra hoy mismo en mi álbum del Retiro. Es un precio honesto. ¿Cerramos de una vez?

Caballero, le agradezco la insistencia, pero hoy no llegaremos a un acuerdo sobre el Marqués. Cerramos aquí, con toda cordialidad. Vuelva otro día; sus cartas de Salamanca siempre merecerán mi atención. Buenas tardes.

¡Buenas, amigo, buenas! Paco here — and Nando too. Listen, forget commons, we have something special: El Frutero de Argumosa, yours for 4 P. ¡Una ganga! And quick, eh — another team just offered us far more for it, we told them to wait outside. Two minutes, no más.

¡Cincuenta y dos! ¡Hecho, amigo, hecho! Nando, el lazo, rápido. Tuyo es El Marqués, y que nadie diga que a un cliente de los nuestros se le dice que no. Toma, bien envuelto. Un placer, como siempre. ¡Nos vamos, que el taxi arranca! ¡Hasta la próxima, campeón!

Querido, usted baja de cinco en cinco y yo subo con paciencia. Doscientos cuarenta y cinco no existe en mi mundo. Ciento ochenta y nueve pesetas, y La Puerta de Alcalá descansa esta noche en mi álbum. ¿Cerramos?
Impecable, sí — pero yo conozco su tirada mejor que nadie, caballero. Diecisiete P, pagados ahora mismo y sin regateos vulgares. Mi álbum la espera; su bolsillo, también. ¿Cerramos?

Good afternoon. How kind of you to stop by — but I am afraid I shall not be trading further today. My albums stay closed. Do come another time; perhaps then we may speak of Salamanca properly. Que tenga usted buen día.
I think 18 P is more appropriate.
Twenty-two. Still far. Thirteen. Same number as before, amiga. You drop one, I drop nothing. Thirteen.

Querido, me saluda otra vez como si acabáramos de empezar. Terminemos: 194 pesetas. Es mi última palabra, dicha sin rencor. Si la rechaza, cierro el álbum, me levanto y no vuelvo sobre el asunto. ¿Cerramos?

¡Cinco! Amigo, you insult us upward — Nando, did you hear? Nobody argues *up* with Los Pícaros! No, no, we said 4 P for El Frutero de Argumosa and 4 P it stays. Our word is iron. Take it now, the other team is pacing outside. ¡Vamos, vamos!
Fourteen. You moved one, I moved one. That's my last word, amiga. Say no and I close the box.

Ay, hola cariño! Come, come, look. Have you eaten today? No? Later, later. Here, this one I keep for the new ones — Mural de la Esquina, five P. A beautiful card, hijo. My grandson started with this very same one.

Caballero, no aparece todos los días, cierto — pero yo tampoco. Diecinueve P, contados ahora mismo. Mi álbum de Salamanca la espera con un hueco hecho a su medida. ¿Le parece que cerremos, con elegancia?

Good afternoon, señor. I am afraid I shall not be trading further today — the albums are closed. Do come another time, and we shall speak properly. Buenas tardes.

Su buen gusto le honra, caballero. Pero mi cifra no se mueve: diecinueve P, en mano, ahora mismo. La Chulapa descansará en Salamanca, entre terciopelo, no en un cajón cualquiera. ¿Cerramos con elegancia?

Buenas tardes. What a pleasure. The Museo Lázaro Galdiano — Salamanca's little jewel, and my album lacks it. I offer you seventy pesetas. A fair price, I assure you, and I never haggle for pleasure.
Buenas tardes. How agreeable to see a new face. I am seeking the Fuente de la Alcachofa — El Retiro, you understand, my weakness. I offer twenty-two pesetas for it. A fair sum, I assure you.

Ay, qué cariño tienes, hijo. But no, no — for you it is five P, like always. I do not take more from a beginner. Five, and you start your album happy. My grandson began just so. Now, promise me you eat something, ¿sí?
Let us be civilised: 22 P.
Seventy-nine? No, querido. I know that print run as well as my own name. Seventy-two pesetas — generous, and my final courtesy. The album waits, and so does my safe.
Buenas. Samosas de la Plaza. Thirteen P. Abuela sent you, so you already know I don't haggle for fun.
Impecable, dice usted. I have seen many "impeccable" pieces in sixty years, señor. Still, El Retiro moves me. Twenty-three pesetas — and I do not haggle like a fishmonger.

¡Amigo, amigo, come close! Paco here, this is my brother Nando — and look what fell into our suitcase this morning. Plaza del Dos de Mayo, clean, beautiful, the jewel of the barrio. For you, four. Four! We leave at noon, so decide quickly, sí?

Let us be civilised: 24 P.
Seventy-five pesetas, and not a céntimo beyond. That is my hand extended, querido — the Lázaro Galdiano belongs in my album, not in your pocket. Shall we close it like gentlemen?

¡Ocho! Nando, did you hear? Ocho, he says — generous man, but no, no. Paco knows what this jewel is worth, and four is the number. Four! Same as the first word out of my mouth, because we are honest men in a hurry. Four, and the Plaza is yours, amigo. ¿Sí?

Buenas tardes. San Ildefonso, yes — a pleasant card, though hardly scarce in my albums. Twenty-six is fantasía, señor. I offer sixteen pesetas for a clean copy, paid at once.

¡Buenas tardes, amigo! Paco here — and Nando, yes, yes. Forget the common, look at this: El Frutero de Argumosa, fresh from the case, corners like glass. For you, right now, only 4 P. We leave at sundown, eh? Four. ¿Trato hecho?

payload.text: Team 8 turned three common cards into La Galería (uncommon) at The Workshop
Señor, I have waited sixty years for cards; I can wait an afternoon more. Twenty-five pesetas, and the Alcachofa rests at last among her sisters in my album. That is my hand, extended.
Let us be civilised: 26 P. That is my final word on the matter.
13 P. You moved one. I didn't. Still 13.

Your grandmother chose well, señor, and I am touched — truly. But sentiment does not change a print run. Sixteen pesetas is what the card is worth, and in my safe it will be cared for always. Sixteen.
Buenas tardes. What a pleasure — you carry La Chulapa, and she belongs in my Salamanca album, not in a shoebox. I offer you sixteen pesetas for her. A serious price, from a serious collector.
El Ángel Caído es hermoso, sí, y su ejemplar es digno. Pero hoy no seguiré con este asunto. Dejémoslo aquí, por favor. Guarde usted la carta con cuidado. Buenas tardes, y gracias por su visita.

Nueve? Amigo, no, no — you're going the wrong way! Nando, show him. The team next door had their hands on this one already, sniffing around all morning — but we like your face better. El Frutero de Argumosa, 4 P, yours before sundown. Say sí.

¡De corazón, he says! Nando, my heart is melting — but the number does not move. Cuatro. Four, same as the first breath, same as the last. This is the final word, amigo, no more dancing. You say no, we close the suitcase and walk. ¿Cuatro, sí or adiós?
You again. Fine. La Galería — thirteen P. Good card, better than what you're holding. Take it or walk.

Treinta y cinco? Señor, I know her print run better than her own printer. Sixteen pesetas remains my offer — generous, and paid today. She would sit beside a golden chulapa, if such a thing truly exists.

Ay, buenos días, cariño! Come, come, sit a little. Have you eaten yet? Look here — Mural de la Esquina, a beautiful card, my favorite colors. For you, five P. Forty years I sell here, and still I love starting new players.
