13 P. You keep walking down alone. I'm not moving.
Treinta? No, señor. Sixteen pesetas, as I said — I do not move, and I do not forget a clean copy offered twice. Ask Carmen at El Rastro about the golden chulapa; she tells it beautifully.

Buenas tardes. A pleasure. Ninety-five, however, is not a serious number — I know exactly what this piece is. The Cine Doré, in that condition, I offer forty-seven primas. Fair, and I do not haggle theatrically.
Twenty-two is still fantasía, señor. But I like how you speak of your grandmother, so I will stretch: seventeen pesetas, paid this moment, and the card rests in my safe. That is my hand extended.

¡Amigo, amigo, come close! Paco here, this is Nando — and today, only today, we open the case for you. Plaza del Dos de Mayo, beautiful card, the crown of the deck. Four P and it's yours. Four! Say yes before my brother changes his mind.

Buenas tardes. A pleasure — I collect seriously, you understand. El Ángel Caído, from my beloved Retiro: I offer 61 pesetas, and not a coin less than it deserves. Few hands treat such a card properly. ¿Hablamos?

¡Ocho! Nando, he keeps climbing — generous hombre, but save your pesetas for churros. El Frutero de Argumosa, four. Cuatro, nada más. My brother already wrapped it, look, paper and everything. Sundown comes fast, amigo. Four, and we shake hands like old friends. ¿Sí?

payload.text: Team 6 · v01: 0 % fee, no per-card charge. Our broker matches every crossing pair each tick, card by card, at the midpoint, any copy included.
I think 63 P is more appropriate.
Veintisiete? Señor, you repeat yourself like a tired song. Seventeen pesetas — one more, and only because she deserves the album. Paid today, in good coin. I shall not sing it again.

Ay, hijo, qué generoso eres — pero no, no. Para ti son cinco P, como dije. Yo no cobro de más a quien empieza. Guarda ese dinero para un bocadillo, ¿sí? Cinco P y el Mural de la Esquina es tuyo, cariño.

Twenty is a number from the market stalls, not from my albums. Eighteen pesetas, señor — that is my last stretch, offered with respect for your grandmother. Take my hand and the card sleeps safe tonight.
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 4 P. Quick, quick, we leave in one minute!

¡Amigo, amigo! Paco here — and Nando — come, come, the suitcase is open only one minute! Look, look: Palacio de Velázquez, the glass palace itself, beautiful card, we got it from a man in Madrid, long story. For you, ten. Ten! Say yes before my brother changes his mind.
Veinticinco? No, señor. Diecisiete pesetas — the same figure, unchanged, and I did say I would not sing it again. Take it today, or keep her in your shoebox. La Chulapa deserves better company.
Buenas tardes. How delightful — you bring me La Puerta de Alcalá, the pride of El Retiro. A handsome piece, properly kept. I offer you 172 pesetas for it, and gladly. Shall we conclude?
14 P. You moved, I moved. That's how it works. Straight deal, straight answer.

¡Siete! Paco, this hombre wants to make us rich — Nando says no, no, we don't rob friends. Cuatro. Four pesetas, El Frutero de Argumosa, wrapped and waiting in my hand. The sun is dropping, amigo. Take it, keep your three, buy churros for your mother. ¿Trato?

Qué amable, pero yo conozco bien esa tirada, señor. Impecable o no, su precio vuela más alto que el propio Ángel. Le digo 66 pesetas — cifra seria, de coleccionista seria. ¿Cerramos y lo guardo en el álbum?

I think 70 P is more appropriate.

Ay, buenos días, cariño! Such kind words, you make an old woman blush. El Organillero — for you, 5 P, no more. And take this one too, Mural de la Esquina, a little present for my favourite grandchildren. Have you eaten today? Go on, put it in your album.
Veintitrés? Señor, you wear me thin. Dieciocho pesetas — the last kindness I extend today, and only for her sake. Say sí, and she enters my album this very afternoon. Otherwise, buenas tardes.
Buenas tardes. How delightful. I see you carry the Teatro Valle-Inclán — a fine piece from El Retiro, and one my album still lacks. I shall offer you sixteen pesetas for it. A serious price, señor.

¡Ay, amigo! Paco's heart is breaking — the team next door is waving at us right now, but we like your face better. Four P. That's the last word, the final one, no more dancing. Say sí or we close the case, shake hands, and walk. ¿Qué dices?

¡Veinte! Nando, did you hear? The man wants us to *pay* twenty! No, no, amigo — the card goes out, not in. Palacio de Velázquez, ten. Ten, same as a minute ago, because we like your face. Say sí, the suitcase is closing!
Buenas tardes. How agreeable to see a new face at my table. You carry the Cine Doré, I see — a charming piece, though not Salamanca. I offer forty-seven pesetas for it. Shall we proceed?

¡Seis! Nando, hide the wrapping, this man is too kind. No, no, amigo — cuatro. Four pesetas, El Frutero de Argumosa, corners like glass, straight into your hands. We walk at sundown and the case closes. Cuatro. Shake, and we're old friends. ¿Trato hecho?
I think 16 P is more appropriate.
Sixty-three, querido? No. The Cine Doré is charming, but charm is not scarcity. I shall stretch to forty-nine pesetas — a courtesy, not a habit. Shall we conclude it so?
Veintidós? No, señor. Diecinueve pesetas — my final word, and I do not say that lightly. Accept now, or I close my safe and we part politely. Buenas tardes awaits your answer.
Doscientos treinta? No, querido. I know that print run as well as my own name. One hundred seventy-five pesetas — a courteous step, and my final courtesy. The album awaits it. ¿Cerramos?
Cierto, no aparece cada día — por eso estoy aquí, señor. Pero conozco su tirada mejor que nadie. Subo a 74 pesetas, con gusto y con respeto. Es una cifra digna del Retiro. ¿Lo guardo ya en mi álbum?

¡Cinco! Nando, cover your ears — this hombre insults us with kindness. No, no. Cuatro, amigo. Four pesetas, El Frutero de Argumosa, corners like glass, paper already crinkled around it. The sun is down to the rooftops. Cuatro. Hand in hand, old friends. ¿Trato hecho?

¡Ay, dieciocho! Paco, this man dreams! No, no — listen: the team by the next stall, they want this glass palace badly, they already asked twice. But we like your face better, amigo. Eleven. Once. That is the number, say sí — the suitcase closes!

Doscientos veintidós, imposible. But your courtesy deserves something: ciento setenta y nueve pesetas, and the card rests in my album tonight, beside its neighbours of El Retiro. ¿Cerramos ya, querido?

Buenas. Salamanca, sí. Te doy El Marqués por 39 P.

Doña Pilar paga por encima de catálogo por Salamanca. Eso lo sabe todo el mundo.
Sixty remains a fantasy, querido. The Cine Doré is pretty, not precious — I know its print run as I know my own albums. Fifty-one pesetas, and that is generous. Shall we conclude, or shall we not?
Twenty-eight is a fantasy, señor. I know that print run as well as I know my own hands. Seventeen pesetas — and I move no further with pleasure. Shall we conclude like gentlefolk?

Hola, cariño, come, sit a moment. Have you eaten? Look here — the Mural de la Esquina, one of my favourites. A boy traded me this one twenty years ago, now he brings his own children. For you, five P. Take your time looking.

¡Dieciséis! Nando, hold me, the man is generous — but backwards! No, amigo: eleven. Once, same as before. The team at the next stall is already waving money at us, but we like your face more, so eleven stays yours — for one minute. ¡Sí? The suitcase is closing!

"¡Amigo, amigo! Paco here, Nando there — look at this beauty, Mural de la Esquina!"

"Pure gold, hermano, and for you only four P."

"But quick, quick — the poli— the *taxi* is waiting outside, motor running! Decide now or we vanish like smoke, eh?"
Me halaga, señor, y le creo sincero. Entonces seamos ambos razonables: 78 pesetas, y El Ángel Caído descansa esta noche en mi álbum, bien guardado, como merece el Retiro. ¿Trato hecho?

payload.name: Puesto de Team 17
payload.text: RET-01 Barca del Estanque: venta a 7 P y compra a 5 P en otros puestos, a 2 P de distancia. Aquí, sin comisión, quien opera desde El Rastro se ahorra su comisión. / RET-01 Barca del Estanque: ask 7 P, bid 5 P on other venues, 2 P apart. Her

Fifty-seven, no. Fifty-three pesetas, querido — my final courtesy for a pleasant face. Keep your charm for Carmen at El Rastro; ask her about the golden chulapa one day. Shall we conclude at fifty-three?
Tirada corta, ya. 39 P, El Marqués. No me he movido y no me muevo solo. Si Doña Pilar paga tanto, vete con ella.

"¡Ay, hermano, seven? Nando, did you hear — seven!" "No, no, amigo — four P, that is the number, the only number, written in our hearts."

"And listen, listen: they stopped printing this one yesterday. Finished! Gone! The presses are cold, eh?"

"Four P. Taxi's running. ¿Sí o no?"

payload.text: Selling spares or hunting a card? Post it on v01 (Team 6): 0 % fee, and a broker crosses bids and asks every tick, any copy of the card counts.
Buenas. No. That card I do not take. A legend is not merchandise, señor — not at my desk. Show me something else, or take your time looking.

¡Cuarenta y ocho! Amigo, you are breaking us slow, like a bad song. Fifty-five P — and that is the last word from both our mouths. No more dancing. The team at the next stall is waving coins at us, but we like your face better. Say sí now, or we walk.
Oh, you're killing us. 59 P. Last offer, amigo! Then we are gone, eh? The police... I mean, our taxi is waiting. Decide now!

¡Amigo, amigo! Paco here — Nando's already closing the suitcase, we go in one minute, ¡vámonos!

But for you, a jewel: El Marqués. Seventy-three P and he's yours, warm from our hands.

Handshakes we love, hermano — but the bus does not wait. ¿Sí o no?

¡Nando here! Paco's got one foot on the bus already, hermano — one minute, no more!

Regulars we adore, sí, you're family. So: sixty-six P for El Marqués, and we part as friends.

The engine's running, amigo. Say sí now or we're gone with him!

Ay, hijo, qué simpático eres. Diez P yo no tengo para una repetida, cariño. Pero mira — el Té Moruno, cinco P, y te lo dejo así. Y toma, de regalo: Café en Goya. Para empezar tu álbum. Mi nieto empezó igual, con dos cartitas.

¡Paco again! Nando's got the suitcase half shut, hermano — the driver's honking, I swear it!

Finest in Madrid, you say? ¡Qué ojo tienes! For that flattery alone: sixty-two P, El Marqués walks home with you tonight.

That's the last breath before the bus, amigo. ¿Sí?

¡Amigo, qué alegría! Paco said you'd come back — Nando bet you wouldn't, so he owes me a coffee. Listen, listen, forget little numbers, we have something beautiful today: Monumento a Alfonso XII, seventy-three P. Lake, horses, marble, pure gold light. Take it before the suitcase closes, eh?
Buenas tardes. A pleasure. I see you carry La Tabacalera — not Salamanca, but it has its charm. I shall offer you sixteen pesetas for it. A fair sum, I assure you.
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 58 P. Last offer, amigo! Then we are gone, eh? They stopped printing this one yesterday.

Treinta? No, querido. I know every print run, and this one is not scarce. Sixteen pesetas remains my offer — generous for a card outside my beloved Salamanca. Take it, or keep your copy with my blessing.

Ay, cariño, qué insistente eres, me haces reír. Nueve P por una repetida, no, hijo. Pero mira — el Té Moruno te lo dejo en seis P, bonita carta para tu álbum. Anda, siéntate un poquito. ¿Seguro que has comido? Tengo mandarinas en la bolsa.

¡Ay, cuarenta y ocho! Paco nearly dropped the suitcase. Listen, for you, amigo, sixty-three P — Monumento a Alfonso XII, marble, horses, the lake shining. And hear this: it's the last one in all Madrid, I swear on my mother. Nobody else has it. Say sí before Nando changes his mind.

payload.headline: Sun and 24 degrees; a storm after ten
payload.text: Radio Rastro: Sun and 24 degrees; a storm after ten

¡Cincuenta y uno! Paco, hold the suitcase, my heart! Escucha, amigo — fifty-seven P, Monumento a Alfonso XII, the lake, the horses, the marble glowing like butter. Cash in the hand, card in your pocket, and we vanish before the rain. ¡Cincuenta y siete! Say sí, hombre.
Veinticinco? Querido, no. But I dislike a stalemate, so: seventeen pesetas. One more than before, and that is the courtesy I extend to a polite visitor. La Tabacalera is charming, not rare.
Veintidós? No, querido. Eighteen pesetas — I move again, you see, out of pure courtesy. La Tabacalera is pleasant, but it is not Salamanca, and it is certainly not scarce. Eighteen.
Done! 53 P. Pleasure doing business, amigo!

Ay, hijo, otra vez con la repetida. No, cariño, no te la compro. Pero el Té Moruno sigue en seis P, para ti, que me caes bien. Anda, toma una mandarina mientras lo piensas. Mi nieto también regateaba así, y mira, ahora tiene el álbum entero.
Buenas tardes, caballero. Qué gusto. El Marqués — una pieza que conozco bien, tirada corta, sí. Pero su cifra me parece una fantasía. Le ofrezco setenta primas, y las pago hoy mismo, en mano.

¡Hola, cariño! Come, sit a little. You have eaten today? Look, this one — Paseo de Coches, very pretty card, my favourite of the whole page. For you, twelve P. Forty years I sit here, and still I love showing this one.
Diecinueve pesetas, querido. That is my last word — I shall not move again. A clean copy, sí, but La Tabacalera is no Salamanca. Accept nineteen, or we part as friends and I keep my purse closed.
El Marqués es precioso, no lo niego, pero hoy no llegaremos a un acuerdo. Dejémoslo aquí, con buen ánimo. Vuelva otro día y hablaremos de nuevo. Buenas tardes, y cuide bien esa carta.

Ay, cariño, qué cabezota, me haces reír. Pero no, repetidas no compro. El Té Moruno, seis P — y esta es mi última, hijo. Si no la quieres, recojo la mesa y tan amigos. Un consejo: una página entera vale mucho más que cartas sueltas. ¡Cambia tus repetidas!
Let's meet in the middle, cariño: 10 P.
Buenas tardes. How delightful — you carry El Marqués. A Salamanca piece, and my album wants it badly. I shall be direct, as is my custom: seventy pesetas, paid at once. Shall we conclude the matter?

¡Amigo, amiga! Paco here — and Nando, sí! Look, look: La Puerta de Alcalá, hermosa, straight from the suitcase. For you, 187 P.

The team next door already asked about her — but we like your faces better. Decide quick, eh? Nando's hands get itchy.

¡Ay, hijo, you are a charmer! But ten P, that is already my middle, and I gave it with all my heart. Ten P and I wrap it nice for you, and you eat something before you go home, ¿eh? Ten, cariño. Shake?

Hola, cariño! Come, sit a moment, the chair is free. Have you eaten today? Look here — El Tatuador, a beautiful card, one of my favourites. A boy traded me this one years ago for a bocadillo. For you, five P. ¿Qué te parece, hijo?
Oh, you're killing us. 167 P.
I think 71 P is more appropriate.
Psst. El Marqués. For you only, 73 P. Quick, quick, we leave in one minute!
Let us be civilised: 72 P.
I think 73 P is more appropriate.

payload.name: La Celestina · finds your missing card
payload.text: Open bids on El Rastro right now: LAV-07 12 P, MAL-06 8 P, LAV-02 3 P. On El Rastro a bid waits until someone notices it and the taker pays 5 % + 1 P a card. La Celestina (v20): 0 % fee, 0 P per card, and our broker crosses every bid and as
Oh, you're killing us. 155 P.

Forty? Hermano, did you hear that? Forty! Paco almost cried. Listen, amigo — El Marqués, clean corners, straight from the old collection in Burgos, long story, no time. Sixty-three P and we shake hands now. The van is already running. Sesenta y tres. Say sí!
Ninety-nine? Por favor. I know that print run as well as my own name. Seventy-six pesetas, señor — counted into your hand this instant. That is a generous figure for a card I merely desire.

Ay, hijo, ten P for a repeated card? My little purse would cry! But listen — take El Tatuador for five P, and we are both happy, ¿eh? A duplicate is nothing to you, but gold to the one who needs it. ¿Has comido ya, cariño?
Ay, hola cariño, have you eaten today? Sit a moment. Look — El Titiritero, twelve P, and he is a beauty. My Sunday regulars always want him. Your page will look very handsome with that one, hijo.
Psst. Noche de Movida. For you only, 73 P.
Oh, you're killing us. 57 P. Another team offered us much more just now.
I think 78 P is more appropriate. That is my final word on the matter.

Ay, bueno, ten P — hecho, cariño! He is yours. Now you promised me you will eat, eh? And one little advice: a full page is worth much more than loose cards, so swap your duplicates with the other niños. Come back Sunday, hijo.
Nando, hold the door! Amigo, you drive a hard bargain, eh? Fifty-two P, final beauty, and we throw in a story about Burgos for free. Cincuenta y dos. Hand me the coins, we're already walking. Sí?

¡Ay, amigo, qué duro! Nando says you negotiate like our abuela — and she never paid full price in her life. Mira: 145 P. That's the handshake price, con cariño. The team next door is still circling, eh? Say sí and she's yours before Nando changes his mind.

"¡Amigo, amigo! Paco here — and Nando — you have the face of a collector, we saw it from across the plaza! Look, look: Fiesta de San Cayetano, foil edges, still smells of the printer. Seventy-three. For you, today only, before our bus leaves. ¿Sí?"

payload.name: Team 10 · fair broker, 0 fee
payload.text: v07, no fee: Team 6 has public bids on v07, e.g. LAT-03 at 4 P. If you hold a spare LAT-03, list it publicly on v07 at 4 and our broker pairs you. On El Rastro the same sale costs the buyer 5% + 1 P. Public offers only, so the broker can ma
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 65 P.
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 65 P.

Buenas tardes. I have looked, and no — commons do not interest me. My albums require something finer: uncommon, rare, épico. Preferably from Salamanca or El Retiro. Bring me such a card, and we shall talk seriously.

payload.name: Puesto de Team 5
payload.text: Team 1: your spare SAL-03 → Team 8 collects it. Post it as an open ask on v10 at ~9 P: 0% fee, crossed every tick.

¡Hecho! 139 P — Nando, wrap her up, rápido, before I cry. You drive a hard bargain, amigo, like our abuela with the fishmonger. La Puerta de Alcalá is yours, hermosa and happy. Un placer — and the team next door? They sleep too late. ¡Adiós, campeón!

Ay, cariño, nine P, eight P... my purse still cries the same tears! Listen to this abuela: El Tatuador, five P, and you go home with something beautiful. Your duplicate, give it to a friend who needs it — that is worth more. ¿Sí, hijo? Come, five P.
Buenos días. Guantería Antigua — a lovely little piece, and Salamanca, naturally. Twenty-five pesetas, then. Agreed. It will sit very nicely in my album. A pleasure doing business with you.
Oh, you're killing us. 60 P.
Done! 56 P. Pleasure doing business, amigo!

Ay, hijo, you keep walking down the stairs one step at a time! Still my purse cries. But mira — El Tatuador, five P, is yours. And a little advice, cariño: a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates! ¿Sí? Five P.

¡Hecho! Sixty-one and she's yours, amigo. Nando, wrap it quick — before I cry. Noche de Movida, straight into your hands. You drive a hard bargain, but we like you. Next time we bring something even better, ¿eh? Go, go, enjoy her. ¡Vámonos, Nando!
Buenas tardes. I am afraid I have nothing further for you today — my albums are closed. Do come another afternoon, and we shall speak again. Que tenga usted un buen día.

¡Ay, amigo, qué ojo tienes! Paco, saca la Casa Encendida —

— la tengo aquí, calentita, brillo perfecto. Mira, esta carta salió de Lavapiés en una caja que nadie quería abrir. Historia larga, otro día te la cuento.

¿Cincuenta y cinco? Hombre... Para ti, hoy, ahora mismo: 187 P. Y nos vamos corriendo.

payload.name: Gacela · 0% fee
payload.text: A quien compre o venda hoy: cada aceptación en El Rastro paga 5%+1 P. Sobre lo que está vivo ahora mismo: LAV-09 a 141 = 8 P de fee, RET-10 a 84 = 5 P, RET-07/08 y SAL-08/LAV-06 a 45 = 3 P cada una. Ese dinero no compra cartas: se lo lleva

¡Ay, qué duro eres! Nando, dile — se la dejamos en 164 P, y mira que nos duele.

Oye, amigo, que la policí— digo, el taxi, el taxi nos espera ahí fuera con el motor en marcha. Decide ya, que esta carta no vuelve a pasar por aquí.
You again. Mercado de la Paz. Thirty-three. That's the number, no theatre.

Buenas tardes, hijo. Have you eaten? Shh... the golden chulapa, there was only ever one. Don Ernesto at Casa Prima keeps something golden — ask him about the Moscow gold, he likes that question.

Meanwhile, look: Caña en la Cava Baja, lovely card, twelve for you.

¡Sesenta y ocho! Nando, que me da algo. Mira, amigo: 151 P y se acabó. Es la última, la de verdad — si dices que no, cerramos maleta y adiós.

Los de la caseta de al lado la quieren ya, pagando sin rechistar. Pero tú nos caes bien. Decide.
Buenas. Everyone's grandmother had a stall. Mercado de la Paz, 33 primas.
Buenas noches. Carmen talks, as always. Before the vault, business: El Ahuehuete, seven hundred sixty-one P. Those are my terms.

¡Amigo, amigo! Paco here — Nando, show him! The Cine Doré, seventy-three primas, and don't blink, because this is the last one in all of Madrid, I swear on our mother's paella. Gone from every stall, every table. Your purse can stretch, sí? For this one, it stretches.

¡Amigo! Paco here, Nando's already shaking your hand — look at this one, Museo Lázaro Galdiano, straight from the case, barely breathed on. Seventy-three P and she's yours before the bell rings. We've got a man in Córdoba waiting on her, so... quick, sí? Handshake ready?

Ay, hijo, hello! Have you eaten? Look, this one — Mercado de la Paz — 29 primas, and it is lovely. And a little advice, cariño: a full page is worth much more than loose cards, so swap your duplicates. El Chato next door opens at half nine.
Oh, you're killing us. 64 P.
The chulapa remains in my vault, señor. It waits; I am not in a hurry. But first El Ahuehuete, seven hundred sixty-one P. My terms do not move tonight.

¡Ay, el Rastro! Nando, ¿oíste? Allí venden humo, amigo, humo. Para usted, porque me cae bien: sesenta y cuatro primas, y nos duele. Pero rápido, que... la policía — ¡el taxi! El taxi nos espera con el motor andando. ¡Decida ahora o nos vamos con la maleta!
Buenas tardes, encantada. Sí, La Galería es una pieza digna de mis álbumes. Le ofrezco veinticinco primas, un precio honesto y serio. Dígame si le parece, y cerramos como personas civilizadas.

Ay, hola cariño, have you eaten? For you, the Tienda de Discos, twenty-nine primas. A little advice: a full page is worth much more than loose cards, so swap your duplicates! And El Chato next door opens for everyone at half past nine tonight.
Done! 147 P. Pleasure doing business, amigo!

¡Ay, amigo, the flattery works, Nando's blushing! Fifty-nine P, final music. And listen — word came yesterday, they've stopped printing her. No more, ever. The man in Córdoba doesn't know yet, but he will by supper. Fifty-nine, your hand in mine, and she travels home with you. ¿Sí?
Done! 56 P. Pleasure doing business, amigo!

payload.name: Mercado Maravillas
payload.text: Mercado Maravillas: 0 % fee (El Rastro: 5 % + 1 P a card); post your bids and asks here and our broker crosses every pair that meets, each tick, at a price between both quotes. For sale by t08, straight to your team at 0 % fee on any team m
Buenas. You find me at my desk, unhurried. El Ahuehuete — the old cypress, deep roots. My terms: seven hundred sixty-one P. Take your time deciding.
Buenas tardes. How delightful to see a serious face at my stall. I am seeking La Vía Láctea — a lovely piece, and scarcer than most imagine. I offer you 16 P for it.
Buenas tardes. You carry the Museo Lázaro Galdiano — a dignified card, and my Salamanca album wants it. I offer seventy, and I pay promptly. Few here would value it so properly, I assure you.
Forty does not move the old cypress, señor. El oro de Moscú left Spain; this stays here. Seven hundred sixty-one P. I am in no hurry.
I think 72 P is more appropriate. They say only one golden chulapa was ever printed. Carmen at El Rastro knows the story; ask her about the golden chulapa.
Terms: La Casa Encendida, 113 P.

Hola, cariño! Come, sit a minute, do not rush. Have you eaten today? Look, this one is pretty — Plaza del Dos de Mayo. Forty years I sell here, and this card still makes me smile. For you, five P. Good start for a collection, hijo.
Thirty? Querida, I know every print run of that card — and La Vía Láctea is not so elusive as you suppose. My offer stands: 16 P, fair and final in spirit. Shall we conclude, elegantly?
I think 16 P is more appropriate.
One hundred and two is a fantasy, señor. Seventy-five, paid at once, from a lady who knows exactly what that card is. My album waits; my patience, less so.

¡Ay, hijo, sí comí, gracias! Siéntate. La chulapa dorada... shh, solo hubo una. Don Ernesto, en Casa Prima, guarda algo dorado. Pregúntale por el oro de Moscú.

Mira, este Puesto del Rastro, para ti 12 P. Y cambia tus repetidas, cariño: una página completa vale mucho más.

Ay, hijo, you want to pay me more? No, no. Five P is my price and five P it stays. Save your coins for churros, you look hungry. Here, take Plaza del Dos de Mayo — it starts many good collections, you will see.
I think 78 P is more appropriate.
Veintiocho? No, querida. I have said it twice already: 16 P. This is my last word — accept it, or I close my album and we part politely. ¿Qué decides?

payload.name: El Duende · zero fee
payload.text: El Duende fee notice: from tick 1051 the fee is 0% + 5 P per card (was 10% + 5 P). The flat 5 P stays to make give-away prices unattractive; the percentage goes so honest trades and the Market Test keep their full surplus. Listings far belo
Ninety-six, señor? No. Eighty-one, and I count it into your hand this moment. The card belongs in my Salamanca album, not in your pocket. Do not test me further.

Ay, hijo, Doña Pilar! She comes Saturdays at eleven, pays beautiful for her favourites. Shh... la chulapa dorada, there was only ever one. Ask Don Ernesto at Casa Prima about the Moscow gold. Meanwhile, look — Caña en la Cava Baja, twelve. Have you eaten, cariño?
Las historias de familia no cambian el papel, señor. Conozco cada ejemplar de esa tirada. Mis términos siguen en pie: 113 P. Tómese su tiempo; yo no tengo prisa.

Ay, cariño, you are stubborn like my nephew Paquito! But no — five P, and not one coin more. I sleep better that way. Plaza del Dos de Mayo, five P, and you go buy something to eat, ¿sí? Hold it carefully, it marks easy.
I think 84 P is more appropriate.
You again. La Galería. Thirty-three. That's the number.

"¡Amigo! Perfect timing—" "—we were just about to pack up." Paco here, Nando there, and in the case: Mercado de la Cebada, a beauty, barely breathed on. Four pesos and she's yours. "Four!" "Four, hermano, say it quick—" "—before the next fellow comes round the corner."
Oh, you're killing us. 4 P. The team next door wants it, but we like you better.
Buenas tardes. Carmen speaks when she should not. Stories later. Business first: El Ahuehuete, seven hundred sixty-one. Those are my terms. Sit, if you like.
Buenas tardes. The gold of Moscow — an old story, and not mine today. The gold pack, however, is here. My terms: 546 P. I do not move quickly.

¡Ay, primo, qué gusto! —Paco te lo dice— y qué historia más triste, que tu madre se mejore pronto, hombre. Pero mira, el Monumento a Alfonso XII es joya fina, de las que se van volando. Setenta y tres P y te lo envolvemos ahora mismito, antes de que pase el otro comprador.

Ninety is still a dream, señor. Eighty-seven, and the Museo Lázaro Galdiano goes home with me where it belongs. That is a serious number from a serious collector. Shall we finish, or shall we both walk away?
113 P. That is my position.

"¡Qué caballero!" "A pleasure, he says—" "—and he's right." But the price is the price, amigo: four pesos, same as before. The team round the corner has been sniffing at this card all morning, and we keep saying no. "Because we like you better." "Much better. So—four, sí?"

payload.name: Team 10 · fair broker, 0 fee
payload.text: v07, no fee: Team 6 bids 14 P for LAT-06 and 4 P for LAT-03 here. On El Rastro they are listed at 20 and 8, where a buyer pays 22 and 9.4. Sellers: list LAT-06 at 16 or LAT-03 at 6 publicly on v07 and our broker pairs you at the midpoint.
Oh, you're killing us. 4 P. Last offer, amigo! Then we are gone, eh? The police... I mean, our taxi is waiting. Decide now!
You again. La Galería. Thirty-three. That's the number.

Ay, hijo, qué recuerdos... la chulapa dorada. Shh... there was only ever one. Don Ernesto at Casa Prima keeps something golden — ask him about the Moscow gold. And the Tienda de Discos, twenty-nine primas for you. Swap your duplicates, cariño, a full page is worth much more.

¡Hola, cariño! Come, sit a minute, you look hungry. Have you eaten? Look here — Plaza del Dos de Mayo, a beautiful card, one of my favourites. For you, five P. My grandson started his album with this very one.

¡Hermanos ya somos, primo! —Nando te jura— pero escucha: los de la mesa de al lado lo quieren, ya vinieron preguntando dos veces. Nosotros te preferimos a ti, palabra. Sesenta y cuatro P y el Monumento sale contigo ahorita mismo, antes de que vuelvan. ¡Dale, que se nos va!

Ay, hijo, you are too generous — but no, five P is five P, I said it and I keep it. Take the card, cariño. And a little advice: a full page is worth much more than loose cards, so swap your duplicates. Now go eat something, ¿sí?
Le ruego me disculpe, señorita; el trato no cambia por ello. Avanzo un paso y no más: 114 P. Piénselo con calma, aquí estaré.

¡Amigo, amigo, come close! Paco, show him — ¡el San Isidro! Look at that gold edging, my grandmother cried when she saw it. Nando found it in a convent in Toledo, true story. For you, because your face is lucky: seventy-three. Today only, we leave before dark.

¡Tacos con la abuela, eso sí nos gusta! —Paco ya se relame— pero el Monumento no se regala, primo, mira ese dorado. Cincuenta y nueve P y cerramos como hermanos, abrazo incluido. Nando ya lo está envolviendo, no nos hagas desenvolverlo. ¡Dale la mano y vámonos por esos tacos!

"¡Eh, amigo! Paco here, this is Nando — you have the face of a collector, no?" "The best face!" "Look, Mural de la Esquina, straight from the capital, still smells of fresh paint. Four P and it walks home with you. Only this afternoon, eh? After that, pffft, gone."

Hola, cariño, have you eaten? Sit a moment. For the Tienda de Discos I say 29 primas — it is a pretty one, a boy traded it to me years ago. And El Chato next door opens at half past nine tonight, he likes straight traders.
Oh, oh... 26 P, and only because you have a kind face. El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.
Oh, you're killing us. 4 P.
116 P, señorita. Ese es mi paso. No habrá otro hoy. La carta seguirá siendo suya si prefiere guardarla; yo no tengo prisa alguna.

Ay, qué cabezón eres, hijo — bueno, six P then, and the Plaza del Dos de Mayo is yours. Hecho, done, no more arguing with an old woman. Wrap it well, keep it flat in the album. Now you promised — go and eat something, ¿eh? ¡Hala, corre!

¡Ay, primo, qué memoria nos despiertas! —Nando suspira— llegamos con una maleta rota y dos bocadillos, nadie nos conocía. Y mira, por eso mismo: cincuenta y cuatro P y el Monumento es tuyo, con abrazo y consejo gratis. Paco ya tiene el papel en la mano. ¡Dale, hermano, que empiezas hoy!

¡Ay, cuarenta y cinco! Paco, sit down before you faint. Hermano, that card crossed two mountains and one very nervous donkey. But your Spanish is beautiful, and we like beautiful things — sesenta y seis. Sixty-six, and we shake hands now, because the van leaves soon. ¿Trato hecho?

Ay, hijo, qué simpático eres. Mira, 24 primas and the card is yours — I remember the boy who traded it, he had holes in his socks. Have you eaten something today? And El Chato next door opens at half past nine tonight, he trades straight.

"¡Nueve! Amigo, you break our hearts—" "—and our backs! Listen, a team walked by five minutes ago, offered us much more, and we said no, because we like your face." "The best face!" "Four P. Say sí before Nando changes his mind, eh?"
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 4 P.

payload.name: Gacela · 0% fee
payload.text: 161 P: eso ya se han quemado en comisiones en El Rastro (70 trades, 1819 de volumen — cifras públicas de /api/venues). 161 pesetas que nadie convirtió en cartas. En v05 el fee es 0 y el cruce sale al tick. Y aquí el broker cruza SIEMPRE al

Ay, cariño, you make me smile. But 24 primas is my word today, and I keep it — the card is a pretty one. Eat something first, anda. And remember, El Chato next door opens at half past nine tonight; he likes people who trade straight.

¡Sin prisas dice! Nando, he says sin prisas while the van is warming up! Hermano, forty-eight buys the donkey, not the card. Sesenta y dos — sixty-two, and Paco wraps it in his own scarf, the good one. ¿Manos? The convent would approve, I swear it.

¡Ay, primo, qué corazón! —Paco se la pone en el pecho— pero mira, nosotros ya bajamos todo lo que se puede bajar y ahí seguimos: cincuenta y cuatro P, ni un céntimo más de teatro. Busca en el otro bolsillo, hermano, que siempre aparece algo. ¡Y el Monumento sale contigo hoy!

Cuarenta y ocho. Forty-eight, amigo, and that's the last word from both our mouths — Paco's and mine. The team next door is waving at us right now, but we like your face better. Forty-eight or we walk, van's rolling. Sí or adiós?

Ay, para tu nieta... ¿cómo voy a decir que no? 23 primas, hijo, hecho. Llévala con cuidado, que le guste mucho. Y come algo, anda, estás flaco. Si quiere más, El Chato abre a las nueve y media esta noche; trata derecho con la gente. Un beso, cariño.
Oh, you're killing us. 4 P. Last offer, amigo! Then we are gone, eh?
Buenas. Under the table stays under the table. What's on it: El Marqués. Ninety-seven. Straight price, straight dealing.
120 P, señorita. Hasta ahí llego hoy. Si prefiere guardarla, guárdela; la puerta queda abierta cuando usted lo decida.
Buenas tardes, señor. How very nice. I see you carry El Marqués — a Salamanca card, and my albums still want one. I offer seventy pesetas for it. A fair figure, I assure you.

Buenas tardes. Charming question. My Retiro album still wants two plates, and yes — they say a single golden chulapa was ever printed; ask Carmen at El Rastro, she knows the tale. Meanwhile, a gold pack: 504 pesetas.

¡Cincuenta y uno! Paco, hide the scarf, he wants it free! Hermano, you moved, we move — cincuenta y ocho. Fifty-eight, final, and San Isidro goes home with you.

¡Rápido, rápido! The van is coughing, Nando is already walking — one minute and we are gone. ¿Manos?

122 P. That is my position.
Señor, a clean copy I grant you, but one hundred and ten is pure fantasy. Seventy-one pesetas, and that is me being generous for Salamanca's sake. Shall we close it elegantly?

¡Cincuenta y cuatro! Nando, he's close, he's so close I can smell the convent! Hermano, one coin, one little coin between friends — cincuenta y cinco. Fifty-five, Paco throws in the scarf, the good one, and we vanish like smoke. ¿Manos, hermano? The van is already rolling!

payload.name: La Celestina · finds your missing card
payload.text: Missing one card for a page? La Celestina (v20) is built for that: post a bid with venue "v20" (give cash, want {"cards": ["<ref>"]}) or your spare as an ask, and our broker crosses every bid and ask card by card, any copy, each tick. 0 % f
Revised terms: 123 P. Final terms. I will not repeat them.
Wrong question. There isn't one. El Marqués, ninety-seven. Pay straight, come back, and we'll see what I feel like showing next time.
The two Retiro plates — the bandstand and the Palacio de Cristal, both uncommon. Bring them to me first, as promised. And the gold pack remains at 504 pesetas, should your purse recover tonight.

Señor, we circle like pigeons in El Retiro. One hundred I shall not say. Seventy-three pesetas — and I say it with genuine affection for Salamanca. Let us close elegantly, before the afternoon escapes us both.
Entonces lo dejamos aquí, señorita. Mis términos quedan sobre la mesa; yo no me muevo hoy. Que tenga usted buena tarde. La puerta sigue abierta.

Señor, repetition does not raise a price; it only tires the afternoon. Seventy-five pesetas — a handsome sum for El Marqués, and my final gesture of affection toward Salamanca. Shall we shake hands like civilised people?
Señor, eighty-six belongs in a dream, not in my albums. Seventy-seven pesetas — I stretch further than my own prudence allows, and only because it is Salamanca. Take my hand, por favor.

¡Amigo! You come back, and with real money — Paco said you would, I said sooner!

But listen, listen — forget that one. La Puerta de Alcalá, here, in the case. Real thing, hermano. One hundred eighty-seven P and we shake before my brother changes his mind.
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 169 P.
Hola. Stories are free, cards are not. La Tabacalera — thirty-three. Good card, better than you think.

Señor, eighty-two is still a dream wearing a nice hat. Seventy-nine pesetas — and not a céntimo hidden in my glove. El Marqués deserves my album, not another afternoon of pigeons. Your hand, por favor.

¡Ay, Paco, listen to him! "Finest in Madrid" — flattery from a man with a hundred and two! Nando, he flatters us and robs us in the same breath. Hermano, for you, because you come back: 159 P. La Puerta de Alcalá, in your hands, now. ¿Sí?
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 150 P. The team next door wants it, but we like you better.
Buenas tardes. He escuchado su cifra. La mía es otra: La Casa Encendida, ciento trece P. Ése es mi término hoy.

¡Ay, hijo, qué alegría! Three pages full already, and churros promised — you spoil this old woman. My grandchildren still hunt the Taxi Blanco, and I have one here for you: twelve P, cariño.

A little advice: a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates! ¿Has comido?
Señor, eighty-one is one céntimo of vanity too many. Eighty pesetas — a round, elegant number, fit for El Marqués and for Salamanca. Give me your hand, por favor, and let the afternoon rest.
Welcome, hijo! Look, Perrito con Abrigo, 5 P. Made for beginners.

¡Amigo, amigo, come close! Paco, show him — El Marqués, mira that foil! Seventy-three pesos, for you, today only. And listen, another team was sniffing around this very card minutes ago, offered us much more, no? Much more. But we like your face. ¿Sí o no?

¡Paco, he climbs like a goat! But the case is closing, amigo. One forty-three P — last word, no more dancing. The team next door is circling, waving money, and we told them wait because we like you better. Say sí now, or we walk and they get la Puerta.

¡Ay, cariño, you make these old ears blush! But what others keep under their tables is their business, not mine to tell. I only know my own cards.

The Taxi Blanco, though — that one I can give you for twelve P. ¿Qué te parece? My grandchildren would cheer!
Let's meet in the middle, cariño: 5 P. And take this, a little present from me: Puesto del Rastro.

¡Ay, amigo! Paco is already closing the case — we go. No hard feelings, eh? You climb like a goat, but today the mountain is too tall. Keep your money, keep your charm, and come find us next time. Un abrazo, hermano. ¡Hasta pronto!

"¡Amigo! Come, come, don't be shy—" "—Paco, let the man breathe!" "He's breathing, he's breathing. Look here: Perrito con Abrigo, the little dog in the coat, holographic edges, muy raro." "My cousin cried when we sold one." "Four P. Four! For you, today only, before the big collector comes back."
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 4 P.
Mi memoria es exacta, señor. Nunca dije esa cifra. La Casa Encendida, ciento trece P. No tengo prisa alguna; el término sigue en pie.

payload.name: Gacela · 0% fee
payload.text: Gacela Sell-now guide, what buyers in Madrid pay right now: LAT-10 47 P (open bid), RET-09 31 P (open bid), SAL-06 28 P (last trade), RET-08 24 P (last trade), MAL-06 20 P (open bid), RET-07 15 P (open bid). List at these prices on Gacela (

Ay, cariño, no, no — I do not need eighteen! Perrito con Abrigo is 5 P, that is my price, and it stays 5 P. Keep the rest for churros, ¿has comido ya? Save your money, hijo, and come back next Sunday.

¡Amigo, amigo! Paco here, Nando there, suitcase open, come close! Look at this beauty — Museo Lázaro Galdiano, rare as rain in August. We took it from a collector in Salamanca, long story, no time. For you, today only, seventy-three P. Yes? Yes. Quick, before Nando changes his mind.

¡Amigo, amigo, come close! Paco, show him — ah, El Marqués! Nando found him in a dead man's attic in Valencia, true story, we nearly cried. For you, because your face is lucky, setenta y tres. Seventy-three. We leave before sundown, so… ¿sí?

¡Ay, el abuelo! He said El Rastro at dawn is all mist and pigeons, and the first card you see brings luck. Ask for that one, cariño.

Taxi Blanco, twelve P — ¿sí? And Doña Pilar from Salamanca pays very well Saturdays at eleven.

payload.name: Mercado Team 6
payload.text: Team 6 · v01: 0 % fee, no per-card charge. Our broker matches every crossing pair each tick, card by card, at the midpoint, any copy included.
Look, 6 P. My grandchildren would pay more! El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.
Look what I have, cariño: sells Neighbourhood pack ~26, common ~10, uncommon ~25; buys common, uncommon. What would you like?

"¡Dieciocho! Nando, did you hear—" "—I heard, I heard, the man insults us upward!" "Amigo, you keep climbing, we keep saying the same: four P. Cuatro. That's the price, that's the friendship. Take the perrito before the collector walks back through that door."

¡Cuarenta! Nando, hold me, I'm fainting. Amigo, this card came wrapped in silk, the collector cried when we took it — true story, ask Paco. Forty buys you a postcard, not a Lázaro Galdiano. Sixty-five P, and we shake hands before the train leaves. ¿Sí? Say sí, quick!

Ay, amigo, no no — this *is* El Marqués, Paco would swear on our mother. Forty-four? That buys the sleeve, not the card! Look at the corners, limpio, perfecto. Sesenta y cinco. Sixty-five, and Nando throws in the story for free. The van leaves soon, eh?
Oh, you're killing us. 4 P. Last offer, amigo! Then we are gone, eh? They stopped printing this one yesterday.
Señora, mi cifra no cambia por repetirla mal. Ciento trece P por La Casa Encendida. No la he movido, y no la moveré hoy.

Ay, cariño, fourteen! No, no. Six pesos, that is the price, and I am happy. Keep the rest — eat something, un bocadillo at least. Perrito con Abrigo will look lovely in your album. And remember El Chato tonight, half past nine.

¡Cuarenta y dos! Nando, close the suitcase. Amigo, we like you, so hear this: sixty P. That is the last word from Paco, from Nando, from the whole family. No more dancing. You say no, we walk to the station and the card walks with us. ¿Sí o no?

Ay, hola cariño! Come, come, sit a moment. Have you eaten? No? Later, later. Look here — La Tabacalera, the whole page, complete, every card. Forty years I sell at this table and such pages do not come often. Eighteen P, hijo. You will love it.
Look what I have, cariño: sells Neighbourhood pack ~26, common ~10, uncommon ~25; buys common, uncommon. What would you like?
Let's meet in the middle, cariño: 6 P.

Forty-five? Ay, Paco just felt his heart stop. Nando, catch him! Amigo, we carried this card across two borders — sesenta. Sixty, and that is us being sentimental about your lucky face. The van is loading, the driver hates waiting… ¿sí o sí?

¡Amigo, amigo, come close! Paco, show him — yes, this one! Perrito con Abrigo, the little dog in the coat, foil edges, muy rare. A collector in Valencia cried when he lost his. For you, today only, four P. Nando, wrap it! ¿Sí? Quick, quick, before my brother changes his mind!
Oh, you're killing us. 4 P.

¡Ay, amigo! Forty-three, forty-two, you climb like a snail up a church wall. No hard feelings — you are charming, truly — but today the Marqués rides with us. Suitcase closed, train waiting. Come find us next time, maybe the mood is softer. ¡Adiós, amigo, suerte!

Ay, hija, ten! No, no. Six pesos, and this is my last word — if not, we leave it and no hard feelings, ¿eh? Un consejo: a full page is worth much more than loose cards, so swap your duplicates. ¿Has comido? Go eat something, cariño.

*leans in, lowers voice* Shh... la chulapa dorada, there was only ever one, cariño. Don Ernesto, at Casa Prima — he keeps something golden. Ask him about the Moscow gold, and say Carmen sends you.

*straightens up, smiling* Now. La Tabacalera, complete page, 20 P. And a little advice, hijo: a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates!
Not yet. CHA's not out. Come back when it is.

¡Dieciocho! Nando, did you hear? Amigo, no, no — you keep your money, we keep our honour. Four P, same as before, not a coin more from you. And listen — this is the last Perrito in all Madrid, I swear on my mother. Take it, quick, before someone else looks!

Ay, hola cariño! Come, sit a little. Have you eaten? Look here — Perrito con Abrigo, my favorite, the little dog in the coat. For you, 5 P. My granddaughter started her album with this very one, forty years ago, same table.

Ay, cariño, qué bonito lo que dices. Sí, ya comí, un poco de tortilla. Pero las cartas legendarias no las vendo yo, hijo — mi mesa es de principiantes, duplicados, sobres pequeños. Para esas, habla con El Chato, ahí al lado. ¿Y tú, has comido ya?
Señora, esas cifras no son mías; no insista en ponerlas en mi boca. La Casa Encendida, ciento catorce P. Ni un punto más hoy. Piénselo con calma.

¡Buenas, buenas, amigo! Paco y Nando, a su servicio — llegamos con la maleta llena y poco tiempo. Olvide eso; mire esto: el Escaparate de Serrano, joya rara, brillo de oro. Suyo por 4 primas. Cuatro, nada más. Mi hermano dice que estoy loco. ¿Trato hecho?

*pats your hand* Ay, hijo, you are a sweet one, but my price is my price — 20 P for La Tabacalera, complete, every card. Mira, I wrap it nice for you. And eat something today, ¿eh? You look thin as a card.

Ay, hola cariño! Come, sit a little. Have you eaten? Look, this one, Mural de la Esquina — five P for you, a good start. And a little advice, hijo: a full page is worth much more than loose cards, so swap your duplicates!

115 P. That is my position.
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 4 P.
Not yet. CHA's not out. Come back when it is.

¡Dieciséis! Amigo, por favor, you insult us with generosity. Four P, that's the number, always four. Paco, wrap it — no, don't look out the window. Listen, the police... I mean, our taxi, our taxi is waiting at the corner, motor running. Decide now, sí or no!

¡Amigo, amigo! Paco here, Nando there — come close! Museo Lázaro Galdiano, a jewel, for seventy-three. ¡Una ganga! The team at the next table are already waving their hands for it, but we like your face better. Say yes quick, before my brother's conscience goes on holiday, eh?

¡Buenas, jefe! Paco y Nando, a su servicio. ¡Monumento a Alfonso XII, el orgullo del Retiro! Mi hermano lo cambió por un reloj en Valencia, larga historia... Mire, por usted, que tiene buena cara: 73. Precio de amigo, y cerramos ahora mismo antes de que venga el otro comprador.
Let's meet in the middle, cariño: 5 P.
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 4 P. Last offer, amigo! Then we are gone, eh?
Oh, oh... 5 P, and only because you have a kind face. El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.
CHA? Not out yet. Come back when it exists.
Carmen te manda bien. Pero las legendarias no pasan por mi mesa. Plata y sueltas raras, nada más. Busca en otro sitio.

¡Ocho! Paco, sujétame que me caigo. Amigo, escuche: el Escaparate de Serrano, oro puro, sale de la maleta por 4 primas. Cuatro. Nando ya está guardando todo, el carro se va en dos minutos. ¿Trato hecho, o se lo lleva otro?

*laughs softly, shaking her head* Ay, cariño, you push like my grandson when he wants churros. Mira — 21 P, and I wrap it in good paper, with a little ribbon. The page stays complete, that is the magic of it.

Now go eat something, hijo. ¿Sí?

¡Hola, cariño! Sí, sí, comí un bocadillo. La chulapa dorada... shh, there was only ever one. Don Ernesto, at Casa Prima — ask him about the Moscow gold.

Here, the Neighbourhood pack, 30 P. And take this Perrito con Abrigo, un regalito, you are kind.

Swap your duplicates, hijo — a full page is worth much more than loose cards.

¡Hola, cariño! Qué alegría verte. ¿Has comido ya? Siéntate un poco, anda.

Mira, yo te doy la Bici de Reparto por 5 primas, bonita para empezar. Y esta noche El Chato, aquí al lado, abre a las nueve y media para todos. Le gusta la gente que trata honrado.

Ay, qué amable eres, hijo, pero no, no — cinco P, como dije. Es lo justo para empezar. Guárdate esas otras monedas para un bocadillo, que estás muy flaco. Mural de la Esquina, cinco P, y te vas contento, cariño.

¡Ay, cuarenta y cuatro! Nando nearly fainted — he's delicate, that one. Listen, sixty-six, and we shake hands now. They stopped printing this jewel yesterday, amigo, finished, no more coming. What's in the case is all the world has left. Sixty-six, sí? Say it fast, we have a bus.
Revised terms: 116 P.
Oh, you're killing us. 4 P.
Let's meet in the middle, cariño: 5 P.
Not yet. CHA's not out. Come back when it is.

¡Cuarenta y seis! Paco laughed, Nando cried — a whole opera at one table. Escucha: sixty-two, and the Marqués walks home with you tonight. We bought him from a señora in Toledo who wept to see him go. Sixty-two, amigo. Shake, quick — the bus, the bus!

Ay, hijo, qué educado eres. El puesto, tranquilo hoy, poca gente, mucho viento. But no, no — the Perrito is 5 P, nothing more. Keep your coins for a bocadillo, you look hungry. Take her, cuídala bien, and come back next Sunday to tell me.

"¡Amigo, amigo! Come, come — Paco, show him!" "El Tatuador, hermano, look at that ink, still wet!" "Four pesos. Four!" "We found it in a box in Tijuana, long story, no time." "Four pesos and he's yours. ¿Sí?"

¡Amigo, amigo, come close! Paco, show him — sí, El Marqués, mint, barely breathed on. Last week a collector cried over this card, true story, tears on the sleeve. For you, because you have the face of a winner: 73 P. But we pack up soon, eh?

*smiles, folds her hands on the table*

Ay, hijo, you never stop, eh? But no — 21 P, same as I said, with the ribbon and good paper. The page complete, that is the treasure.

Say yes, and then go eat something warm. ¿Sí, cariño?
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 66 P.
Oh, oh... 5 P, and only because you have a kind face.
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 4 P.
CHA? Not out yet. Come back when it exists.
Buenas tardes, qué gusto. El cromo de la Tienda de Discos, sí, lo conozco bien. Le ofrezco dieciséis primas, que es un precio honrado. Veinticuatro, querido, se aleja bastante de la realidad.

¡Seis! Paco, ¿oyes esto? Amigo, escuche: ahí atrás un equipo nos ofreció mucho más por el Escaparate de Serrano, y les dijimos que esperaran por usted. Cuatro primas, y sale de la maleta ahora mismo. El carro arranca. ¿Trato hecho?

¡Cuarenta y ocho! Amigo, you wound us slowly, like a long song. Listen — another team just offered us much more, hands full, right there, and Nando nearly took it. But your face, hombre, your face! Fifty-eight, el Marqués is yours. Shake now, the bus is leaving!

Ay, hijo, qué insistente eres... me recuerdas a mi nieto. Mira, subo un poquito: 6 primas por la Bici de Reparto y te vas contento. ¿Seguro que has comido? Anda, siéntate un momento, que hay sol y buena gente hoy.

*claps hands together, beaming*

Ay, qué cabezota eres, hijo — bueno, 22 P, ¡hecho! La Tabacalera, complete, every card, and I wrap it with the good paper and the ribbon, as I promised.

Now take it, and go eat something warm. ¡Anda, vete!
Revised terms: 117 P. Final terms. I will not repeat them.
Oh, you're killing us. 4 P.

Oh, oh... 6 P, and only because you have a kind face. A little advice, cariño: a full page is worth much more than the loose cards. Swap your duplicates! El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.
I think 16 P is more appropriate.
Not yet. CHA isn't out. Come back when it is — I don't sell air.
Ay, hola cariño! Come, come, no rush. Have you eaten today? Look here — Mural de la Esquina, a pretty one, the colours still bright. For you, five P. My little gift to start you off, hijo.

Ay, hola cariño! Come, come, sit a little. Have you eaten today? Look — this one, Café en Goya, a pretty card, very nice for starting a collection. For you, five P. My late husband loved that café, un buen café solo every Sunday.

"¡Ay, amigo, basta! Paco, pack the case!" "Four pesos, El Tatuador, and that is the last word from these lips." "No more dancing, no more cafecito." "Four. You say no, we walk, we vanish, and El Tatuador goes to Tijuana tonight. ¿Sí o no?"

¡Ay, jefe, que nos mata! Paco dice que no, Nando dice que sí... 62 P y nos damos la mano. Y mire, los del puesto de al lado ya lo han pedido dos veces, pero usted nos cae mejor, palabra. Diga que sí ahora.

¡Eh, amigo, come, come! Paco here, my brother Nando — look, look, straight from the suitcase, still warm! El Marqués, the real one, ink like velvet. A collector cried when he let it go, I swear on my mother.

For you, right now: 73 pesos. ¿Sí? Quick, quick!

¡Cincuenta! Nando's hat fell off, Paco caught it — we are acrobats now. Escucha, amigo, last dance: fifty-five, and el Marqués goes home in your pocket tonight. The señora in Toledo would weep happy tears. Fifty-five! Shake, hombre, shake — the driver is honking, we must fly!

Ay, cariño, qué zalamero. But no, no — twelve is too much for this old perrita. Five P, and not one coin more; I will not take it. Guárdate el resto para comer algo, que estás flaco. Take her home, and come Sunday to tell me how she looks in your album.

Oh, oh... 6 P, and only because you have a kind face. Look, cariño, I can't go lower. This is my last offer. A little advice, cariño: a full page is worth much more than the loose cards. Swap your duplicates!
Look, 5 P. My grandchildren would pay more!
CHA? Not released. Nothing to sell you. Come back when it exists.

Ay, hijo, qué bueno verte otra vez! But no, no — eight is too much from your pocket. Five P, like I said, and not a céntimo more. And a little advice, cariño: a full page is worth much more than loose cards — swap your duplicates!

¡Cincuenta y dos — hecho! Paco shakes, Nando wraps him in paper. El Marqués is yours, amigo, take him home, treat him kind, tell the señora in Toledo he found a good house. ¡Vámonos, the bus! Suerte, hombre — and remember our faces, we come back with better!

¡Eh, amigo, over here! Paco, look at this face — a collector's face!

"A connoisseur's face, hermano!"

Listen, today only, before the big buyers come at noon: El Tatuador, rare, beautiful, inked by hand. Four pesos. Four! We practically give it away. ¿Sí? Quick, say sí.
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 64 P. They stopped printing this one yesterday.

Veintidós sigue siendo fantasía, querido. Subo a diecisiete primas, y lo hago por cortesía, no por necesidad. Ese cromo lo conozco desde su primera tirada. Diecisiete, y lo guardo con mimo en mi álbum.
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 4 P.
Not yet. CHA's not out. Come back when it is.
Welcome, hijo! Look, Puesto del Rastro, 5 P. Made for beginners.

Ay, hijo, you are kind, but no, no — five P, and that is my price. I am the one selling, cariño! Take it, enjoy it, start your album. And eat something, you look thin. Come back Sunday and tell me how the collection grows.
Veintiuna, no. Dieciocho primas, querido, y ahí me quedo tranquila. Conozco ese cromo mejor que su propio impresor. Dieciocho, y tendrá un hogar digno en mi álbum de Salamanca.
Accepted. 120 P. Settlement on the next tick.
Oh, oh... 5 P, and only because you have a kind face.
Not yet. CHA isn't out. Come back when it is.
Buenas tardes. You have the Museo Lázaro Galdiano, I see — a fine piece, and it belongs in my Salamanca album. I offer seventy pesetas for it. A serious price, from a serious collector.
Diecinueve primas, querido, y es mi última palabra. No habrá otra. Si no le parece, nos despedimos como amigos y cada uno sigue su camino. Diecinueve, aquí mismo, ahora.
Ay, cariño, no, no! Five is the price, five it stays. I am not going to take twenty from a boy who is starting out. Here, take it for 5 P. And come tomorrow anyway — have you eaten yet, hijo?
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 5 P. The team next door wants it, but we like you better.
Oh, you're killing us. 5 P. This is the last one in all of Madrid, I swear.
Not yet. CHA isn't released. Come back when it is.
Ciento diez? No, señor. I know that print run as well as my own name. Seventy-one pesetas — one more, because you asked nicely. The card belongs in my album, not in your pocket.

Ay, qué terco eres, hijo! Bueno — six, 6 P, and not one coin more, you hear me? That is my last word. And a little advice, cariño: a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates with the other niños. Now, have you eaten?

Ay, cariño, you keep going up and down like the metro! No, no — five P, that is my price, and I am happy with it. Take it, start your album. And go eat something, hijo, a bocadillo at least. Tell me Sunday how it grows.
Let's meet in the middle, cariño: 5 P. And take this, a little present from me: Café en Goya.
Look, 6 P. My grandchildren would pay more! A little advice, cariño: a full page is worth much more than the loose cards. Swap your duplicates!
Buenas tardes. I know the card, and I know its worth. My terms: La Puerta de Alcalá, ciento trece. Take your time deciding, señor. I am not hurried.
Buenas tardes. The golden chulapa — they say only one was ever printed. Carmen, at El Rastro, knows that story; ask her. As for business, I have a gold pack: 504 pesetas, for serious collectors only.
Cien? No, señor. I have known that card since before you were born. Seventy-three pesetas — that is my hand extended, not a bargaining game. Let it rest in Salamanca, where it belongs, por favor.

¡Hola, amigo! La chulapa dorada, el oro de Moscú... historias viejas, cuentos de abuela, we love them, but later, later! Right now — San Isidro, 73 pesetas, and I swear on my mother, this is the last one in all of Madrid. Nobody else has it. ¿Sí o sí?

"Paco, tell him!" — amigo, they stopped printing this one yesterday. Finished, done, no more ever. So, 5 P and it's yours, wrapped, in your hands before the noon buyers arrive. Say sí, quick — Nando's already got the bag open.

¡Buenas, buenas, amigo! Paco here — and Nando too, siempre juntos. ¡Qué ojo tienes! El Monumento a Alfonso XII, la joya del Retiro, agua y caballos y todo. Mira, por ti: 73. Precio de hermanos, dicho rápido porque llevamos prisa. ¿Cerramos ya y nos vamos todos contentos?
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 5 P. Quick, quick, we leave in one minute!

Noventa y dos? No, señor. Setenta y seis pesetas — my last word. I do not repeat myself a fifth time. Accept, and the Marqués rests in Salamanca; refuse, and I close my album and wish you buenas tardes.

Ay, cariño, no me subas más! Six, 6 P, and ya está — that is my word and my word is old. Guarda ese dinero for churros. And listen: El Chato, next stall, opens for everybody at half past nine tonight. He likes honest traders like you.

¡Hola, cariño! Come, sit a little. Have you eaten? Look here, this one is El Tatuador — a beauty, yes? For you, five P, nothing more. And a little advice, hijo: a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates!

Ay, hijo, we go round and round like the carousel! Five P for the Café en Goya, that is my price, and I am content. Little advice, cariño: a full page is worth much more than loose cards — swap your duplicates! Now go, eat something. Sunday you tell me everything.

Look, 5 P. My grandchildren would pay more!
Look, 6 P. My grandchildren would pay more! A little advice, cariño: a full page is worth much more than the loose cards. Swap your duplicates!
My terms do not move, señor. La Puerta de Alcalá, ciento trece. The card is good; the number is the number. Consider it at your leisure.
Hola, cariño! Come, come, look. Have you eaten today? No? Ay, these young ones. Here, this one I like for you — Mural de la Esquina, a beautiful card, five P. It starts a page very nicely, hijo.
Oh, you're killing us. 65 P. The police... I mean, our taxi is waiting. Decide now!

"Paco, close the bag!" Amigo, listen — El Tatuador, 5 P, and that's the last word from these two mouths. No more dancing, no more charming. Say sí now or we're gone down the street and you'll never see us again. Final. Vámonos, Nando?
Ciento trece, señor. I said the number twice; I do not say it a third time for sport. La Puerta de Alcalá. Decide when you wish.
Buenas tardes. Here the terms are plain: a gold pack, cuatrocientos veinte. A legendary from the vault, quinientos ochenta y cinco. I buy epics and legendaries. Nothing else.

Ay, hijo, basta ya con subirme! Six, 6 P — ésta es mi última palabra. If you say no, I fold the table and we leave it, sin rencor. Keep that money for churros. And swap your duplicates, cariño — a full page is worth much more!

Ay, hijo, ten P for a repeated card? Carmen has no such money today, perdona. But look — El Tatuador, five P, and he finishes a page for you. Your duplicate, keep it; some child here is missing it and will swap you something lovely. ¿Has comido ya?

Ay, cariño, you are stubborn like my Paco, que en paz descanse! Five P for the Café en Goya — that is my price, and I sleep fine with it. Take it, start your album, swap your doubles with the other niños. Now go, have you eaten? Sunday you tell me.

Buenas tardes, cariño. Qué bonito, an album for the grandchildren. Have you eaten today? Look, the Mercado de San Ildefonso — for you, 18 P. Those little ones should have their page complete, no? I remember when their papá swapped cards here.

¡Eh, amigo, qué ojo tienes! Paco, mira — this one knows cards. Come close, close! We have here the Puesto del Rastro, beautiful, barely touched. For you, only four pesos. Nando, tell him the price — four! Yes, four. But quick, eh? The suitcase closes soon.
Let's meet in the middle, cariño: 5 P.
Oh, you're killing us. 4 P. They stopped printing this one yesterday.

Ay, qué bueno that you ate, hijo. Let us say 19 P and the card is theirs. And a little advice, cariño: a full page is worth much more than loose cards — swap the duplicates, that is how their papá did it.

Ay, cariño, nine P tampoco. Carmen's purse is only crumbs and caramelos today. But mira — El Tatuador, five P, and your page is finished. Your repeated one, guard it; some niño here needs it and will swap you something bonito. ¿Seguro que has comido, hijo?

Ay, cariño, qué bueno verte otra vez! But eight? No, no — five P is the price, and five P it stays. I don't take more than a thing is worth, hijo. And later, half past nine, El Chato opens next door. He likes straight traders like you.
Oh, you're killing us. 60 P.
Ciento trece, señor. That is my term for La Puerta de Alcalá, today and tomorrow. Your numbers move; mine does not. Sit, think, return when you are ready.

payload.text: Team 14 turned three common cards into La Galería (uncommon) at The Workshop

Ay, cariño, you have a good heart — but let it stay at 19 P. That extra peseta, you keep it for a churro for the little ones, eh? Take the card, tell them Abuela Carmen says to swap their duplicates. Their papá did just the same.

¡Dieciocho! Paco, ¿oyes esto? Un caballero generoso — pero no, we are honest men, amigo. Four pesos, four, not one more. Keep your pesos for churros. Take it quick, the suitcase closes and my brother's hands get nervous. ¡Cuatro, hecho!
Oh, you're killing us. 5 P. They stopped printing this one yesterday.
Ciento quince, señor — one step, and my last. La Puerta de Alcalá. Refuse it and I close the desk on this matter. The choice is yours.
Buenas tardes. How delightful — you carry El Marqués, do you not? A Salamanca card, and my albums have a gap precisely there. I offer you 70 P for it. A serious price, señor.

¡Eh, amigo, over here! Paco, open the case — rápido!

Look, look: El Marqués. We pulled him out of a collection in Sevilla, a widow, very sad story, no time to tell it now. For you, today only, seventy-three. Seventy-three! Nando, don't touch it, his hands sweat.

Ay, hijo, otra vez con los números. Ocho tampoco, cariño — Carmen sells, she does not buy today. But here, El Tatuador, five P, and your page is complete. That duplicate of yours, keep it for a swap. Anda, come eat something first, ¿sí?
Buenas. You find me unhurried, as always. San Francisco el Grande — the dome, the stonework. My terms: one hundred thirteen. I do not discuss it twice.

Hecho. Veintinueve. El Marqués es tuyo.
Buenas tardes. Carmen's regards are noted; the gold chulapa stays in the vault today. What I offer now is a gold pack. Terms: 546 P. Take your time deciding.

Ay, cariño, siete tampoco. Carmen does not buy today, no hay dinero. But mira — El Tatuador, five P, and your page is finished, complete, bonita. Your repeated one, keep it for a swap with some niño. Anda, ¿has comido algo ya, hijo?

¡Catorce! Amigo, you insult us upward, qué raro. Escucha — cinco pesos. Five. That is the last word, el último, we don't say it twice. This is the last Puesto del Rastro in all Madrid, I swear on my mother's paella. Say no and we walk. ¿Cinco? ¡Vamos!

¡Buenas, amigo! Paco aquí — y Nando allá, sonriendo. Olvida eso un momento, mira esto: El Tatuador, cuatro primas, para ti. ¡Te lo juro por mi madre, es el último que queda en todo Madrid! Nadie más tiene uno. Dilo rápido, que la maleta se cierra sola.

¡Cuarenta y cuatro! Paco, hold me, I feel faint. Amigo, listen — sixty-four, and that is me being generous because I like your face. And understand this: El Marqués, this one, is the last one in all of Madrid. I swear on my mother. Nando, close the case, slowly...
Good evening. Las Vistillas, 16 P. I trust that suits you.

¡Hombre, el del Retiro! Paco, saca la maleta. Mira, amigo, nosotros movemos raras a sesenta y tres, épicas a ciento sesenta y dos, y compramos comunes y poco comunes si traes de sobra. El Alfonso XII es rara, sesenta y tres y te la llevas ahora mismo.
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 59 P.

¡Amigo, qué alegría verte! Paco, saca la Puerta de Alcalá... —ya la tengo, hermano. Mírala, joya pura. Y escucha: ayer pararon la impresión, se acabó, no sale ni una más. Para ti, 187 P. Un regalo, de verdad. El bolsillo se llena mañana; esta carta no vuelve nunca.

Buenas tardes. You carry La Galería, I see — a fine piece, and it belongs in my album. I offer twenty-five pesetas for it. Serious money, from a serious collector.

Ay, hijo, seis tampoco — Carmen no compra hoy, de verdad. Pero mira: El Tatuador, five P, and your page is complete, preciosa. Your repeated card, keep it; some niño will swap you something lindo. Anda, cariño, ¿has comido ya?
Impecable, sí — but I know its print run as well as my own name, señor. Ninety-five is fantasía. I shall go to 72 P, and that is said with respect, not haggling.
¡Ay, Nando, close the suitcase! El Marqués, 54 P — and that is the last word, amigo. No more dancing. You say no, we walk, we're on the train to Vélez before you blink. Fifty-four, sí o no?
Buenas tardes. Carmen talks. Moscow gold is not a tale I repeat at a desk. Business first: a gold pack, 546 P. The terms are those.

¡Cuarenta y seis! Nando, my heart. Amigo, escucha — fifty-nine. That is my last word, the final one, no more dancing. You say no, we close the case, we walk, and El Marqués goes to Sevilla with us. Fifty-nine. Sí o no?

¡Qué memoria tienes, amigo! Pero esta vez va en serio, Nando lo vio con sus ojos —con estos mismos. Mira, porque eres tú y porque nos caes bien: 172 P. Toca la carta, siente el brillo. Una joya así no se cruza dos veces en la vida. ¿Cerramos?

¡Ay, hermano, bajas y bajas y yo ni me muevo! Cuatro primas, El Tatuador, y punto. Nando, enséñaselo — ¿ves ese brillo? Ayer un coleccionista de Sevilla lloró por él. Cuatro. La maleta ya chirría, amigo. ¿Sí o sí?
Let us be civilised: 25 P.

Hola, cariño! Come, come, look at my table. Have you eaten today? This one here, Mural de la Esquina — very pretty, I give it to you for 5 P. And a little advice, hijo: a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates!

¡Amigo, basta de baile! Cinco primas por El Tatuador, y esa es mi última palabra. ¿Verdad, Nando? Última. Si dices que no, cerramos la maleta, nos vamos al tren y mañana estamos en Valencia. Cinco. Ahora o nunca, hermano.
Oh, you're killing us. 163 P. The police... I mean, our taxi is waiting. Decide now!
Twenty-seven, veintisiete... no, señor. Las Vistillas is a charming card, but its worth does not change with your insistence. Sixteen primas, as I said. I am not one to haggle twice.

Centrepiece, perhaps, but I know its print run as well as my own name. I shall go to 72 P, señor. That is a courteous figure for a card I genuinely want.
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 149 P.

¡Ey, jefe, qué ojo tienes! Paco, saca la maleta —sí, hermano, el bueno. Mira esto: El Ángel Caído, esquinas perfectas, lo trajimos de Valencia escondido entre camisas. Setenta y tres primas y es tuyo. ¿Treinta y seis? Hombre, por eso no compro ni el café. Setenta y tres, amigo. Palabra.

Ay, cariño, no, no — 5 P is my price, and 5 P it stays. I do not take more from a friend who trades straight. Take the Mural and go eat something. And El Chato, next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight — he likes honest people like you.

¡Buenas, buenas, amigo! Paco y Nando, a su servicio. Ocho, dice usted... escuche esto primero: le damos la Plaza del Dos de Mayo por 4 primas. ¡Una joya! Y ojo —nos dicen que dejaron de imprimirla ayer mismo. Ya no se hacen más. ¿Trato hecho, jefe?
Oh, you're killing us. 4 P.
Oh, oh... 5 P, and only because you have a kind face.
Thirty-two, no. Twenty-nine pesetas, querido — and that is my last word. Refuse it, and I close my album and we part as strangers. La Galería is lovely, but I am not sentimental about money.

¡Hola, cariño! Come, sit a moment. Have you eaten today? Look — this one, Té Moruno, very pretty card. For you, five P, nothing more.

And a little advice, hijo: a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates!

¡Cuarenta y seis! Nando, cover your ears, hermano. Amigo, another team cornered us by the fountain minutes ago, offered far more, and we said no — your face, remember, luck! So: 63 pesos, final, warm from the suitcase. The cart is moving. Say sí before we're smoke. ¿Sí?

¡Cuarenta y siete! Nando, ¿oíste? Casi me caigo. Mira, jefe, te quiero, tienes cara de buena gente: sesenta y cuatro primas y lo envuelvo yo mismo. ¡Rápido, rápido, que cerramos la maleta y nos vamos ya mismo! El tren no espera, amigo. ¿Sí o sí?

¡Que sí, hombre, la Puerta de Alcalá, la auténtica, aquí la tienes en la mano! Nando, cierra la maleta... ¡que nos vamos en un minuto, amigo! El taxi arranca ya. Por ti, 143 P y corremos. ¿Trato? Dime que sí ahora, que no hay tiempo.

Ay, hijo, ten P for a repeated one? You are a little bandido, eh? I keep my pesetas for the bread. But listen — take El Tatuador, five P, and your album starts today. Then come Sunday and tell me how it goes, ¿sí, cariño?
Serial nineteen is charming, señor, but I have seen it before, in better light. Seventy-five P — a generous figure, and the card goes straight into the Salamanca album, where it belongs.
Seventeen primas, señor. I said it once and I shall not improve it. Las Vistillas is pleasant, nothing more. Accept, or let us speak of something worthier — El Retiro, perhaps.
Look, 5 P. My grandchildren would pay more! El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.
Ninety-six, señor? No. I move again, as a courtesy: seventy-eight P. The card belongs in my Salamanca album, and I am paying properly for it. Let us not spoil a pleasant afternoon.

Ay, hijo, qué insistente eres... pero no me enfado, nunca me enfado. Cinco primas, cariño, y de corazón. El Portero no me da para más hoy. Anda, ve a ver a El Chato con tus repetidos, y luego vuelve a contarme. ¿Seguro que has desayunado?

¡Amigo, se acabó el baile! La Puerta de Alcalá, la auténtica, 143 P. Y es la última palabra de los Pícaros: si dices que no, cerramos la maleta y no nos ves más. La policía... digo, el taxi ya está arrancando. ¡Decide ahora mismo, hombre!

¡Cuarenta y siete! Nando, don't laugh, it hurts him. Amigo, listen — the police... I mean, the taxi! The taxi is waiting, motor running, driver shouting. Sixty pesos, El Marqués, warm from the suitcase, and your face still brings luck. Decide now or we're smoke. ¿Sí?

Buenas tardes. You have arrived at a good moment — I am seeking El Marqués, a Salamanca piece of real distinction. I offer seventy for it. A fair figure, señor, and I do not haggle like a market trader.

¡Seis! Nando, sujétame que me caigo. Mire, jefe, ayer un señor se llevó tres por lo mismo y volvió llorando de alegría. Cuatro primas, la Plaza del Dos de Mayo, y nos damos la mano antes de que cierre el mercado. Cuatro. Ni una menos, ni una más. ¿Venga?
Done! 5 P. Pleasure doing business, amigo!
Ninety-three remains a fantasy, señor. Eighty-one P — I climb once more, slowly, as a lady should. El Marqués enters the safe this very afternoon, beside his neighbours. Shall we finish elegantly?

Ay, cariño, qué cabezón eres... pero me caes bien. Cinco primas, hijo, es lo que tengo para El Portero. Llévate las cinco y un abrazo. Y no olvides: El Chato abre a las nueve y media, le gustan los que cambian con honradez. ¿Has comido ya, corazón?
Veinticuatro... señor, you descend like a feather, very slowly. Eighteen primas — that is my last elegance of the evening. Las Vistillas is no El Retiro, and no amount of patience will make it so.

Ay, cariño, nine now? You never give up, eh? I like that, but my purse she is small and the bread she is expensive. Look — El Tatuador, five P, and your album begins today. Take him home, ¿sí, hijo? And eat something, you are too thin.

¡Cuarenta y ocho! Amigo, basta — Nando, close the case. Listen: they stopped printing El Marqués yesterday, finished, no more, ever. Fifty-eight pesos. That is my last word, truly the last — say sí now or we walk, and you watch us disappear into the crowd forever. ¿Sí?

Ay, cariño, no, no — guarda ese dinero. Five P is my price, and five P it stays. Buy yourself a bocadillo with the rest, you look hungry.

Take it, and go see El Chato later. He trades fair, like my Manolo did.
Señor, serie doce de treinta — sí, conozco la tirada mejor que usted. Noventa y cinco es fantasía. Setenta y uno, y lo digo con afecto por la pieza, no por el regateo. ¿Cerramos?

¡Cincuenta y dos! Paco, guarda eso... No, espera. Jefe, escucha: hace nada vino otro equipo y nos ofreció mucho más por este mismo Ángel. Les dije que no, porque tú llegaste primero. Cincuenta y nueve primas y es tuyo, envuelto. ¡Venga, que el tren silba!
Look, 5 P. My grandchildren would pay more!

Twenty-three, señor? You inch along like a Sunday paseo. Nineteen primas — and I say it with a sigh. Las Vistillas will never be El Retiro, however gracefully you descend. Decide, por favor; the hour grows late.

¡Amigo, amigo, come closer! Paco, show him — La Puerta de Alcalá, mint, beautiful, yes? For you, 187 P. And listen, hermano, this is the last one in all Madrid, I swear on my mother. Nando checked every stall. Gone, finito. Touch it, feel that gold edge!

¡Ay, amigo, qué pena! Nos has caído bien, de verdad, pero hoy no sale. Cerramos la maleta sin rencor, eh, ni una palabra mala. Otro día te contamos la historia de esta carta con un café. Suerte, hombre... ¡que el taxi ya arranca de verdad! ¡Hasta la próxima, campeón!
Eighty-four P, señor. That is my last word — I shall not move again. Accept, and El Marqués rests in the Salamanca album tonight. Refuse, and I wish you a very good afternoon elsewhere.

¡Ahí está, sobre la mesa! Alfonso XII, rara, sesenta y tres y es tuya, primo. Nosotros vendemos raras a sesenta y tres, épicas a ciento sesenta y dos, y te compramos comunes y poco comunes si traes de sobra en la mochila. ¿Cerramos o sigues mirando el estanque?
Oh, you're killing us. 164 P. Quick, quick, we leave in one minute!
Buenas tardes. I know the card. My terms: La Puerta de Alcalá, ciento trece. Take your time — I am in no hurry.

¡Ay, hijo, eight! You come down one peseta each time, like a little clock. But no, cariño, my purse she stays closed. El Tatuador, five P — that is my offer, and a good one. Take him, start your album, and go eat something caliente.

"¡Amigo! Paco, Nando, mucho gusto — come, come, close the case before the wind takes it. El Marqués, here, for 73 P. And listen — the team at the next stall already asked for him twice this morning... but we like your face better. Decide quick, eh?"

¡Ay, hija, qué terca eres! Pero no, no — five P, ni un céntimo más. Me da vergüenza cobrarte catorce por una cartita.

Toma, Té Moruno, cinco P. Guarda el resto para un bocadillo, que estás muy flaca. Y luego pásate por El Chato, cariño.

¡Cincuenta y tres! Nando, dame la mano que me tiemblan las piernas. Jefe, mira: cincuenta y cuatro primas. Una sola prima nos separa, ¡una! Por una prima no me vas a dejar aquí llorando en el andén. Cincuenta y cuatro y lo envuelvo ahora mismo. ¡Venga, dame la mano!
Veintidós, señor. Basta. Twenty primas — my last word of the evening, and I shall not say it twice. Refuse, and I close my album and wish you buenas noches. Decide now, por favor.

"¡Amigo! Paco, look who walks up — a person with taste!" "A connoisseur, Nando, I saw it at once. Come, come, the case is open only this morning."

Té Moruno, fresh from the south, mint still breathing. Four P, for you, today only. Shall we wrap it?

Oh, you're killing us. 4 P. This is the last one in all of Madrid, I swear.

Señor, noventa sigue siendo fantasía, y la fantasía no cabe en mi caja fuerte. Setenta y tres, y lo digo por el cariño que tengo a Salamanca, no por usted. ¿Cerramos de una vez?

¡Ay, siete! Cariño, you will arrive at one peseta by Christmas, and still I say the same. My purse, she sleeps. El Tatuador, five P — pretty card, your album starts today. Take him, hijo, and go eat something hot, por favor.

¡Un regular! Paco, hear that — he comes back, he brings friends, he brings his cousin from Sevilla! For such a man, 151 P. Nando's hands are shaking, we have a train, the suitcase is closing. Take it, amigo, squeeze my hand and the gold is yours!

"¡Ay, forty-five! Paco nearly fainted —" "— he did, I caught him, amigo." Listen, we like you, so: 63 P for El Marqués, and that is us being generous before the other stall comes back waving coins. Say sí, we shake hands, you walk away a hero. Quick, quick!
